Full Commentary:
Thanks for joining our commentary this afternoon. Until next time, goodbye.
Everton end their campaign with a whimper and Ronald Koeman has a lot of decisions to make over the summer over the future of his key players. Romelu Lukaku and Ross Barkley could be on the move and it's vital that they are sufficiently replaced should they leave. There's plenty to build on though for the Dutchman following a successful first term.
Goals from Hector Bellerin, Alexis Sanchez and Aaron Ramsey secured the win, with Romelu Lukaku netting a consolation goal for the visitors from the spot. It's a good end to the season for the Gunners, who will now be looking to take momentum into their clash with Chelsea next week in the FA Cup fina.
Arsene Wenger's played well despite being reduced to 10 men in the 15th minute when Laurent Koscielny was dismissed. The Frenchman will now miss the FA Cup final next week, while Gabriel Paulista also suffered a serious injury.
Arsenal did their job this afternoon, but in the end it's not enough to secure Champions League football as wins for Manchester City and Liverpool elsewhere see them settle for fifth place and the Europa League.

(90’) SAVE! Welbeck is played through on goal and only has Robles to beat, but the keeper spreads himself well enough to deny the forward.

Ozil picks him out on the edge of the box and he is afforded space to turn and shoot, finding the top corner with his strike. Robles has been good today, but he could not do anything about that. ---

(81’) Arsenal are just putting men behind the ball now as Everton are controling proceedings at the moment.

Everton have been very wasteful in front of goal, with Ronald Koeman visibly frustrated on the sideline. The Dutchman faces an important teamtalk at the break if his side are going to avoid ending their term with a whimper.
It's all for nothing for Arsene Wenger's men currently as Liverpool lead Middlesbrough, while Manchester City are well ahead at the break against Watford. The Gunners need an equaliser from Boro in the second half to send them into the Champions League next term.
A weird first half of football comes to an end with Arsenal holding a 2-0 lead over Everton, despite being reduced to 10 men. Hector Bellerin opened the scoring in the early stages, but the Gunners were dealt a blow when Laurent Koscielny was given a straight red card for a loose challenge on Enner Valencia. However, lapse defending from the visitors allowed Alexis Sanchez to double the home side's lead with a simple strike.

(38’) SCRAMBLE! Mirallas drives the ball at goal from the right inside channel, but Cech makes the save. Barkley keeps the attack alive, only to scuff his effort at goal. Valencia then has a go from the edge and his strike almost trickles towards Lukaku, but the Arsenal keeper gathers at the feet of the Belgian.
(37’) Bellerin probes down the right flank and sends a teasing cross to the back post where Welbeck waits. However, Holgate is there to head the ball behind for a corner.
(36’) Gabriel has to win his challenge with Mirallas to stop the Belgian racing away down the flank. Unlike Koscielny he times his tackle to perfection and clears the ball away.
(34’) Holgate swings a dangerous cross into the box from the right flank, but Cech is alert to the danger and comes off his line to gather ahead of the Belgian.
(32’) CLOSE! Sanchez hammers the ball towards goal from the free-kick and it almost catches Robles out at his near post. The keeper makes the stop, but palms the ball out into the box. It strikes Welbeck on the leg and bounces safely out of play for a goal-kick.
(31’) Welbeck does well down the left flank and he draws the foul from Holgate to win the Gunners a free-kick in a threatening position.
(29’) BLOCK! Barkley threatens in the final third and tries to go himself to carve out room for a strike, but his effort is blocked by Holding.
--- 27’ Assist Welbeck notches his second assist with a simple pass back to Sanchez to score. ---
--- 27’ Goal! GOALLLL!!!! SANCHEZ FINDS THE NET! A bizarre goal for the Gunners as they double their lead. Sanchez strikes the ball from the edge of the box, but it hits Welbeck. The Everton defence stop expecting either a handball or an offside decision against the forward, but he and the Chilean play on. He passes back to an unmarked Sanchez to fire the ball into the bottom corner. ---
--- 26’ Substitution Barkley replaces Davies for the visitors in an attacking substitute. ---
(26’) Valencia latches on to a ball over the top of the Arsenal defence and he has Lukaku in support in the box, but he fires his low cross straight at Cech.
(24’) OVER! From the resulting corner Arsenal take a short one and Sanchez curls his delivery to the back post for Gabriel. The defender rises well, but can only send his headed effort over the bar.
(23’) BLOCK! Sanchez takes the free-kick and he hammers his effort towards goal, but the wall does its job and the ball spins out for a corner.
(22’) Sanchez goes down on the edge of the box as he gets clipped just when he fires at goal by Gueye.  Replays show that the Everton man got nothing but the ball in that challenge. Not a good sign that the referee has been influenced by the home crowd.
(20’) Lukaku collects a ball down the left flank and he beats the challenge of Holding to fire a low ball across the face of goal. However, Davies fails to gamble on the cross and the opening is spurned for the visitors.
--- 19’ Yellow card Williams goes into the book for a foul on Sanchez. The Welshman will have to be very careful now. ---
(18’) OFFSIDE! Ramsey loses possession in the middle of the park and Mirallas tees up Lukaku on the edge. The Belgian powers an effort at goal, but he blazes his strike over the bar. Lukaku will be relieved to see the offside flag go up anyway.
(15’) That's huge for the Gunners in the context of the Champions League race. Wenger's men now have to play the final 75 minutes with 10 men.
--- 14’ Red card! OFF! Koscielny is off as he lunges in on Valencia and the referee does not hesitate to dismiss the Arsenal skipper. The Everton man was raiding away down the right flank and the defender slid in hard and missed the ball. He wiped Valencia completely out and deserved to receive the red card. ---
(13’) UPDATE: Romelu Lukaku's hopes of catching Kane at the top of the goalscoring charts are already taking a hit. The England striker has scored twice already today against Hull.
(11’) Sanchez gets the better of Schneiderlin in the middle of the park and advances to the edge of the box, but before he can shoot enough blue shirts get back to crowd him out.

STAT ATTACK! Everton beat the Gunners earlier this season and Koeman's side are aiming to do the double over Arsenal for the first time since the 1985/86 campaign.
STAT ATTACK! Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 20 Premier League home matches against Everton, winning 16 of the contests.
Everton have made one change from their win over Watford, with Barkley being dropped to the bench and Enner Valencia replacing him in the side. Given the speculation over Barkley's future - the decision from Ronald Koeman may be political.
Arsenal have made three changes from their win over Sunderland during the week. Gabriel Paulista, Laurent Koscielny and Danny Welbeck come into the fold this afternoon, with Kieran Gibbs and Shkodran Mustafi dropping out of their squad, while Olivier Giroud starts from the bench.

The team news has been announced and we'll start with the home side.
Everton have been inconsistent of late, but did bounce back from successive defeats by beating Watford last week thanks to a strike from Ross Barkley. His future is far from certain and he could be aiming to leave his hometown club on a high note.
The first order of business for Arsenal is to beat Everton, although that will be far from an easy task. The Toffees have been impressive this term and Romelu Lukaku will be determined to get himself back on top in the race for the golden boot after Harry Kane's exploits on Thursday.
The race can also get a bit weird and wonderful and result in a play-off between Arsenal and Liverpool/City. If the Reds lose to Boro at home 2-0 and Arsenal play out a 1-1 draw with Everton this afternoon - or if City lose 4-0 to Watford and the Gunners beat the Toffees 1-0. However, unlikely those are the options still available.
Should Liverpool fail to beat Middlesbrough at Anfield that will open up the path for the Gunners to sneak ahead of Jurgen Klopp's side into the top four. Another avenue could open if Manchester City lose to Watford at Vicarage Road, although it will also require a swing of five goals to benefit the Gunners.
Arsene Wenger's men have been in excellent form of late, winning their last four matches on the spin. They've beaten Manchester United, Southampton, Stoke and Sunderland on their surge, but need to overcome Everton to have any chance of securing a top-four place for the 20th year on the spin.
Arsenal have put the pressure well and truly on Liverpool and Manchester City in the race for the top four. The Gunners know a fifth win on the bounce is necessary to dislodge the Reds or Pep Guardiola's men.
Good afternoon and welcome to the live commentary of the final day Premier League clash between Arsenal and Everton at the Emirates Stadium.

It’s all over at Old Trafford and United will go into the Europa League final on the back of a win thanks to goals from debutant Josh Harrop and the outstanding Paul Pogba, who was then replaced before half-time ahead of the final. Palace were far from their best and played like a side who had very little to play for, but they will be satisfied to be playing Premier league football next season after being in serious danger of relegation throughout the campaign. That’s all from us for today and for this Premier League season, thanks for joining us and we hope you can join us again soon.
Full-time: Manchester United 2-0 Crystal Palace
(90’) United are in cruise control now just knocking the ball around midway through the Palace half, and the visitors can’t get a touch of the ball.
(90’) We’re into the first of three minutes of added time at the end of this game.
(90’) Gomes gets a couple of touches just inside the Palace half as he links up with Mitchell on the left-hand side, but the ball eventually runs out of play for a Palace throw.
--- 88’ Substitution A third and final change for United now and Rooney is the man to be replaced, going off to a standing ovation in what could be his final United appearance at Old Trafford, with 16-year-old Angel Gomes coming on in his place. ---
(85’) Jones goes on a wonderful run towards the Palace penalty area, skipping past several Palace players on his way, but he chooses not to shoot and instead tries to pick out Rooney at the back post only for his pass to sail out of play for a goal kick.
(83’) We have another break in play now as Ward is down receiving treatment with what looks to be a nasty blow to his nose, and now the United fans are finding their voice.
(81’) United are in no rush to do anything now and Palace don’t look to be too bothered about it either, although their fans are still making plenty of noise in the away end.
(79’) Palace are certainly looking a little more threatening now but they are forced to put the ball out of play as Zaha is down close to the left-hand side. Sam Allardyce won’t be too happy if he has to go off as he’s certainly been on the end of some tough tackles in this game.
--- 79’ Substitution Zaha is going to be forced off bringing an end to what has been a pretty impressive season for the winger. Fraizer Campbell comes on in his place. ---
(77’) Save!! Milivojevic curls the free-kick over the wall and towards the corner but Pereira leaps across his goal to catch the ball, although the dive was perhaps a little more spectacular than it needed to be.
(76’) Palace have just lifted the intensity of their play in the last few minutes and they win another free-kick, 25 yards out in a central area following a foul on Sako by Tuanzebe.
--- 74’ Yellow card Zaha is the victim of another foul, this time by Carrick who pulls him back midway through the United half and is subsequently shown a yellow card by referee Taylor. ---
(73’) CLOSE!! Palace win a free-kick to the right-hand side of the penalty box following yet another foul on Zaha by Tuanzebe, and Sako’s whipped in delivery skims off the head of Carrick at the near post and flies narrowly over his own goal.
(71’) Wonderful play from Mitchell as he skips past Zaha and Ward to get to the byline and into a position from where he can cross, although the delivery is a poor one and goes straight into the arms of Hennessey.
(69’) Puncheon and Benteke exchange passes 30 yards out from goal and the former has space ahead of him to either shoot or roll the ball back to Benteke who’s peeled away into a good position, but he does neither and ends up giving the ball straight back to United.
--- 67’ Substitution Another change for Palace now as Sully Kaikai comes on for van Aanholt. ---
(66’) Martial this time wins a free-kick just inside the Palace half after a good run and pass by Harrop, who’s looked extremely comfortable on the ball so far in this game.
(64’) Martial picks up the ball in space on the left-hand side and drives into the corner of the Palace penalty area at pace, but he opts against going for goal himself and instead plays the ball behind Harrop, rather summing up his confidence levels at the moment.
(63’) The tempo of this game has really dropped in the last few minutes with neither side seeming to have much desire to throw too many bodies forward.
--- 61’ Substitution Palace are making their first change now with McArthur going off to be replaced by Bakary Sako. ---
(59’) United are in absolutely no rush to go forward now and Carrick has taken over from Pogba in controlling play from midfield, albeit from a deeper position.
(57’) Sam Allardyce looks a rather bemused figure as he makes his way back up into the dugouts from his technical area, although his side do look as though they have a goal in them, particularly if they can get the ball into Zaha and Benteke.
(55’) OFF THE POST!! United were all set to make a change as Bailly hobbled off but it looks as though he’s going to continue, but they switch off momentarily at the back as Zaha stands up a cross towards Benteke who climbs well and turns a powerful header onto the foot of the post from eight yards out.
(53’) The Palace players eventually put the ball out of play following a loud chorus of boos from the home fans as Bailly goes down having landed heavily following a battle in the air with Benteke. The centre-back did go down just before the break but this does look more serious.
(51’) The Palace winger is back on the field and is going to try and run the injury off as Puncheon draws another foul close to the left-hand touchline just inside the United half.
(49’) Zaha is still down receiving treatment following that foul and it does look as though he may have landed awkwardly.
--- 48’ Yellow card Zaha knocks the ball past Scott McTominay and looks to break away into the United half, but the young midfielder just clips his heels and is shown a yellow card for the foul. ---
(46’) Kick-off! Referee Anthony Taylor blows his whistle and Palace get the second half underway.
Sam Allardyce may well have to change the system in order for his side to get back into this game in the second half, as United have defended in numbers and looked well organised at the back, although Zaha did cause them a few problems in the latter stages of the first half. Jose Mourinho meanwhile will be asking for more of the same from his side.
United go into the break in complete control of this match thanks to a goal from debutant Harrop and one from the influential Pogba, who was then replaced before the break along with Lingard.
Half-time: Manchester United 2-0 Crystal Palace
--- 45’ +2 Substitution This is quite extraordinary from Mourinho now as he makes a second change before the break with Anthony Martial coming on to replace Lingard. ---
--- 45’ Substitution A first change for United now, and one that has come completely out of the blue too as Pogba is replaced by Michael Carrick. The Frenchman doesn’t look to be injured so that change is presumably with the Europa League final in Jose Mourinho’s mind. ---
(44’) Both Zaha and Bailly appear to have taken a knock in that challenge but both players look as though they’re going to be able to continue.
(42’) Zaha’s influence in this game is starting to grow and he wins yet another free-kick following a foul by Fosu-Mensah, although he does throw himself to the ground in a rather theatrical manner. Zaha then gets in behind the United defence down the left-hand side of the penalty box, but his second touch is too heavy and allows Bailly to slide in with an important tackle to take the ball away from the winger.
(40’) The United fans are in full voice now and understandably so as their side look relatively comfortable as things stand.
(38’) Milivojevic goes for goal but his effort is deflected out off the wall for a corner, which is confidently claimed by Joel Pereira.
(37’) Zaha wins another free-kick, this time just outside the United penalty area having been brought to ground by Fosu-Mensah, and Milivojevic once again stands over it.
(35’) Zaha has been pretty quiet in this game so far but he wins a free-kick midway through the United half having been pulled back by Axel Tuanzebe. Milivojevic takes the free-kick and very nearly picks out Tomkins who is free at the back post, but the ball is fractionally too heavy for the centre-back to get on the end of.
(33’) Close!! Harrop goes close to getting his second of the game as he once again cuts inside onto is right foot and curls a dipping effort narrowly over the bar from the left-hand corner of the penalty box.
(32’) Palace are really struggling to get out of their own half just at the minute and United are knocking the ball around with ease, with both Fosu-Mensah and Mitchell playing extremely high up the pitch in the full-back positions.
(30’) Pogba is running things for United at the minute and he plays in Lingard down the left-hand side of the penalty area and Lingard has Rooney to aim for in the middle, but his low cross is a tame one and is easily diverted out for a corner, which comes to nothing.
(28’) Lingard picks out Mitchell on the left-hand side and the left-back has space to cross, but he just dwells on the ball for too long allowing Ward to make a tackle. Ward will not be too pleased with Wilfried Zaha there though as the winger made no attempt to track the full-back.
(26’) CHANCE!! A chance for Palace to pull one back now as Puncheon swings in a wonderful inswinging corner from the right-hand side and an unmarked Benteke attacks it six yards out from goal, but he somehow manages to miss the ball completely and it rolls out of play for a goal kick on the far side.
(24’) United look quite happy to allow Palace to have the ball at the minute and they’re getting plenty of numbers behind the ball, meaning Palace are going to have to be extremely patient.
(22’) Benteke holds the ball up well inside the United penalty area and looks to play van Aanholt in on goal down the left-hand side, but the pass is just too heavy for van Aanholt who is forced wide, allowing Fosu-Mensah to recover and regain possession for United.
(21’) United look extremely comfortable in possession now and Palace are struggling to get into forward areas as they were doing in the opening minutes.
--- 19’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAALLLLL!!!! Pogba makes it two!! United break forward quickly at pace as Lingard brings the ball up towards the Palace penalty area from inside his own half before sliding a pass into the area, and Joel Ward fails to deal with it allowing Pogba to slide the ball under Hennessey and into the back of the net. ---
(17’) Palace had settled into a very compact shape with five men in midfield before that goal, but they may well have to be a little bit more adventurous now.
--- 15’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLLLL!!!! Harrop gives United the lead!! Paul Pogba picks out the youngster with an outstanding pass down the left-hand side and he cuts inside Martin Kelly onto his right foot before firing a powerful effort into the far corner from 15 yards out. ---
--- 15’ Assist Pogba's pass down the line was weighted perfectly for Harrop to get on the end of, but he still had an awful lot to do. ---
(12’) CLOSE!!! Demetri Mitchell plays a lovely long ball over the top of the Palace defence and Rooney controls it well before attempting an ambitious left-footed lob over the onrushing Wayne Hennessey, but he puts fractionally too much on the shot and lands it on the roof of the net.
(10’) It’s been a relatively quiet start to the game from both sides so far, but Palace will probably be the happier of the two sides having looked the more threatening going forward.
(8’) Christian Benteke receives the ball into his feet with his back to goal just inside the United penalty area and looks to shoot on the turn, but Phil Jones sticks with him well and makes a good block on the striker’s well-struck, low shot.
(6’) Josh Harrop gets his first chance to run with the ball at his feet and he’s brought to ground by Luka Milivojevic close to halfway. The debutant showed a good turn of speed there to get away from the Palace midfielder who is perhaps lucky to have escaped a booking.
(4’) Jesse Lingard looks to have started out on the right-hand side of the front three but the Englishman is already showing his willingness to come in field and support of Rooney through the middle.
(2’) Chance! An early chance for Palace as Patrick van Aanholt gets in behind the United defence inside the left-hand edge of the penalty box after a lovely one-two with Jason Puncheon, but Timothy Fosu-Mensah recovers well to make a superb sliding challenge to deny him.
(1’) Kick-off! Wayne Rooney gets the game underway for United.
The players are making their way out onto the pitch, kick-off is not far away now.
Zlatan Ibrahimovic scored a late winner to secure a 2-1 victory when the two sides met at Selhurst Park earlier in the season, after James McArthur had cancelled out Paul Pogba’s opener.
Sam Allardyce makes just two changes from the side that beat Hull, with James McArthur and Patrick van Aanholt replacing Yohan Cabaye and Andros Townsend.
Jose Mourinho chose to rest a number of key players for the midweek clash with Southampton, and the United manager has opted to do the same again today with Demetri Mitchell, Josh Harrop and Timothy Fosu-Mensah all getting a run out along with goalkeeper Joel Pereira, while Phil Jones and Wayne Rooney are the only survivors from the draw with Southampton.

Despite being in danger of relegation just a few days ago, Palace could finish as high as eleventh in the table with a win, should other results go in their favour, such is the tight nature of the bottom half of the Premier League.
Palace meanwhile secured Premier League survival with a 4-0 win over Hull City last time out, a result that moved them up to 13th in the table as well as condemning their opponents to relegation.
They will certainly want to take some confidence into that game with a win today though, especially as they are without a win in their last four games in all competitions.
Manchester United currently sit sixth in the Premier League table, seven points adrift of Liverpool in fourth, meaning winning the Europa League final on Wednesday is their only route into next season’s Champions League.

Sam Allardyce has done it again, guiding another club to safety as he did with Sunderland last term. It was closer than he would have liked, but Palace managed to get over the line in the end.
The Tigers seemed doomed from the off as Andrea Ranocchia's mistake handed Wilfried Zaha the opening goal inside the third minute. Christian Benteke's headed effort in the 34th minute put the game beyond the visitors, while further strikes from Luka Milivojevic and Patrick van Aanholt compounded the agony.
Hull's relegation is confirmed as they are hammered this afternoon by Crystal Palace, who retain their Premier League status. The Eagles' victory also allows Swansea to remain the top flight next season.
HULL CITY ARE RELEGATED FROM THE PREMIER LEAGUE!

Palace have been clinical enough and solid at the back, which will delight Sam Allardyce. He knows that his side are just 45 minutes away from securing their place in the Premier League for another season.
The Tigers will also feel hard done by as two missed handball decisions from Martin Atkinson cost them. First he missed a handball by Zaha in the build-up to Christian Benteke's header to double Crystal Palace's lead, while no more than a minute later the referee missed Jason Puncheon's block with his outstretched arm in the box.
Hull have 45 minutes to find two or more goals to save themselves from relegation after a disastrous first half for Marco Silva's men. The game could not have started any worse for the visitors when Andrea Ranocchia missed his kick and allowed Wilfried Zaha a free run to slot his effort past Eldin Jakupovic.

Sam Allardyce has never been relegated as a manager from the Premier League, and that record will be put to the test this afternoon - with a draw or a victory guaranteeing their safety. A loss would send the Eagles to Old Trafford next week in danger of dropping down to the second tier.
Palace must have also believed they were safe from the perils of relegation following their impressive run of form that saw them defeat Chelsea, Arsenal and Liverpool. However, three defeats on the bounce, including one damaging home loss against Burnley have put them in trouble.
After looking like they had done enough to beat the drop since Silva's arrival, the club's defeat at the hands of Sunderland last week has put their top-flight status in jeopardy. The Tigers have an inferior goal difference to both of their relegation rivals - as a result, a victory must be their priority this afternoon to avoid further heartbreak on the final day.
The formula for Hull is simple today. If they are beaten by the Eagles they will be joining Sunderland and Middlesbrough in the Championship next season in an immediate return to the second tier. If they win or draw Marco Silva's men will take the battle for the drop into the final day of the season.

FULL-TIME! Leicester coast to a comfortable 3-0 win over Watford at the King Power, courtesy of goals from Ndidi, Mahrez and Albrighton. The visitors were never really in this game after the second goal, with Shakespeare's men proving yet again that there is plenty of life in last season's title winners. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
--- 90’ +3 Assist Vardy unselfishly squares a pass to his teammate, who was left in acres of space. ---
--- 90’ +3 Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! ALBRIGHTON MAKES IT 3-0! The English winger is picked out brilliantly on the right flank by Vardy, after Watford's back four got sucked right in. A low finish from Albrighton kisses off the inside of the near post and nestles in the back of the net. ---
(90’) Okaka tries to spin in the penalty area and force Schmeichel into a near-post save, but the Italian striker is watched closely and physically by Benalouane and can't get a shot off. Great defending from the Leicester centre-back once again.
(90’) There are three minutes of stoppage time at the King Power.
(88’) Good defending from Prodl! Gray drives down the left and drills a low cross in towards the six-yard box, but the Austrian centre-back slides in to make a brilliant interception! Moments later, Mariappa is forced to make a good sliding block to deny a dangerous delivery from Vardy.
(86’) Amrabat tees up Zuniga for a shot on the edge of the Leicester penalty area, but the Colombian substitute fires an awful effort high and wide of the target. The home fans cheer. Sums up Watford's day at the office.
(85’) Pereira curls a lovely cross towards the back post from the right-hand side, with the ball knocked down by Okaka. Deeney gets onto it and lashes a close-range effort over the crossbar from about six yards out! It looked easier to hit the target. His blushes are spared by an offside flag!
--- 83’ Substitution Niang is replaced by Pereira for the last five minutes or so, with the youngster getting a chance to show what he can do. ---
(82’) We're into the last 10 minutes at the King Power, with Leicester having this victory sewn up with ease. The second goal from Mahrez killed both the competitivity and the atmosphere here, with Mazzarri's side crashing to another loss with just a whimper. Okaka and Deeney have been anonymous up top since the latter's introduction.
(80’) Watford are continuing to try and penetrate this Leicester defence, but much of their effort is being spent watching Amrabat run down dead ends on the right flank. The Morocco international has been incredibly frustrating this afternoon.
--- 78’ Substitution Mahrez is given a standing ovation on his way off the field, with Gray getting the last 10 minutes to make an impression from the bench. ---
(77’) Amrabat picks out Cleverley on the edge of the penalty area, with the English midfielder doing well to force Schmeichel to palm the ball over the crossbar for a corner! The resulting corner is met by Prodl, but his header flies straight into the goalkeeper's waiting gloves.
(76’) Leicester are easily keeping Watford at bay, with the away side taking far too long on the ball. The Foxes are able to stay compact and organised, with their opponents never playing with the tempo required to stretch their two banks of four. Schmeichel is kept awake by a long-range effort from Niang, that he parries to safety well, before the Danish goalkeeper smothers a tame shot from Cleverley.
(74’) Albrighton gets inside Zuniga easily and makes his way into the penalty area, but then loses his footing and slips over. The Englishman and Mahrez have been complete livewires down the flanks in this second half. Their confidence is sky high! Watford are fading badly in this game.
--- 72’ Substitution Kabasele is replaced by a more orthodox full-back in Zuniga. That change should have probably happened at the break. ---
(72’) Over the top from Fuchs! The Austrian left-back lines up a speculative free kick from around 25 yards out, with the ball shaving the top of the crossbar on its way behind. Gomes had to get up well to make sure that he had his angles covered.
(71’) Niang tries to check infield and cause some problems on the edge of the Leicester box, but the ex-Milan wide man takes an awful touch. Albrighton is onto it in a flash and curls a lovely ball down the line for Mahrez to chase. The Algeria international drives into the box and cuts a pass to the edge of it for his compatriot, but Slimani hammers a finish over the bar! Moments later, another Mahrez ball in from the right flashes dangerously across the face of goal without a touch.
(69’) Slimani leads a break for the home side, before feeding Vardy down the left channel. The England international cuts inside very easily, with Mariappa being beaten all ends up by a simple jink infield. His eventual shot, however, is poor. Gomes makes a simple save! That should have been 3-0.
--- 67’ Substitution Deeney is introduced for the away side, with Capoue jogging off. That should see Watford go with their captain and Okaka up front now. ---
--- 67’ Substitution Drinkwater is the next man to take his leave for the Foxes, with Andy King getting a run out in central midfield. ---
(66’) Vardy finds Mahrez out on the right-hand side yet again, but this time Doucoure covers back well to rob the Leicester goalscorer of possession deep inside his own penalty area. It must be said, Mahrez really does look on form and in the mood today.
(65’) Albrighton scampers down the left-hand side and tries to angle a cross in from the byline, but his attempted delivery swerves dangerously into the side netting. Gomes was worried for a second there! Leicester look really threatening when they get the ball forward at pace.
(64’) Mahrez whips a delivery in from the right-hand side, but Mariappa hooks a clearance away, as Leicester continue to keep causing problems out wide. Watford are struggling to control this contest, with their lacklustre and slow possession usually ending in a Foxes' counter attack.
--- 63’ Substitution Slimani is introduced for the home side, with Okazaki taking his leave. He has worked incredibly hard yet again this afternoon. ---
(61’) Okazaki and Vardy link up on the break, with the latter then bending a cross to Mahrez at the back post. The Algerian tries to cushion a square pass towards the penalty spot for Okazaki, but Watford clear their lines. Some classic Leicester counter-attacking football there.
(60’) Only half an hour remains for Leicester to see out, with that second goal appearing to kill the contest off. Watford try to respond immediately, with Amrabat looking to drive straight down the right wing, but Fuchs uses his strength brilliantly to ease his opponent off the ball.
--- 58’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! MAHREZ MAKES IT TWO! The Algerian winger cuts in again from the right-hand side and gets into the penalty area, before slotting a beautiful finish in between Gomes' legs from a tight angle by the byline. Watford's defending is embarrassing, however, with Mariappa gifting the ball away to the hosts' danger man. ---
(56’) Albrighton bends in a corner from the right-hand side, but Okazaki is beaten in the air, before a long-range effort from outside the box is blocked ahead of Gomes. Little mistakes are threatening to settle this game, with both teams guilty of being irresponsible in possession.
(54’) Watford are trying to get their foot on the ball and to turn the tide in the midfield battle, but neither side is able to really exert any control on this game. Chances are popping up at both ends, and neither defence looks entirely convincing this afternoon.
(52’) Over the top from Okaka! The Watford striker is picked out at the back post by Amrabat, but some pressure from Benalouane forces him to head over the bar. That was a big chance for the away side to equalise, but the Italian striker appeared a little hesitant to put his head in where it hurt.
(50’) Good stop from Gomes! Vardy is fed into a pocket of space by Okazaki, in behind the visiting defence. The England international races onto the ball and fires a low shot towards the bottom-right corner, but the Watford goalkeeper gets down smartly to make a solid save!
(48’) Okaka and Amrabat link up on the edge of the Leicester penalty area, but the Moroccan winger spends so much time on the ball that the hosts can get back into shape. Kabasele swings in a cross from the right, but Schmeichel claims easily. Watford appear to have shifted to a back four now.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Leicester have a narrow and perhaps undeserved lead, but Watford are left with it all to do if they want to try and turn this one around. Deeney might be the man to inspire a comeback from the bench.
HALF-TIME! Leicester go into the break with a 1-0 lead, given to them by some neat poacher's work from Ndidi. Watford have had their fair share of chances, with Mazzarri sure to feel hard done by so far. Quality in the final third has been at a premium from both sides, but this has been a very even contest indeed.
(45’) Over the top from Okaka! Janmaat bends in a cross from the left-hand side, which isn't cleared well by Drinkwater. Mariappa gets onto the loose ball and finds his striker in the box, but an inventive flicked attempt at a finish loops behind and to safety. Moments later, Amrabat dips an excellent delivery in, but nobody can get on the end of it in the six-yard box!
(44’) Gomes is able to claim a cross from the left-hand side with relative ease, as Leicester continue to just focus on their wingers this afternoon. Outside of Albrighton and Mahrez causing problems, they've offered very little. One-dimensional stuff from the Foxes, but they have the lead they would have wanted.
(42’) OFF THE BAR! Mahrez dances infield from the right-hand side and beats Janmaat easily, before trying his luck with a right-footed shot. The ball clips off Cleverley and loops over Gomes, but kisses the top of the crossbar on its way behind for a corner. The resulting set piece is whipped in towards Ndidi, but the Foxes' goalscorer can't head goalwards.
(40’) Out of nowhere, Leicester have the lead! Shakespeare's men have only really threatened through set pieces this afternoon, though they have dreamed up some interesting little short routines to cause Watford problems. Mazzarri will be furious, as his side had really stepped up over the last 10 minutes or so.
--- 38’ Goal! GOOOOOOAL! NDIDI MAKES IT 1-0! Prodl gives away a free kick right on the very edge of his own penalty area. Mahrez tries his luck with his left foot, but the Watford wall jumps well and deflects the ball behind for a corner. The resulting set piece is taken short again, before Drinkwater helps it into the back post. Capoue takes a terrible touch and Ndidi reacts first to slam home a cracking finish! ---
(36’) Watford's back three are having a very easy day at the office so far, with crosses in from either flank being gobbled up greedily by three players that can handle themselves in the air. Okazaki and Vardy definitely aren't armed with the best attributes to fare well in these aerial battles. Cleverley forces Schmeichel into a very smart save, after the English midfielder was found in acres of space on the edge of the area by a deflection off Ndidi. Well struck and well stopped!
(35’) Drinkwater is picked out in plenty of space on the left-hand side, but the England international strangely opts to shoot from a very tight angle rather than look for Mahrez at the back post. That was an odd decision! The referee has a little chat with Cleverley, with the ex-Manchester United midfielder involved in a fair few fouls early on.
(33’) Cleverley tries to lift a lofted ball over Simpson for Janmaat to chase, but the Leicester right-back deals with the danger easily. Leicester respond with their own attempt to get down the left, but another Albrighton cross fails to find a blue shirt. Vardy and Okazaki have been anonymous.
(31’) Janmaat is invited down the left-hand side and hangs a cross into the box, but Capoue can only send a very tame header straight down Schmeichel's throat. Mazzarri's wide men continue to offer a real threat against Leicester, as their four-man midfield is being considerably stretched.
(29’) Good stop by Schmeichel! The Danish goalkeeper manages to get down low to his left-hand side to block a powerful shot from Okaka, after the Watford striker swivelled very smartly to escape the clutches of Huth in the penalty area.
(27’) Benalouane is forced to stick a foot in to direct a dangerous cut-back away from Okaka, as Watford continue to show a little bit of promise when getting their wing-backs involved in advanced areas of the field. Amrabat has been bright and a threat for the Hornets. Mazzarri will be pleased with how this game has gone so far, with his system doing its job.
(26’) Capoue feeds a long pass down the right-hand side for Niang to chase, with the Milan loanee latching onto the ball smartly. He gets to the byline with ease, before blasting an awful attempting cross into the stands! The home fans cheer sarcastically - that was pretty dreadful. Sums up the lack of quality in the final third so far, really.
(24’) Amrabat bends another delivery in from the right wing, but a volleyed effort from Okaka is blocked smartly by Huth. The Foxes head up the other end to try and force the issue themselves, with Fuchs bending in a brilliant cross from the left. Vardy is the target, but Kabasele gets his head on the ball instead, forcing his own goalkeeper into a fingertip save!
(23’) Leicester are having plenty of opportunities to take advantage of mishit clearances and balls upfield from the away side, but they are yet to put their opponents to the sword for doing so. Watford threaten down the right, as Amrabat faces up Fuchs and drills in a cross from just outside the penalty area, but Huth makes a good block at his near post.
(21’) Watford haven't created much at all, with the hosts looking the more likely of the two sides to open the scoring this afternoon. Troy Deeney will be wondering why he isn't figuring up top, as Okaka hasn't been able to lead the line too effectively yet. Niang and Janmaat combine down the left, but Schmeichel is off his line quickly yet again to beat an eventual cross away.
(19’) OFF THE POST! Cleverley gives away a free kick, with Watford switching off entirely while defending it. Mahrez slides a pass into space in the box, rather than curling a normal cross in towards the back post, with Vardy able to squeeze a finish beyond Gomes. Mariappa covers in behind his goalkeeper and makes a vital interception, diverting the ball onto the woodwork and to safety!
(18’) Janmaat gives away a free kick for a foul on Okazaki, with Leicester opting to take the dead ball quickly. Albrighton is the target of a clipped pass over the top, but a stray first touch from the ex-Aston Villa winger bobbles through for Gomes to gather. The ideas are there from both outfits, but the execution isn't following suit.
(16’) Vardy hares his way down the left and threatens to get to the byline, but Kabasele stands up to the pace of the Englishman well. Watford attempt to kick on themselves, after a mistake from the hosts in midfield, but Okaka can't quite roll Huth to get in behind the Foxes. It has been a story of almosts so far at the King Power.
(14’) Capoue dances into space down the right-hand side and clips a lovely pass over the top for Okaka to chase. The ball skids off the turf, however, putting enough pace on it to head behind for a goal-kick. Lovely movement helped the Watford striker escape Benalouane, but he couldn't bring that down.
(13’) Albrighton jinks inside Amrabat and delivers yet another cross into the penalty area, but this time Prodl is present to clear. Vardy just hasn't been found in the box. Niang threatens down the left-hand side for Watford, but a looping delivery from the Frenchman is claimed well by Schmeichel. Moments later, Cleverley shoots a long way wide from the edge of the box.
(11’) Neither goalkeeper has been forced into a save quite yet, with the final ball not coming easily for either of these sides. Leicester have been looking the more likely to make something happen, but Vardy and Okazaki haven't received any good service thus far.
(9’) Amrabat drills in a low cross from the right-hand side, but Benalouane is very alert to slide in ahead of Okaka to clear the danger for the hosts! (8’) Mahrez and Albrighton have been very busy in the opening stages, flighting in plenty of crosses which have asked Gomes to command his area quite well. (6’) Leicester have stepped it up over the last few minutes, after a ponderous start. The Foxes win a corner on the left-hand side, which is punched half clear by Gomes, before Drinkwater lashes a terrible effort a long way over the crossbar from outside the box!
(4’) Albrighton whips in a cross from the left-hand side, but Janmaat is there to easily head clear. Moments later, Mahrez breaks down the opposite flank and dips a great delivery to the far post which forces Kabasele to nod a defensive header behind for a corner. The resulting set piece is taken short, before Albrighton's eventual cross sails over Benalouane. Wasteful stuff.
(2’) Janmaat cuts in from the left-hand side and tries his luck with his stronger right foot, but the Dutchman bends a shot shy of the far post. From the early stages of this game, it appears that Okaka is playing as a lone striker, with Capoue and Niang trying to get up in support.

Adrian Mariappa, Christian Kabasele and Sebastian Prodl make up a back three. The visitors have plenty of option to change system in-game, too.
TEAM NEWS: Yohan Benalouane features at centre-back for Leicester, as captain Wes Morgan is still struggling with injury problems. Neither of these sides have much to play for other than pride, which could lead to a rather deflated atmosphere at the King Power, but the Foxes will have their eyes set on a top-half league finish. Ending the campaign in eighth place is certainly not out of the question, which was unthinkable under Claudio Ranieri.

If Arsenal win their game in hand they will displace United in fifth and move to three points behind Manchester City. It's going to be a tense end to the season, that's for sure! United, though, will quickly turn their attention to the Europa League and hope to book safe passage to the final on Thursday.
FULL-TIME - Arsenal 2-0 United: After 25 matches without defeat, Mourinho's men go down to goals from Xhaka and Welbeck at Emirates Stadium. Wenger ends his Premier League hoodoo against the Portuguese and keeps his side's top-four hopes alive in the process.

HALF-TIME - Arsenal 0-0 United: The first half at Emirates Stadium fails to produce any goals, but it did provide plenty of excitement. De Gea was forced into a couple of impressive saves, the best coming when he kept out Ramsey with a strong right hand. Cech has been active too, reacting quickly to keep out Martial and Rooney across the opening period.
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) There will only be one minute of added time.
(43’) Sanchez attempts a one-two with Oxlade-Chamberlain but the England international supplies him with an overhit return pass that United mop up. Mourinho's side seem content to sit back and hold out until half-time.
(41’) The tempo has slowed since that flurry of action around the half-hour mark. Arsenal are playing more of the expect role now, though, controlling possession and working across the pitch in order to probe for openings.
(39’) OPTA STAT: Arsenal midfielder Xhaka was completed all 31 of his passes so far today.
(38’) We've got a break in play after a clash of heads between Monreal and Herrera. The United man appears to come off worse, but neither player goes off for treatment before the action resumes.
(37’) Welbeck controls a pass from Sanchez with a header free in the centre of the box, but as he goes for an ambitious overhead kick he misses the ball and the offside flag goes up! That was a pretty marginal call.
(36’) Ozil feeds Ramsey with an incisive ball to the edge of the area, but the Welshman has it hooked away from him by Jones. It's been an enthralling first half. Will we get a goal before the interval?
(34’) Smalling sends a wayward pass out for a throw-in near the halfway line rather than get Tuanzebe involved to his right. Mkhitaryan appears to point that out, and Mourinho gets up from his seat to try and rile the players with some applause.
(32’) ROONEY SHOULD'VE SCORED! Holding is pressured in the corner and opts to play the ball back into the box. Cech and Koscielny hesitate and Rooney pounces, latching onto the ball before being denied by the onrushing keeper! Poor communication in the Arsenal defence there.
(31’) It's all getting a bit frantic now! Ramsey narrowly misses a cross inside the six-yard box, with Ozil keeping it alive at the back post despite United claiming the ball hand gone out. Arsenal work it to Oxlade-Chamberlain, whose deflected shot is batted away by De Gea!
(30’) WELBECK! That was a great chance! Sanchez once more creates the opening with a final throughball for Ramsey. He holds off his marker and drills a pass towards Welbeck, whose first-time shot is blocked by Smalling. Sanchez is livid! He'd followed his pass and wanted it back.
(28’) Sanchez slips a pass towards the byline for Ramsey to chase. The Welshman tries to stand the ball up at the back post but he cannot get his foot around it enough to keep it in play.
(27’) GOOD BLOCK! An Arsenal corner falls for Welbeck at the back post and he controls it before taking a touch to try and spin away from Jones and get a shot in. He does just that, but the centre-back slides to get a leg in the way.
(26’) Herrera releases Mata down the right with an excellent ball. The former Chelsea man swings an early cross into the box with Mkhitaryan free, but he only finds Cech's hands.
(24’) Another positive run down the left from Gibbs sees the referee play on after a tug back from Mata. He loves to dribble across the top of the box but Carrick dispossesses him. Koscielny concedes a corner in a race with Martial as United look to break, and Rooney heads wide from the set-piece.
(22’) Arsenal opt to sit a bit deeper after the corner and United find it tough to break through their bank of nine players, five at the back with four in front of them.
(20’) Tuanzebe sets off down the right and is sent to ground by Sanchez, winning a free-kick in a dangerous area. Mata floats it to the back post for Mkhitaryan and his header back into the middle is put out for a corner.
(19’) After a dominant start from United, Arsenal have started to take control of the action. They're seeing more of the ball and keeping United penned back inside their own half for longer periods.
(17’) Gibbs is proving a real threat down the left, with Mata not always quick to follow his runs. The wing-back earns a corner which Ozil takes short to Sanchez, before Oxlade-Chamberlain passes straight to Martial. However, a handball by the Frenchman gives Arsenal another chance.
(15’) Ramsey slides a lovely pass down the right-hand channel for Welbeck, but the curl on it sends him away from goal rather than into the box. That enables Jones to get goal-side and hold up the striker, who loses out to Herrera when attempt to drive inside onto his left foot.
(14’) Oxlade-Chamberlain sees his cross headed away by Tuanzebe and the young right-back then plays a give-an-go with Martial, who knocks the return pass beyond Koscielny and draws a foul inside the Arsenal half to alleviate the pressure.
(13’) It's been an expansive start to proceedings, with both teams keen to attack and create openings. Cech and De Gea have already been called into action, but Arsenal will hope they can start to dictate terms more as the half continues.
(11’) OPTA STAT: Mourinho has faced Arsenal without losing more times in the Premier League than he has any other side (12 - W5 D7 L0).

(8’) United have seen the majority of possession so far in north London. Martial wriggles his way into the box before being tackled, but Herrera latches onto the loose ball and earns a corner off Holding.

(78’) This game is there for the taking for either side. There hasn't been many chances and it looks like one goal would be enough to clinch victory. As we approach the final 10 minutes of the game, it really could go either way.

(67’) Tadic tries his luck from long-range... It goes well wide of Jakupovic's goal. Better from Southampton going forward but they still lack urgency and neither goalkeeper has had a notable save to make here today.
(64’) Hull win a free-kick in the middle of the pitch, which Clucas lofts into the box and is met by Maguire, who heads the ball across goal. (51’) Markovic does well to dribble the ball to the Saints byline, however excellent defending from Stephens sees the danger cleared and they win a goal-kick.

(48’) Marco Silva will have been the happier of the two managers at the break, as the Tigers dominated much of the first-half but failed to show the same dominance and resolve in the final third.
(46’) The second half is underway!
Other than a superb Grosicki free-kick which clipped the post early on, there has been very little action here on the south coast. Neither side has had a shot on target. Southampton have been very lacklustre, and Hull have been on top, but they need to find that extra bit of quality in the final third.

The victory all but confirms Leicester's place in next season's Premier League, highlighting what a good job Craig Shakespeare has done since taking over. They now sit nine points clear of 18th-place Swansea City, who are in action tomorrow afternoon.
For the fifth league game in a row, West Brom were unable to find the back of the net, and it means that they have to leave with their fourth defeat in as many games. They were on the front foot for most of the second half and were presented with good opportunities to score, but, in the end, they couldn't do enough to get the better of Leicester's resolute back line.

Bar a surprising, but well-deserved, victory against Arsenal a month and a half ago, it’s been a slightly disappointing two-month period for West Brom, who seem to have taken their foot off the pedal since confirming their safety. Five of their last seven league games have ended in defeat, with Watford, Southampton and Liverpool all getting the better of the Baggies in their last three outings.
Another season, another 40-point barrier smashed by a Tony Pulis team, meaning that West Brom are not only safe from relegation but also have a great chance of finishing in the top half of the table for the first time in four years. They’re also only two wins away from surpassing their Premier League points record of 49, but they’ll have to perform much better here today than they have during April so far if they’re to get the better of Leicester.
Arsenal were the latest side to get the better of Leicester, although the Gunners’ victory only came courtesy of a late Robert Huth own-goal. With Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur still to play, the reigning champions will be viewing today’s clash as a must-win for them, especially as their opponents haven’t been in the best of form in recent weeks.
With six points separating themselves and the relegation zone, Leicester aren’t safe from the drop just yet, but a win here today would surely confirm their place in the Premier League for another season. Craig Shakespeare has done an excellent job of steering the Foxes away from danger since taking over from Claudio Ranieri, but his side currently find themselves on a slightly worrying three-game winless run.

Christian Benteke's double against his former club sees Crystal Palace come from behind to win their third successive match at Anfield, the first team to do so since Chelsea in 2005, as they take a massive step towards securing their place in the top-flight, while blowing the top-four race wide open.
(90’) FULL-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-2 CRYSTAL PALACE.
(90’) Palace are putting in an expert performance in seeing this match out, right in line with how they have played all afternoon. Right from the off they seemed to have it all figured out in defence, and they've been able to keep that focus all the way through, even after falling behind 1-0.
(90’) The first two minutes are plagued by an injury to Tomkins and a referee stoppage, as precious seconds continue to run off the clock. Palace are almost there - moments away from taking a massive step to pulling clear of the bottom-three.
(90’) The fourth official raises his board to indicate there will be six minutes added on at the end of this match - the first thing Liverpool fans have had to cheer about all afternoon.
--- 89’ Yellow card Grujic gets his name in the stats sheet, but not for the right reason as he's issued a yellow card soon after coming on. ---
--- 88’ Substitution Benteke cherishes the long walk to the touchline, and savours every moment of it, wasting precious time as he gives way for Frazier Campbell. ---
(86’) Liverpool are struggling mightily here. They've been unable to create much of anything all night, and now just keeping the ball in attack is proving problematic for them, while the tempo is completely gone from the match following the string of substitutions.
--- 84’ Substitution Klopp's third change in five minutes as Clyne replaced by Marko Grujic. ---
--- 83’ Substitution Palace use the stoppage to make their second swap as well, with Damien Delaney entering the fray at the expense of Cabaye. ---
--- 82’ Substitution Liverpool's second change sees Alberto Moreno replace Milner. ---
(81’) Defeat for Liverpool would leave them just two points up on Manchester City and three up on Manchester United, each of whom will have played two games fewer. Those clubs face each other in the Manchester Derby on Thursday, which is the silver lining for Liverpool, but defeat here would blow the top-four race wide open.
--- 79’ Substitution An attacking switch here for Liverpool, and a necessary one at that, as teenager Trent Arnold comes on to replace Lovren. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Palace's first change sees Patrick van Aanholt come on to replace Zaha. ---
(76’) STAT: Liverpool have lost just once in their last 24 Premier League games at Anfield (W15 D8).
--- 74’ Assist Puncheon is credited with the assist as he's the one who took the corner. ---
--- 74’ Goal! FROM BEHIND, PALACE LEAD! And it's that man, Benteke, again! A poor corner is played in by the visitors, but it skips by Firmino at the far post as the attacker fails to clear his lines, running kindly through for Benteke who tucks it in confidently! Muted celebrations from him against his former club, but you can see what it means to him! ---
(72’) Anfield has grown frustrated and impatient, as have the Reds, which is playing right into the hands of Palace who will probably be sensing the opportunity to go on and win this thing in the final 20 minutes.
(70’) Liverpool's inability to create seems to be spurred on by their impatience in possession. They aren't willing to slowly work the ball around in attack and wait for Palace to break their shape, instead trying to get forward quickly, which is playing right into the Eagles' hands.
(68’) Liverpool are up close to 500 completed passes, with Palace labouring to make it to 200. Those stats are far from telling, however, as it's Palace who will be far more pleased with their performance thus far and the result. Liverpool's 500 passes have hardly resulted in a chance from open play.
(66’) This second half has been rather dire and there are no signs of it coming to life in the final 25 minutes. That's what Palace will want, of course, so the responsibility falls to Liverpool to try and change that.
(64’) STAT: Roberto Firmino has scored in his last two Premier League games against the Eagles, with the goals coming in the 71st and 72nd minutes.
(62’) Changes certainly must be imminent, one would have to imagine, for Liverpool especially. Klopp surely will be pondering the idea of moving Firmino into a more central role, as Origi has hardly been able to factor into the match. Liverpool's bench tonight is relatively youthful, so he may bide his time before dipping into it.
--- 60’ Yellow card Milivojevic arrives late and trips up Can rather cynically, showing no remorse as he's shown yellow. ---
(58’) That's more like it! Firmino is onside as Lucas springs him with an incisive throughball, but Hennessey spots it right away and manages to burst off his line and collect just in the nick of time! Liverpool need more of that.
(56’) The tempo has struggled to find consistency in this match. There are spells of good, encouraging attacking play, but they're often short and sandwiched between long spells of nothing.
(54’) STAT: Crystal Palace have won on their last two visits to Anfield in the Premier League. The last team to win three in a row there were Chelsea in October 2005.
(52’) UNBELIEVABLE RUN! Simply sensational from Coutinho to skip past Puncheon, nutmeg Ward and nudge the ball beyond Kelly to tee himself up for a shot from eight yards, but his effort is blocked from point-blank range!
(50’) Coutinho lashes a shot wildly over the bar, but that's better from Liverpool as they show signs of life in attack. Hennessey has really had nothing to do since Coutinho's opener in the 24th minute - that's simply not good enough.
(48’) Lively start to this second half, as Palace have a spring in their step. The visitors seem encouraged by their late equaliser in the first half, as momentum is very much on their side at the moment. Liverpool have to be better if they are to push on and win this thing.
(46’) Here we go again!
Philippe Coutinho's magnificent free-kick put Liverpool ahead at the midway point of the first half, and it was looking like staying that way into the break until a Christian Benteke strike in the final minutes pulled Palace level heading into the interval. Chances have been few and far between through 45 minutes, but it's wonderfully poised in advance of the second half.
(45’) HALF-TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-1 CRYSTAL PALACE.
(45’) Benteke manages another shot, though this one significantly tamer and easy for Mignolet, as the board goes up to indicate an additional two minutes of stoppage-time.
(43’) STAT: Former Liverpool player Christian Benteke has now scored four goals in his three previous Premier League games at Anfield as an opposition player.
--- 42’ Assist Cabaye provides the assist. ---
--- 42’ Goal! PARITY RESTORED AT ANFIELD! Ward and Cabaye link-up craftily on the right flank and the Frenchman picks out a delightful cross for Benteke, who got behind his marker to smash home a first-time finish from close range! From nothing, Palace have the equaliser! ---
--- 40’ Yellow card Benteke becomes the first player booked on the night, following a foul on Lovren. ---
(38’) WHAT WAS HE DOING?! Lovely one-two on the left between Wijnaldum and Milner, with the former bursting into the area and squaring for Can. The midfielder has the goal at his mercy from 12 yards, but snatches at the shot and scuffs an effort laughably wide of the target!
(36’) Palace are showing the greater urgency here as we enter the final 10 minutes of the first half. Too much time is elapsing now between Liverpool's attacks, which has allowed Palace to generate some momentum after Coutinho's goal really took the wind out of their sails.
(34’) Better! That all stemmed from a good run from Zaha out wide, something Palace have had little of thus far. They win a corner and the pressure stays on following the initial delivery, but Puncheon's eventual header is straight into the waiting arms of Mignolet.
(32’) Palace are having next to no success trying to orchestrate an opening in attack. They don't have nearly enough width about them going forward, which has made life relatively easy on this Liverpool defence.
(30’) It has already opened up a fair bit here, with Palace committing more bodies forward than they have previously, and it leads to a good spell in attack for Liverpool as they exploit the newfound space available to them on the break.
(28’) STAT: Sam Allardyce has never won a Premier League game at Anfield as a manager (D3 L10). The only away ground he’s lost at as many times is Old Trafford (also 10).
(26’) That goal should go a long way to opening things up here at Anfield. Palace cannot afford to simply just sit back and defend now. They will have to loosen things up, which should really help the tempo of the match from a neutral perspective.
--- 24’ Goal! STUNNER! ABSOLUTE STUNNER! Well it was going to take something special for Liverpool to find the breakthrough, and that's about as special as it gets! Coutinho bends a sensational free-kick over the wall and back towards the near post, where it just sneaks in beyond a despairing Hennessey! That's a work of art! ---
(23’) Count them: nine players in defence for Palace as Liverpool get into the final third, almost all of them level with or in the penalty area. It's going to take something special from the Reds to pry themselves an opening - though they certainly have the creative types capable of pulling it off.
(21’) DECENT EFFORT! Well you know Benteke would love to bag himself a goal today! The striker shows great skill and strength to get beyond Lucas, with plenty of green grass in front of him. He approaches the top of the box and tries to bend on in at the far post, but his effort drifts just wide of the mark!
(19’) Liverpool are facing a sea of yellow every time they get into the final third. They're enjoying plenty of possession high up the pitch, but it's all been very innocent from them, largely due to the strong work being put in by the visitors in defence.
(17’) STAT: Only Spurs (18) and opponents Liverpool (14) have won more points across their last six Premier League games than Palace (13).
(15’) Both these teams are capable of scoring in bunches, but this start from Palace is indicative of a different sort of match than what would have perhaps been expected. Palace are packing bodies back in defence, basically telling Liverpool to try and break them down - which suggests we are in for a match a bit cagier in nature.
(13’) Puncheon is warned by the referee following a late and painful challenge on Firmino. The visitors are struggling to win the ball back, and when they do, keeping it is proving a whole other issue.
(11’) Nice work from Wijnaldum on the left as he does well to turn his man and cut inside on his right, but he passes up the chance at a shot, instead trying to thread a ball through for Fimino which never comes to fruition. Still, it earns a nice applause from these Anfield fans.
(9’) Palace have been far from sharp in the early stages, still trying to get into a rhythm. They have not looked very adventurous in possession, though have managed to tighten up at the back and make Liverpool work hard for an opening, which the hosts have yet to be able to do.
(7’) STAT: Liverpool have won their last two Premier League games against Palace, after going four without a victory against them (D1 L3).
(5’) Liverpool have started positively, showing good intent on the front foot as they get forward encouragingly and deliver some enticing crosses into the area. The hosts are enjoying plenty of possession on this sunny Sunday afternoon.
(3’) The pressure on both these sides has increased in the past 24 hours with Hull City, Swansea and Manchester United all winning this weekend. These clubs do not know where they will end up in a month's time, but three points today would be a massive step for them in the right direction.
(1’) AND THEY'RE OFF! Crystal Palace in yellow as they get the match underway, attacking left to right, with Liverpool in red.
Sam Allardyce makes one change from last weekend's draw against Leicester. James Tomkins comes in to partner Martin Kelly in defence, replacing Mamadou Sakho, who is ineligible to face his parent club.
Jurgen Klopp names an unchanged side from last weekend's victory at West Brom. Joel Matip and Lucas Leiva were doubts, but they keep their place in the side despite not being able to train all week because of minor injuries.
SUBS: Van Aanholt, Sako, Speroni, Flamini, Campbell, Delaney, McArthur.
CRYSTAL PALACE (4-2-3-1): Hennessey; Ward, Tomkins, Kelly, Schlupp; Cabaye, Milivojevic; Townsend, Puncheon, Zaha; Benteke.
SUBS: Grujic, Moreno, Karius, Arnold, Gomez, Woodburn, Brewster.
LIVERPOOOL (4-3-3): Mignolet; Clyne, Matip, Lovren, Milner; Wijnaldum, Lucas, Can; Firmino, Coutinho, Origi.
CONFIRMED TEAM NEWS:
Despite their recent good run of form, Palace have yet to pull comfortably clear of the relegation zone, just four points up on Swansea, whose victory on Saturday keeps the pressure on – and trips to Liverpool, Manchester United and Manchester City, as well as a home date with Tottenham, certainly complicate matters.
While the difference between them and Crystal Palace in the table is rather large, today’s fixture is far trickier than it appears. Sam Allardyce has the Eagles firing on all cylinders once again, winning five of their last seven in the league.
The good news for the Reds is four of their final five matches comes against teams in the bottom half of the table, with the lone exception being a home fixture against ninth-place Southampton – a very negotiable fixture list for Jurgen Klopp and company.
Liverpool, unbeaten in seven in the Premier League, have a battle on their hands over the final five games of the season to fend off the two Manchester clubs and keep their place in the top-three, which of course comes with automatic qualification to next season’s Champions League.
