(46’) Palace get the second half underway!
Andros Townsend has Palace ahead at the end of a consistently entertaining first half at Selhurst Park, with chances bountiful for both sides. Arsenal held the advantage in possession, but it's the Eagles who looked more threatening going forward, and they have a lead to show for it.
(45’) HALF-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-1 ARSENAL.
(45’) There will be one minute added on at the end of this first half, as Arsenal win a corner shortly after the board goes up. Xhaka picks out Gabriel with his delivery, but the defender's header is saved by Hennessey.
(44’) Successive corners for Palace, but nothing comes of it. The second leads to an Arsenal throw, deep in their end, and they can't get the ball out from the back. Palace attack again quickly and a cross comes in for Townsend, but the winger is called for a foul and finally the visitors can relieve the pressure. They get up the pitch in a flash, but Welbeck sends an effort wide from an wakward angle.
(42’) Arsenal defenders standing and watching as Palace march their way up the pitch. It looked a few times like the visitors had a chance to break up the move, but it doesn't happen, and it leads to a real chance for Benteke, but he's thwarted at the near post by Martinez! Good positioning and reactions from the Arsenal keeper.
(40’) STAT: Goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez had kept a clean sheet in three of his four previous Premier League games started for Arsenal.
(38’) Everything good happening for Arsenal at the moment has Sanchez at the heart of it. If Palace can smother him and close him down, no one else, at least as of yet, has shown an ability or desire to step up and take charge.
(36’) What was Bellerin doing?! A dreadful attempt at a backpass threatens to play Benteke through. The striker pounces, but he lacks the pace to get through on goal as the threat is averted, much to the relief of the right-back.
(34’) CRUCIAL BLOCK! Ozil wriggles his way into the area from the left and threads in a low cross. Sakho partially cuts it out, but Sanchez is there to pounce, only to see his first-time effort blocked again by Sakho! Great bit of defensive play there, and at a vital moment from the Palace centre-half.
(32’) Arsenal have noticeably upped their urgency in the last few minutes, which has seen the tension rise at Selhurst Park. These loyal Palace supporters, some of the best in the top-flight, remain in full voice as they continue to create a hostile atmosphere for the Gunners.
(30’) Nervy moments in the Gunners defence as Cabaye sends a free-kick into the danger area, which leads to a half-chance for Kelly. The pace of this match is still very high and it remains wonderfully open, which had resulted in some excellent viewing from a neutral's perspective.
(28’) Arsenal have played much better since conceding, which will have to please Wenger. This is a side whose confidence has been shaken in recent weeks, so they easily could have folded in their attempts to weather Palace's storm.
(26’) STAT: Arsenal haven’t lost away to the Eagles in the top-flight since November 1979 (W6 D5).
(24’) NOT FAR AWAY! Hennessey beaten for the first time here, but he will be relieved to see that Sanchez strike flash just wide of the far post. It was cleverly orchestrated by the Chilean to carve out space for a shot and open up the angle, but he just fails to bend it in at the far post.
--- 22’ Yellow card Mustafi has been walking a fine line since his early foul on Benteke. His next one was always going to prompt a booking, and it does here in the 22nd minute. He has to be careful the rest of the way. ---
(21’) Decent response here by Arsenal as Sanchez and Monreal make noise in and around the penalty area. The full-back picks out the Chilean, who does well to set himself up for a shot with his first touch, but can't send his effort far enough away from Hennessey, who makes a relatively simple save.
(19’) There's a great tempo to this match, which remains entertainingly open as both sides show plenty of attacking intent. If the first 20 odd minutes are any indication, there should be plenty more goals to be had in this contest.
--- 17’ Goal! PALACE STRIKE FIRST! Great combination play between Cabaye and Townsend, with the former playing Zaha through on the right. The winger slips as he sends in his cross, but gets enough on it to return it to Townsend who powers home from in close! ---
--- 17’ Assist Zaha lost his footing but still managed to get the cross in as he assists the goal. ---
(15’) Great centre-forward play from Welback, who shows his underrated physicallity as he battles away to put Kelly under pressure. The centre-half does well to recover, and smartly forces the ball behind for a corner, as not to take any chances.
(13’) A poor ball out from the back by Martinez leads to a period of unnecessary pressure on the Arsenal defence, but the visitors do well to organise themselves quickly and see away the threat, with Sanchez doing especially well to track back and intervene.
(11’) STAT: Sam Allardyce’s last league win over Arsene Wenger in the Premier League was in May 2010 with Blackburn Rovers – he’s lost nine of the last 10 meetings since (D1).
(9’) LOVELY HIT! Much, much better from Arsenal as they mount their first threatening attack of the night. Monreal picks out Elneny smartly from the right and the midfielder places a first-time effort in towards the far post, but Hennessey is able to parry at full-stretch.
(7’) Nasty challenge! Mustafi gets the timing all wrong and scissors Benteke to the ground just outside the box. Michael Oliver does well to play advantage and it ends with a shooting chance for Milivojevic, but his effort bends wide of the near post. Oliver has a talking to with Mustafi after, who is incredibly lucky to escape without a booking.
(5’) The pace of these Palace attackers is already causing one or two problems for the Arsenal backline. Townsend and Zaha are flying down the flanks at every opportunity, with Palace quick to play balls over the top for them to chase.
(3’) Arsenal, a team whose confidence is in a fragile state, need a quick start to settle the nerves, but they don't get one. Palace have a spring in their step from the off, while the Gunners appear very tentative in possession. Cabaye gets the first shooting chance, but lifts an effort miles over as he gets the contact all wrong.
(1’) AND THEY'RE OFF! The Eagle soars across Selhurst to signal kick-off, and soon after Arsenal get the game started. The visitors are in their yellow away strip as the get us underway, attacking right to left, with Palace in red and blue.
Arsene Wenger also names an unchanged side, this from the win over West Ham last weekend. Emiliano Martinez keeps his place in goal as Petr Cech (calf) and David Ospina (back) miss out, while Laurent Koscielny remains sidelined at least one more week with a back issue.
Scott Dann, Patrick van Aanholt, James Tomkins and many of Palace's other regulars remain out, as Sam Allardyce names an unchanged side from the defeat at Southampton last weekend. Joe Ledley, who was supposed to return following the birth of his child, is not in the team, but James McArthur returns from a knock and is included amongst the substitutes.

Palace’s winning run has brightened their outlook on next season, as they have pulled three-points clear of the relegation zone, having played two fewer games than both Hull City and Swansea below them, putting added emphasis on tonight’s London derby.

And while Arsenal’s top-four streak is in peril, that’s not what’s grabbing the headlines. Everyone is fixated on what the future holds for Arsene Wenger, with many of even the club’s most loyal supporters turning on English football’s longest-serving manager.
Arsenal enter tonight’s match seven points back of fourth place Manchester City, albeit with two games in hand. Their recent slide has created plenty of cause for concern in north London, as the club’s streak of 20 successive seasons finishing in the top four looks in real jeopardy.

FULL-TIME: LEICESTER CITY 2-0 SUNDERLAND
(90’) There goes the final whistle and it's five out of five for Craig Shakespeare and Leicester City, who move up to 10th in the table, while Sunderland remain eight points from safety at the bottom of the Premier League.
(90’) GREAT BLOCK! Leicester are looking to put the icing on the cake and Slimani twists and turns in the area to work space for the shot. However, Kone recovers to block his strike on goal to prevent further embarassment for Sunderland.
(90’) We are now into the first of three minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game.
(90’) Mahrez finds the chest of Slimani with a good diagonal ball. The Algerian waits before laying it off for Albrighton, but he drills his ambitious attempt wide of the post.
(87’) Seconds later, Mahrez gets the better of Oviedo before whipping the ball towards the near post. However, Pickford is equal to it before Vardy's rebound is deflected wide.
(86’) Leicester are just growing in confidence as the game goes on. A neat passage of play opens the door for King to run through and try his luck, but it is simple enough for Pickford to gather.
(84’) Vardy has now scored seven goals in his last nine appearances for club and country. It is strange now to think that, under Ranieri, he managed just five goals in his previous 23 games in the Premier League this season.
--- 82’ Substitution Leicester's third and final change sees Ndidi replaced by Andy King who, last season, became the first player to win the top three divisions with the same club in the Premier League era. ---
--- 80’ Substitution The final throw of the dice from Sunderland sees Rodwell replaced by Darron Gibson, whose last Everton appearance came here at the King Power Stadium on the day that Leicester were officially crowned Premier League champions. ---
--- 78’ Assist Albrighton claims his second assist of the game after showing great determination for the ball, before showing equally good awareness to pick out Vardy in the box. ---
--- 78’ Goal! VARDY STRIKES AGAIN!!! Five goals in five games for the rejuvenated number nine! Albrighton is the architect once again as he gets away from Jones down the left wing before finding Vardy, who controls before firing into the roof of the net beyond the despairing dive of Pickford. 2-0 Leicester! ---
(77’) OFF THE POST! Rodwell's cross is cleared by Fuchs but only as far as Anichebe, whose shot deflects off Huth before crashing against the upright, before Defoe smashes the rebound into the side-netting. That passage of play sums up Sunderland's season in all fairness.
(75’) Shakespeare is on course for a fifth straight Premier League victory since taking charge of Leicester. Only Carlo Ancelotti and Pep Guardiola have won more, having come out on top in each of their opening six matches as a manager in the English top-flight.
--- 73’ Substitution The other sees Larsson replaced by Wahbi Khazri, who comes on as a sub for the sixth game running. ---
--- 73’ Substitution Moyes looks to the bench and makes a double substitution. First, Cattermole's return comes to an end as he is replaced by Victor Anichebe, who makes his own comeback after nearly three months out with a knee ligament injury. ---
(71’) That was the breakthrough that the hosts had been threatening over the last few minutes, although Sunderland will feel hard done by after failing to make the most of their opportunities earlier in the match.
--- 69’ Assist Albrighton created the goal with a wonderful cross from the left that was begging to be attacked. ---
--- 69’ Goal! SLIMANI HEADS LEICESTER INTO THE LEAD!!! The substitutes combine to put the hosts in front! Albrighton is able to cut back onto his right foot and deliver a delicious ball into the box for Slimani, who powers a header past Pickford for his first goal of 2017 and sixth in the Premier League. 1-0 Leicester! ---
(67’) Leicester have their tails up here and Mahrez sends an inviting ball into the box, but an alert Kone is able to clear the danger with Vardy and Slimani lurking.
(65’) Leicester's record signing after arriving from Sporting Lisbon for £28 million at the start of the season, Slimani is now making his seventh consecutive appearance as a substitute for the Foxes. A first goal of 2017 would be greatly appreciated for the home fans here...
(63’) GOOD SAVE! Leicester immediately threaten with a long throw into the box met by Huth, whose header forces Pickford into a smart save at full stretch.
--- 62’ Substitution Meanwhile, Gray makes way for Marc Albrighton, who comes on for his 99th Leicester appearance. ---
--- 62’ Substitution Shakespeare makes a double change in a bid to break the deadlock. The first sees Islam Slimani replace Okazaki. ---
(60’) We are still goalless as we hit the hour-mark at the King Power Stadium, where the home fans are getting a little restless with their side at the moment. However, their players are looking a lot more purposeful at the moment.
(58’) GOOD EFFORT! Larsson's free-kick is deflected away but only as far as Defoe, whose instinctive volley from the edge of the area is straight at Schmeichel. Nevertheless, that just demonstrated the natural ability that the 34-year-old possesses and he will be craving further opportunities.
(56’) WHAT A DISAPPOINTMENT! Larsson has not scored for two years and that was evident, as he gets his delivery all wrong and sends it flying over the crossbar much to the amusement of the home fans.
(54’) FREE-KICK TO SUNDERLAND! Defoe runs at Benalouane and draws a foul out of the Tunisian. A free-kick is awarded in a very dangerous position for the hosts and Larsson is stood over the ball...
(53’) It has been a very open start to this second half and Larsson tries his luck for Sunderland. The Swede lets fly from outside the area but his shot is right down the throat of Schmeichel, who easily gathers.
(51’) Huth endured contrasting fortunes against Sunderland during his time at Stoke City. He scored the winner against the Black Cats in February but, 12 months later, was sent off in a defeat for the Potters. He will be hoping his latest appearance against them results in three points.
(49’) GOOD BLOCK! Sunderland launch a strong attack at the start of the second half and an unmarked Borini is found in the box. However, the Italian's shot is well charged down by Huth.
(46’) KICK-OFF! There goes the whistle and Leicester get the ball rolling once more.
The teams are making their way back out onto the field and the second half is imminent...
Sunderland have looked dangerous going forward and asked plenty of questions of the Leicester defence so far. However, they have all been answered by the hosts, who are stubborn defensively and strong on the counter-attack but not offered too much else otherwise.
HALF-TIME: LEICESTER CITY 0-0 SUNDERLAND
(45’) And that was the last action of the first 45 minutes as Mr Scott blows for half-time.
(45’) JUST WIDE! Leicester embark on the counter and Mahrez sweeps the ball towards Gray on the left flank. Once again, he drifts inside Gray but his effort is well wide of the target on this occasion.
(44’) GREAT EFFORT! Gray drifts inside of Jones before unleashing a bending effort towards the far corner, which is brilliantly pushed around the post by the outstretched Pickford.
(42’) It is now eight hours since Sunderland last found the net in the Premier League. However, you feel that breaking the deadlock here would rejuvenate their confidence in front of goal, which will be vital in their survival bid.
(40’) We are into the final five minutes of the first half and we are still goalless at the King Power Stadium. Sunderland are looking a lot more dangerous going forward, but Leicester have been very strong defensively so far.
(37’) Meanwhile, Sunderland are awarded another free-kick but, yet again, Leicester are equal to Larsson's delivery. They may not have got anywhere so far, but Moyes will be pleased with the Black Cats' efforts.
--- 35’ Yellow card Business as usual for Cattermole, who marks his return by going into the notebook after trying to stop Gray from embarking on a dangerous counter-attack following a Sunderland corner. ---
(33’) Sunderland's record signing after joining from Lorient for £13.6 million at the start of the season, N'Dong has earned his recall to the starting line-up after impressing as a sub against Watford on Saturday. He was not too far away there and needs to continue to ask questions of the Leicester defence for his side.
(31’) N'Dong is the next player to try his luck for the visitors. The Gabon international lets fly from the edge of the penalty area, but pulls his effort well wide of the post.
(30’) Sunderland will be pleased with the way they have performed in the opening half an hour. The Black Cats have forced several corners, but do need to make more of those opportunities in order to take anything away from this game.
(28’) Defoe's most recent goal against Leicester came in a 2-1 victory in December's reverse fixture. However, the Black Cats have won just two of their 14 Premier League matches since then.
(26’) Defoe, who has scored four goals in his last five appearances against Leicester in the Premier League, is looking to continue his impressive record today. He drops off to the edge of the area to receive the ball from Borini, but an ambitious long-range effort curls well wide of the target.
(25’) Larsson's delivery is never normally far off the target and he asks question once more, but Leicester answer them with some stubborn defending to clear the danger.
(24’) A fourth corner of the match for Sunderland after their third deflects behind off Huth. The Black Cats need to make the most of these opportunities, you feel...
(22’) Both sides appear to have lost a little bit of momentum over the past couple of minutes. Neither are really pushing forward and instead trying to regain some rhythm by knocking the ball around in defence.
(20’) We are still goalless after 20 minutes at the King Power Stadium, where Sunderland have never been Leicester in the English top-flight. Although, the Black Cats have won on two of their last four visits here - both of which came in the Championship.
(18’) Route one from Sunderland as Pickford's long kick is flicked on by Borini for Defoe to chase into the area. The England striker gets in behind the defence but the angle is tight and Schmeichel is able to block. Nevertheless, those are worrying signs for Leicester, who cannot afford to give the 14-goal striker any time whatsoever.
(16’) Leicester are awarded a free-kick near the touchline, which Mahrez stands over. The winger's delivery is met by Huth at the far post, and Pickford has to punch his looping header over the crossbar.
(14’) At the other end, some space opens up for Oviedo on the left hand side. The Costa Rica international whips an inviting ball towards the six-yard box, but an unchallenged Schmeichel gathers.
(13’) PENALTY?! Gray goes to ground under a challenge from Rodwell just inside the area. However, the referee remains unmoved and Sunderland are able to clear the danger.
(12’) It is now 10 years since Simpson made 14 appearances on loan at Sunderland during their promotion to the Premier League, while he also played 139 times for their great rivals Newcastle from 2009 to 2013.
(10’) GOOD DEFENDING! Unusually, Defoe finds himself in space out on the right wing and whips a delicious delivery into the box. Larsson is waiting at the far post, but Simpson reads the danger and is able to make a very important clearance.
(9’) The Foxes' transformation is epitomised by the fact that they have scored 11 goals in four Premier League games under Shakespeare. That is just as many as they managed in their last 14 league matches under Claudio Ranieri!
(7’) Leicester are slowly starting to gain the upper hand on proceedings. They are looking so confident on the ball and more like the side that won the Premier League title last season.
(5’) Okazaki, who recently scored his 50th international goal for Japan, last found the net in the Premier League against Sunderland in the reverse fixture in December. The 30-year-old got into a good position there and will need to produce more of the same movement in order to end his drought.
(3’) GOOD PLAY! Following an open start to the match, Gray gets the better of Larsson down the left flank and delivers a low cross to the near post. Okazaki meets it but can only direct the ball wide of the target Nevertheless, that was very positive play by Leicester.
(1’) KICK-OFF! Mr Scott blows his whistle and Sunderland get the match underway at the King Power Stadium.

And that will do it from Vicarage Road as Watford pick up their second win on the bounce. Goals from Niang and Deeney did the damage at home, as the Hornets were able to withstand the dismissal of Britos without too much worry. West Brom flattered to deceive all game. That's all from us, thanks for tuning in.
(90’) Nyom gets space at the back post once again, and this time his strike finds its way through to goal, only for the keeper to parry it. That sparks an interesting counter, but Doucoure made the wrong choice to lay it off to Cleverley.
(90’) A gap opens up for Robson-Kanu, who plays a great pass for Nyom at the back post, but he's blocked by his own teammate Phillips, to a loud cheer from the home fans at the expense of their former player.
(89’) Gomes is out again to leap onto a cross from Brunt, and West Brom's chances of getting anything from this game are diminishing by the second.
(86’) Robson-Kanu breaks and has Phillips to his left and Rondon to his right. He opts for the former, who continues down the flank and whips in a dangerous ball that's headed away at the back post.
--- 83’ Yellow card Chadli's free-kick is sent right back to him, and the winger runs right into Cleverly, losing the ball. The ex-Manchester United barely has time to get his bearings before he's barged over by Nyom. No escaping a yellow this time. ---
(81’) Nyom scythes down Success in view of the referee, and he looks like he wants to go back in for more! The referee pulls the West Brom man over, and he's lucky to escape with just a lecture.
--- 79’ Substitution Niang looks exhausted, and is withdrawn for Success, who made his debut for Nigeria recently. ---
(78’) Scenes in the Watford dugout as Mazzarri has some heated words for his goalkeeping coach. You wouldn't think that his side are two goals to the good! All isn't well in Hornets land it seems.
(76’) SPILL! Rondon worked the ball through to Chadli. It looked to be all Gomes as the keeper raced off his line, but the ball slipped out of his grasp, surprising Phillips who was in a position to tap that in!
(73’) Brunt again puts the defence under pressure with a testing ball, but Rondon, who connected with it, wasn't able to steer it on target. Watford continue to hold on.
(71’) West Brom have been dominating the ball for the past few minutes, but Watford are dealing with everything that's being thrown their way. Less than 20 minutes for the visitors to make something happen.
--- 69’ Yellow card Niang is the latest player to get booked. ---
--- 69’ Substitution Amrabat is sacrificed to get an extra defender on in the shape of Mariappa. ---
(68’) Mazzarri is absolutely furious at that turn of events and had to be physically calmed down by one of his staff members. This is the immpetus that West Brom needed - Deeney's goal is so vital for the home side now.
--- 65’ Red card! MIGUEL BRITOS IS SENT OFF! Second bookable offence for the defender. He was playing catch-up with Rondon and appeared to tug the shirt of the West Brom forward, who needed no second invitation to go down. And down go Watford to 10 men. ---
(65’) Better from Watford as they pen the visitors back in their own half. This is the kind of play that Mazzarri would like to see for them to close out this game.
(63’) Amrabat gets space down the right-hand side and feeds Janmaat on the overlap. The substitute pings in a vicious ball that is inches away from being met by the head of Deeney.
--- 61’ Substitution Another Baggies change as Rondon replaces Livermore. ---
(60’) West Brom had a good chance there to tie things up as Chadli gets on the end of a Brunt pass but can't convert at the back post. Moments later, Phillips latches onto a long ball out of defence and wins a corner for the visitors.
--- 58’ Yellow card Livermore got away with a bad challenge earlier on Niang, but after he hacked down Janmaat, the referee decides to take action and book the midfielder. ---
--- 56’ Substitution James Morrison is introduced for McAuley. ---
(56’) Niang is chopped down by Jake Livermore, and Mazzarri isn't happy at another tough challenge against one of his players. He has a few words for the West Brom players.
(53’) Brunt sends a free-kick into the thick of the mixer, and it falls kindly for Chadli, who was running at too much speed to direct that one on target.
(51’) West Brom now have a mountain to climb. Watford have shown that they can take the visitors completely out of the game, and look set for another spell of dominance.
--- 49’ Assist That was nothing more than a punt from Niang and it ended up working out. ---
--- 49’ Goal! DEENEY MAKES IT TWO! A hopeful hoist down the centre catches Nyom and Evans out, with the Watford captain stealing in between the pair to prod the ball into the net on his backside! ---
(46’) Off we go again.
--- 46’ Substitution McClean, centre of the firestorm at the end of the half, is withdrawn for Matt  Philips. ---
And that will do it for now from Vicarage Road, as Watford hold a 1-0 advantage thanks to a stunner from Niang. West Brom were in the ascendancy as the half progressed, but were unable to seriously test the keeper, although they certainly tested the patience of the officials and the home fans with some rough challenges. A lot to play for in the second half, so stay tuned.
--- 45’ +6 Yellow card McClean and Holebas clash in an aerial challenge and as they trudge down the touchline, the West Brom man kicks out at the full-back. This time, the officials step in to issue a booking. ---
(45’) Watford are up in arms as Holebas is again sent to the turf, this time from a terrible challenge from Dawson on the near side. The assistant referee was right on top of that one but doesn't make a call!
--- 45’ +3 Substitution Prodl is off and on comes Janmaat. ---
(45’) It looks like Watford have done enough to see this game out to half-time, although there may be one last twist before the break as Prodl looks to be in some pain and unable to continue.
--- 43’ Yellow card Robson-Kanu tugs back Holebas and is shown a yellow card. ---
(43’) This has really been a decent spell for West Brom, and Pulis will want his men to translate that to the scoreboard with half-time around the corner. Watford are just trying to steady things.
(41’) GRAZES THE POST! Chadli takes charge of the set-piece, and curls it for the top corner, but it takes a lick of paint off the frame of the goal before heading out of play!
--- 40’ Yellow card Britos fouls Robson-Kanu and is shown the first booking of the game. ---
(38’) Watford again defend well to deal with a potentially dangerous free-kick from Chris Brunt. West Brom have shown more ambition since the half-hour mark, but it's nothing to seriously trouble the home isd.e
(35’) Robson-Kanu holds up the ball and inches it wide for Nyom who chops past Amrabat, but is forced to hack the ball into the box before it goes out of play. Watford can defend that cross.
(33’) Good play from Allan Nyom following the breakdown of a corner. He embarks on an ungainly but powerful run down the right that takes him past two players, before Tom Cleverley eventually robs him of possession.
(31’) Doucoure pushes the ball through to Amrabat, who did well to make something of that tricky pass. He releases a shot that's so bad it almost ends up being a nice little tee up for Deeney.
(26’) Even though Niang's wonderful goal is the difference between the sides, Capoue has been the most influential player on the park. He's a magnet for the ball, and West Brom have resorted to fouling him more than once.
(23’) West Brom haven't managed to escape their own half for a long while now. Despite limiting the shooting chances that Ben Foster has had to face, Tony Pulis will be concerned at their lack of time on the ball.
(21’) Watford are trying to use what's left of the momentum from Niang's goal to score again, but they're having no luck getting any change out of the West Brom defence.
(18’) Jose Holebas lines up a long throw aimed for the head of Etienne Capoue. It bounces kindly for Niang at the top of the box, but the forward lashes it wildly into the evening sky.
(16’) Niang, with confidence coursing through his veins after that goal, goes charging at the defence but loses his balance. However, he keeps his head and works the ball wide, where a dangerous cross into the six-yard area is inches away from Deeney.
--- 13’ Goal! SUPERB GOAL! Niang sets this game alight with a sublime piece of football. He gets the ball a long way from goal but drops his shoulder and drifts infield. Once the ball's on his right boot, he lets fly from the edge of the area and arrows it in! ---
--- 13’ Assist Deeney will be credited with the assist. ---
(11’) There's a little bit of space between the Watford midfield and the defence, with the home side pushing their central trio up to press their West Brom counterparts. Another quick ball like Fletcher's earlier and the hosts could be in trouble.
(9’) It continues to be relatively quiet and uneventful here with both sides taking some time to get into their stride. Will Chadli come back to rue that missed chance?
(6’) HE CAN'T FINISH! Darren Fletcher sprays a good ball down the line for Chadli to chase, and the winger evades the keeper and tries to follow it over the line, but it's cleared away!
(3’) Not a whole lot happening to start the game, although Walter Mazzarri has already hopped out of the dugout to express his frustration at a needless corner given away by his side.
(1’) Off we go.

A thrilling contest at Stamford Bridge ends with what is arguably Chelsea's most important victory to date under Antonio Conte! Eden Hazard's first half brace, see the Blues through by the narrowest of margins as Chelsea take a massive step towards the title - they haven't clinched it yet by any means, but it sure feels that way after tonight.
(90’) FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 2-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Kante goes into the book for a poor challenge, but the ensuing free-kick is dealt with and that may just about do it! ---
(90’) SHOCKING MISS! That should have tied it! No ifs, ands or buts, that should have been the equaliser! The ensuing corner is flicked on and falls directly into the path of Stones, wide open in the centre, but somehow he gets under it, sending his effort over the bar! Unbelievable!
(90’) WAS THAT THE CHANCE?! Three minutes of stoppage-time and City come to life out of nowhere! Nolito lifts an exquisite delivery in for Aguero at the far post. The striker slides in at full-stretch to meet it, but he's thwarted by Courtois!
--- 90’ Substitution A roar of approval as these Chelsea supporters greet the final change of the night with a thunderous applause, as Hazard departs, having scored both the Blues' goals tonight, replaced by Ruben Loftus-Cheek. ---
(89’) You have to imagine that should Chelsea hold on to this lead, and it's looking that way now as they won't let City out of their own half, then they will have one hand on the trophy. Their remaining fixture list isn't very daunting, with the trip to Old Trafford in a fortnight the only real difficult test, at least on paper. It would take an unprecedented collapse and a perfect end to the season for Spurs to turn this title 'chase' into a 'race'.
(87’) Chelsea have taken the match over, as fatigue appears to have set in for City, who are struggling to get back on the ball. The Blues are spending a lot of time in attack here, and it's the new face of Willian who wins them a corner, in front of a patch of screaming supporters, urging their side through to the finish line.
--- 85’ Substitution Another roll of the dice from Guardiola, as City are running out of time. Nolito comes on for the final five minutes, replacing Sane. ---
--- 83’ Yellow card Hostile appeals for a sending off from the Chelsea faithful as Kompany goes sliding into a challenge on Hazard with reckless abandon. It looked a lot worse initially that it actually wound up being in the end, so Dean does well to only produce a yellow. ---
--- 81’ Substitution Substitutions taking over here, plaguing the tempo of the match. Chelsea use their second to replace Fabregas with Willian. ---
--- 79’ Substitution City need a match winner and maybe this man can provide it. Raheem Sterling enters the fray, at the expense of De Bruyne, with just over 10 minutes remaining. ---
--- 77’ Yellow card Delph puts in what looked something of a decent challenge, but Dean doesn't see it that way and issues the midfielder a yellow card. ---
(76’) HE'S SKIED IT! Massive chance goes begging for Chelsea! A measured attack by the hosts and a pull-back that comes for Fabregas, who makes a mess of the pass. It still runs through for Hazard, on a hat-trick, but he can't keep his composure as he rifles an effort over the bar!
(74’) STAT: Manchester City have lost just one of their last six Premier League games in London (W3 D2).
(72’) Chelsea get back and win a free-kick in a threatening area, which Luiz stands over, excitedly. The Brazilian takes a measured run up, but lashes his effort straight into the wall as the chance goes begging. Under 20 minutes to play now and it's on a knife edge.
(70’) City are having no luck in the air. They need to adopt a different approach in attack, because what they have going right now isn't working. There's a good width to them, but it's all a bit irrelevant if they can't make anything of the eventual crosses.
(68’) Naughty one from Fabregas as he takes every precaution to ensure Kompany is sent toppling over. The ensuing free-kick is lifted into the area from a long way out, and finds an orange shirt, but it's quickly played into the waiting arms of Courtois.
(66’) City are showing all the initiative, which is somewhat expected given the fact that they trail, but Chelsea have to be careful not to drop too deep. Courtois hasn't been troubled much by any means, but the Blues are going longer and longer between their spells in possession.
(64’) STAT: Antonio Conte hasn’t lost consecutive home league defeats as a manager since November 2009 while in charge of Atalanta.
(62’) Guardiola echoes the frustration of his players as Silva has a decision go against him in midfield. Silva has been on the wrong of a few calls, in his own opinion, and is being warned here by Mike Dean. Meanwhile, Guardiola pleads his case to the fourth official before being greeted by an empathetic Conte, who offers up a friendly handshake, which the Spanish boss accepts with a smile.
(60’) Anticipation builds as City win a free-kick in a threatening area, packing the penalty box with bodies. De Bruyne's delivery is played in low, however, and it's a very poor one for Sane as the German has to work hard just to win a corner out of it.
(58’) It's turning into a bit of a chess match now as Chelsea organise themselves off the ball and invite City to come after them. The Blues are like a pride of lions, sitting in the shade, waiting to pounce. City have to be careful not to get frustrated and open themselves up to much, or they will be punished.
(56’) City are very focused, or at least appear to be, in possession, as they park themselves in the attacking half and patiently search for an opening. Chelsea are so structured off the ball, however, which is making life very difficult on the visitors as they try and break down this wall of blue shirts.
(54’) STAT: There have been four red cards in the last five league meetings between these sides, with three being shown to Man City players.
--- 52’ Yellow card Horribly timed! The tackles continue to come flying in and at this rate, if Dean doesn't take charge, it could lead to someone getting injured. He pulls out the yellow on this occasion and really didn't have much choice as Clichy flies in and takes out Pedro. ---
(50’) Fabregas is the victim of the latest foul, clipped and then stomped on accidentally by Clichy. Nothing more comes of it, as City quickly break the other way and win a free-kick of their own, which falls so kindly for Fernandinho in the area. The midfielder just snatches at it wildly, though, and skies his effort from eight yards!
(48’) A physical start to the second half as Kante gets a deserved talking to from referee Mike Dean following a very rash and unnecessary challenge on Silva, which has left the Spaniard a bit worse for wear. In fact, it was probably deserving of more than just a warning. The ensuing free-kick is headed back into the danger area by Kompany, and winds up smacking off the crossbar!
(46’) Here we go again!
--- 46’ Substitution Nemanja Matic is on for the second half, replacing Zouma. This should prompt another reshuffle, with Azpilicueta expected to drop back, Fabregas to be pushed forward and Pedro to slide to wing-back. ---
Momentum stayed with the visitors, who looked poised to complete the turnaround, before Fernandinho's foul on Pedro saw Chelsea awarded a penalty, which Hazard eventually converted on the rebound after having his initial effort, a poor one at that, stopped by Caballero. And that's where we stand at the interval.
The stakes couldn't be higher at Stamford Bridge, and the match has lived up to the hype - at least for now. Eden Hazard opened the scoring for Chelsea with a deflected effort, but Thibault Courtois' error gifted City their equaliser shortly after.
(45’) HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 2-1 MANCHESTER CITY.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated there will be just one minute added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Chelsea are enjoying a controlled spell in possession as we approach half-time, urged on by these spirited supporters behind them. You can feel the tension all the way up in Manchester, as this tactical battle between two expertly coached sides unfolds in front of their eyes.
(41’) Over 40,000 fans at Stamford Bridge, enthralled, fixated on what has been an appropriate embodiment of a match of this magnitude. A spectacle in every regard and it remains as lively as ever as we enter the final five minutes of this first half, which may yet just have another twist in it.
(39’) STAT: Pep Guardiola has never previously lost both league games against a single opponent in a season as a manager in his career so far.
(37’) Ambitious from De Bruyne! With his skill you really can't fault him for trying. De Bruyne makes waves down the left and finds himself in a generous pocket of space, before trying to catch Courtois off his line, but the angle proves too tight in the end as the keeper is able to knock the attempt behind for a corner.
(35’) Penalty Save Wilfredo Daniel Caballero Lazcano
--- 35’ Goal! HAZARD RESTORES CHELSEA'S LEAD! After having his initial penalty stopped, the Belgian sticks with it to bury the rebound - another massive moment in the title race! ---
--- 35’ Missed penalty A really poor penalty from Hazard, who rolls it tamely to his right, but good determination and focus to stick with it and calmly slot home the rebound. ---
(34’) PENALTY TO CHELSEA! Fernandinho can hardly believe his error! There's no doubt about the decision and no argument whatsoever from the midfielder, who sticks a lazy leg out and clearly trips Pedro to ground.
(32’) Manchester City have responded really well, and Chelsea's confidence appears to be shaken here. The visitors are getting forward at every opportunity as they continue to dictate possession and limit the Blues' looks at the other end. This is exactly the sort of character you would expect from a Pep Guardiola managed side.
(30’) STAT: Sergio Aguero has now scored seven Premier League goals against Chelsea, with five of those coming at Stamford Bridge.
(28’) REDEMPTION FOR COURTOIS! Not sure how much that will console him, but it's certainly a start! Silva produces a delicious throughball to play Sane in, but Courtois is off his line in a flash to close down the angle and deny City a second in as many minutes!
--- 26’ Goal! COURTOIS' GIFT, CITY LEAD! Dreadful from Courtois, whose pass out from the back is nowhere close to finding a blue shirt. He passes it straight to Silva, and while Courtois manages to save the initial effort, he has little chance at keeping out Aguero's rebound. ---
(24’) The tempo is starting to pick up a bit as both teams get a better feel for the rhythm of the match. City look a lot more comfortable on the ball, while Chelsea are content with conceding possession and biding their time before hitting on the break. The Blues' latest counter leads to another deflected effort that narrowly misses, crashing onto the roof of the net.
(22’) Smart run! City are doing a much better job now of getting into the channels and opening up space for the ball carrier. Aguero leads the latest attack and pieces together a crafty run into the final third, but he doesn't get the best contact on his final effort as fails to trouble Courtois.
(20’) Electrifying strike! Clever movement off the ball from the City attackers helps to open up space for Fernandinho, who decides to try his luck from just under 25 yards. He makes superb contact with the strike, stinging the palms of Courtois, who does well to parry.
(18’) STAT: Chelsea haven’t lost back to back Premier League games at Stamford Bridge since November 2011 under Andre Villas-Boas.
(16’) There really has not been much of an attacking threat posed by either side thus far. City have kept close to 65 per cent possession, but have precious little to show for it. Guardiola's side haven't even penetrated the Chelsea penalty area, let alone test Courtois, while one attack was all the Blues needed to snatch the lead.
(14’) Of course Chelsea simply need to worry about taking care of business themselves, but they will be further spurred on by the news of Wayne Routledge's opener at the Liberty Stadium, as Swansea currently lead Tottenham in the first half in Wales. Conte couldn't have drawn up a better start to the evening.
(12’) Has to be better! City try and mount a quick response, and it nearly happens for them as they break three against two. Sane leads the charge, but telegraphs his pass for Aguero, which is actually behind the striker, halting all his momentum and allowing Luiz to get a block in.
--- 10’ Assist Azpilicueta, pushed up to wing-back tonight from centre-half, rewards his manager's decision with an assist after just 10 minutes. ---
--- 10’ Goal! A STEP TOWARDS THEIR CORONATION! Chelsea take a big leap towards the title as they get off to a dream start at the Bridge! Azpilicueta make strides down the right and pulls it back for Hazard, whose first-time effort takes a slight deflection off Kompany to help it beyond Caballero! It's unlucky for the keeper, but he did make a real meal of that. ---
(9’) STAT: Sergio Aguero scored a hat-trick in this exact fixture last season as City won 3-0 – one of just three opposing players to hit a treble in a Premier League game at Stamford Bridge (Kanu in October 1999 and Robin van Persie in October 2011).
(7’) Sergio Aguero is getting booed every time he touches the ball, which isn't all that often actually. These fans remember his performance here last season, scoring all three goals in a lopsided Manchester City defeat. Of course the teams have changed a great deal since then, as has the Premier League landscape.
(5’) Both teams are getting a feel for one another in these opening five minutes. City are enjoying more time on the ball, but showing precious little intent in possession. Chelsea's looks have been limited, but they're doing well to break quickly when they do win it back.
(3’) Plenty of harmless possession for both sides in the early stages, until out of nothing Chelsea have a chance. Azpilicueta finds himself unmarked at the far post as a cross comes in, but instead of swinging his foot through it, he tries to play it back into the centre and City clear the danger.
(1’) AND THEY'RE OFF! A massive, title-shaping, season-altering night in Stamford Bridge, is underway. Manchester City in orange as they kick-off, attacking left to right, with Chelsea in blue.

Chelsea still lead the Premier League by seven points following Tottenham's win this afternoon. However, this defeat means there is plenty of work ahead of them to close out the title.
Crystal Palace make it four wins on the bounce to climb within striking distance of safety in the Premier League. They've beaten Chelsea at Stamford Bridge for the second time in two seasons thanks to goals from Christian Benteke and Wilfried Zaha.
FULL-TIME: CHELSEA 1-2 CRYSTAL PALACE
(90’) That's it. Palace have taken the three points from Stamford Bridge yet again.
(90’) Hennessey punches Hazard's free-kick away from danger. The offside flag is up anyway. That should be it.
(90’) Incredibly there is time for one more cross as Hazard is brought down by Milivojevic. Here comes Courtois...
(90’) One final probe from Chelsea in unsuccessful as Luiz's cross from deep is cleared away by Ward, although Pedro was offside anyway.
--- 90’ +7 Substitution Loftus-Cheek replaces Fabregas for the final seconds of the match. ---
(90’) Chelsea look out of options in the final third. They've tried everything this afternoon, but have been thwarted by resilience from the Palace backline.
(90’) CHANCE! Zaha almost puts the game to bed as he plays in Puncheon with a clever backheel. He collects the return from his team-mate, but can only steer the ball over the bar.
(90’) Chelsea cannot put a cross into the box due to pressure on the ball. Azpilicueta tries to break the stalemate, but sends the ball straight down Hennessey's throat.
(90’) Sakho goes down with apparent cramp. He has been excellent this afternoon.
(90’) There will be seven minutes of added time.
(90’) OVER! Costa drifts into space in the box and Fabregas picks him out with a lofted pass. He heads at goal, but his effort sails over the bar.
(88’) Kante is caught by Milivojevic and it presents the home side with another chance to send men forward. Fabregas lifts the ball to the back post, but Luiz can only power his header over the bar.
(86’) Chelsea continue to flood men forward, but they cannot find a way to goal as Pedro's cross is deflected into Hennessey's arms.
(85’) SAVE! Fabregas takes the ball in stride in the right inside channel and hammers the ball towards the near post, but Hennessey makes the save.
--- 83’ Yellow card Luiz goes into the book for pulling back Benteke and blasts the referee. He has to be careful there. ---
(82’) Willian fires the ball across the face of goal, but this time there is no blue shirt making a gamble at the back post to latch on to the ball. It has been one of those days for Chelsea.
(81’) OFF THE LINE! Hazard fires a low effort at goal and Hennessey makes the save. Costa latches on to the ball and attempts to steer it goalwards, only for Sakho to clear the danger on the line.
(80’) Fabregas sends Pedro down the left flank and he sends a perfect ball across the face of goal that seems destined to find Batshuayi, but Sakho makes a vital interception at the near post.
--- 79’ Yellow card Cahill makes a cynical challenge on Zaha to stop the winger's forward run. ---
(77’) Frustration is beginning to mount for Chelsea as Willian fires a low ball into the box, which is cleared by Sakho. Pedro makes a run down the opposite flank, only to take the ball out of play.
(76’) WIDE! Costa has not been good enough today and his woes continue as he places his header from Hazard's cross wide of the post from close range.
--- 74’ Substitution Substitution Marcos Alonso Mendoza Michy Batshuayi Tunga ---
(74’) OVER! Fabregas goes for goal from the 30-yard free-kick, but he curls his effort harmlessly over the bar.
--- 73’ Yellow card Milivojevic catches Willian late and he goes into the book. ---
(72’) CHANCE! Cabaye floats the ball to the back post and Delaney heads it into the six-yard area. Courtois hesitates and it almost costs the Blues, but Benteke can only steer his effort over the bar from a tight angle.
(71’) Luiz gives away a free-kick as Zaha is brought down on the left corner of the box. The Eagles could have an opening here.
(70’) Chelsea continue to probe away on the edge of the box, but the quality of their passing in the final third has not been good enough this afternoon.
--- 68’ Yellow card Benteke heads into the book for a challenge on Cahill. ---
(68’) CLOSE! Zaha wins a free-kick down the left flank and it allows Cabaye an opening to swing a cross into the box. The Frenchman curls his effort across the face of goal and Milivojevic makes a run over the ball, but it travels just past the post.
(66’) Costa attempts to strike on the turn in the box, but he loses his footing at the vital moment and it takes all the pace off his effort.
(64’) Willian raids with menace down the right and he crosses into the box with pace, but Sakho is there to clear the danger at the near post.
(62’) SAVE! Zaha comes within inches of doubling his tally for the afternoon as he latches on to Puncheon's pass and fires towards the bottom corner. However, Courtois makes a fine stop to steer the ball past the post.
(61’) BLOCK! Delaney makes his first impact off the bench as Hazard gives him an early test, striking the ball straight into his body.
--- 60’ Substitution Kelly replaces Townsend for the visitors. They've now used up all of their subs this afternoon. ---
--- 60’ Substitution Dann is stretchered off and is replaced by Delaney. Palace's second change at the back. ---
--- 59’ Substitution Matic makes way for Willian for the Blues. ---
(57’) Dann took the full brunt of Costa's strike on his knee and is down in agony on the deck. Not good news for the defender or Palace.
(56’) CHANCE! Pedro sends a pinpoint cross into the box for Costa. The striker has time and opts against the header to bring the ball down on his chest. He attempts to fire at goal, but Dann gets in his way to put him off the strike.
(54’) SAVE! Fabregas steers the ball into Costa's path in the box and on the slide the forward stretches out a letg, but Hennessey meets him there and makes the block.
(53’) CHANCE! Pedro slides the ball through to Costa, but he fails to fire the ball across the face of goal for Hazard's run. Instead he raids to the byline and cuts back, only to blast his effort off Dann.
(52’) Alonso sends in a delightful cross from the left flank and it reaches Fabregas 12 yards from goal. With a free header he opts not to go for goal and wastes the opportunity afforded to him in the final third.
--- 50’ Yellow card Costa goes into the book for a stray boot on Sakho in his attempt to win back possession on the edge of the box. ---
(49’) Hazard breaks into the right inside channel and he stands the ball up to the back post, but Costa can only guide his header into the hands of Hennessey.

Since then Chelsea have been on top, but have not managed to find a way through Wayne Hennessey or the Palace backline. A win this afternoon would be huge for the Eagles' survival hopes.
First the Eagles bounced back after trailing in the fifth minute to Cesc Fabregas' opener, with Zaha continuing his run of good form with a fine strike to equaliser. Benteke then displayed composure 90 seconds later to fire the visitors ahead.
Crystal Palace are on course for their fourth win on the bounce thanks to goals from Wilfried Zaha and Christian Benteke. Sam Allardyce's men have been under the cosh for the majority of the half, but have been resilient this afternoon.
HALF-TIME: CHELSEA 1-2 CRYSTAL PALACE
(45’) The referee ends the first half.
(45’) SAVE! Cahill loops a header up into the six-yard box and Luiz goes up to head at goal, but he cannot generate enough power on his effort to beat Hennessey.
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time.
(45’) OVER! The Blues win yet another free-kick and Fabregas floats the ball into the middle. Matic attacks it with a looping header that forced Hennessey to backpeddle and turn it over the bar.
(44’) Chelsea catch Palace out with a quickly-taken corner routine and it almost creates space on the edge of the box. Pedro slides the ball to Luiz, but Ward intervenes before he can strike at goal.
(42’) OVER! Palace win a corner down the right flank and Townsend whips the ball with pace to the back post. Tomkins peels off his man and has a free header at goal, but he can only lift his effort over the bar.
(40’) SAVE! Hennessey to the resuce again for the visitors as he gets down smartly to save Matic's drive from distance. The rebound bounces inside the six-yard box, but the Eagles get there first to scramble the ball away.
(39’) SAVE! Hazard turns his man with ease once again down the right flank and fires his effort towards the near post, but Hennessey is there to cover the angle and make the stop.
(38’) CLOSE! Alonso collects on the left and drills his effort across the face of goal. Hennessey gets a touch but the ball could go land anywhere, but fortunately for the visitors it bounces to safety.
(36’) Conte demonstrates on the sideline as Hazard goes down under contact from Ward. It's the correct decision from the referee not to award the free-kick, but he makes himself an unpopular figure by then giving a foul against Alonso.
(34’) A rare mistake from Hennessey thus far as he slices his clearance into touch under no pressure from the home side.
(32’) SHOT! Luiz takes the strike on this time and he fires his effort over the wall, but straight into the arms of Hennessey.
(32’) Costa is caught on the edge of the box by Puncheon and the Blues are awarded a free-kick in dangerous position.
(31’) Chelsea are probing away on the edge of the box, but the Palace backline are holding firm for now. The Blues' intricate passes are just not clicking at the moment.
(29’) Milivojevic clips the ankles of Hazard in the centre circle and he just avoids a booking from referee Pawson.
(27’) CHANCE! Another opening for Palace on the break as Cabaye tees up Puncheon to strike from 25 yards. He gets decent contact on the ball, sending his effort just wide of the target.
(26’) Cabaye gives the ball away inside his own box, but Chelsea cannot organise themselves in time to capitalise. Kante sends a deep cross for Alonso to attack at the back post, only for the Spaniard to head behind.
(25’) Hazard turns his man inside and out once again down the right flank before firing a low ball into the box, but on this occasion Tomkins clears away under little pressure.
(24’) CHANCE! Palace continue to look dangerous on the counter and Schlupp has an opening as a loose ball finds its way to him on the edge of the box. However, he gets his strike all wrong, tamely firing wide of the post.
(23’) SAVE! Hazard twists and turns his way past three Palace defenders before sending a low cross into the box. Costa latches on to the ball and strikes a low volley towards goal, but Hennessey reacts to make a brilliant stop on the line.
(22’) Hazard swings the ball in and Palace are all at sea at the back. The ball pinballs around the box, but it fails to fall for a blue shirt before the visitors clear the danger.
(21’) Pedro continues to be in the wars as Townsend simply blocks his progress down the right flank. Chelsea win a free-kick in a decent position.
(19’) WIDE! Hazard collects on the edge of the box and goes for the strike, but he slices his effort well wide of the post.
(18’) Pedro was down for some time receiving treatment as he put his body on the line to strike his effort at goal and was caught in the aftermath. However, he appears to be ok to continue this afternoon.
(17’) Replays show that the ball did hit Townsend in the arm. Palace have gotten away with one there.
(16’) PENALTY SHOUT! Chelsea win a corner down the right as Sakho clears behind. From the resulting set-piece Hazard plays the ball short to Pedro, who strikes with power. Only a block from Townsend stops the ball from reaching the net, and the home side go up for a penalty, but the referee dismisses their claims.
(15’) Chelsea are having to battle here as they're not having everything their own way. Palace have come here with a good attitude and are putting the home side under pressure.
(13’) Pedro makes a surge down the right, but as he looks up to cross the ball he loses possession, allowing the visitors to clear the danger.
--- 11’ Goal! GOALLLL!!!! PALACE TAKE THE LEAD! Incredible scenes at Stamford Bridge as Palace forge ahead. Benteke leads a break through the middle of the Chelsea backline before playing a one-two with Zaha. He collects again in the box before displaying composure to dummy his first effort before lifting the ball over Courtois with a neat chip. A sublime effort. ---
--- 11’ Assist Zaha makes another impact in the final third as he tees up Benteke for his strike with a calm pass. ---
--- 9’ Assist Benteke plays a simple pass into the feet of Zaha and is rewarded with an assist as the winger finds the net. ---
(9’) Pedro does well to cover ground at the back as Townsend threatens down the left, making a fine sliding tackle to prevent the cross.
--- 9’ Goal! GOALLLL!!!! ZAHA EQUALISES! Out of nothing Palace are back in the game as Zaha collects a low pass on the edge of the box and somehow manages to squeeze his effort between Alonso's legs and into the bottom corner. ---
(7’) Townsend tries to create space down the left flank and he whips the ball into the area, only for his cross to dip behind for a goal-kick.
--- 5’ Assist Hazard bamboozles Ward with his skill on the left flank before delivering a fine low cross, which allows Hazard to convert. ---
--- 5’ Goal! GOALLLL!!! FABREGAS STRIKES! The Spaniard starts an ends the move as he picks out Hazard on the left to open up Palace before converting the Belgian's cross at the near post. Hazard did brilliantly to square Ward up on the left to send a low ball into the area and Fabregas continued his run to steer his effort into the net with the aid of the post. ---

(3’) Milivojevic brings down Fabregas 25 yards from goal with a late challenge. Chelsea have a free-kick in a dangerous position, with Luiz standing over the ball.

Miguel Britos' first goal for Watford gives them a first victory in five attempts and moves the Hornets up to 10th in the Premier League table. However, Sunderland remain seven points from safety at the bottom after yet another defeat.
FULL-TIME: WATFORD 1-0 SUNDERLAND
(90’) Khazri sends the delivery straight into the wall and Mr Probert swiftly blows for full-time!
(90’) Free-kick to Sunderland! Cleverley brings down Khazri 30 yards from goal and the visitors have one final opportunity...
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Capoue is shown a yellow card for bringing down Oviedo. Sunderland have 60 seconds!... ---
(90’) FOUR MINUTES! That is how many minutes of added time that Sunderland have to find an equaliser here. However, O'Shea has just conceded a free-kick inside his own half and Watford will certainly take their time now...
(89’) Watford deal with the delivery and, after Borini pumps the ball back into the box, Gomes gratefully gathers from the air. Ironically, the Watford keeper was on the bench for Tottenham when the Italian made his Premier League debut for Chelsea back in September 2009.
(88’) The Black Cats have really come to life over these past few minutes and looking a lot more menacing. They are awarded another free-kick and Khazri is standing over the ball...
--- 87’ Substitution Niang is given a breather after an impressive display and replaced by Juan Zuniga, who comes on for his first appearance since January 14. ---
(85’) The Italian, who has only scored once this season, has admitted that his form had dipped this season after being instructed to play as a utility man during the campaign. However, he has looked very lively over these past few minutes.
(83’) GOOD SAVE! That was better by the Black Cats as Borini finds some space and lets fly from outside the box, but Gomes springs to his left and palms the effort away.
(82’) Sunderland have spent 138 days at the bottom of the Premier League table this season and, barring a miraculous change of fortune, it looks increasingly like that will continue here.
(80’) Defoe has barely had a sight at goal all game and looks to get in behind the Watford defence. However, Gomes is quickly out to gather, although the offside flag had already been raised.
--- 78’ Yellow card Niang shows good strength to outmuscle Kone, who prevents the Milan loanee from advancing any further and is the next Sunderland player into the book. ---
--- 77’ Yellow card Khazri demonstrates his frustration a little too aggressively towards the linesman after a decision goes against him, and he is rightly booked by the referee. ---
(74’) We are approaching the final quarter of an hour at Vicarage Road where, if they hold on, Watford will equal their best tally of home wins in a Premier League season with a sixth success.
--- 72’ Yellow card Jones is shown the first yellow card of the game by the referee. Ironically, the right-back, who turned 30 during the international break, scored against Watford for Preston North End back in October 2008. ---
(72’) Having played such a key role in Sunderland's survival last season, Khazri is making his 12th appearance as a substitute of this campaign having started just four times. The president of the Tunisian Football Federation blocked his call-up to the national side because of a "poor attitude" last week, but he will want to let his football do the talking for the rest of the term.
--- 70’ Substitution The Sunderland fans cheer as Moyes turns to Wahbi Khazri for the final 20 minutes. Januzaj is the player to make way. ---
(68’) GREAT EFFORT! Holebas receives the ball after a Watford attack is initially dealt with. The left-back lets fly from 25 yards out and his effort is just over the bar with Pickford beaten.
(67’) That really was the finish of a player low on confidence in front of goal. In fact, since arriving on loan from Manchester United, Januzaj has only found the net once and that was back in August against Shrewsbury Town in the EFL Cup.
(65’) POOR SHOT! N'Dong has looked lively since his introduction four minutes ago. The Gabon international shows great awareness to pick out Januzaj on the edge of the box, but the Belgian's effort is tame and straight at Gomes.
(62’) GOOD SAVE! Watford threaten to double their lead as Success is released through the middle. However, Pickford is quickly out of goal to make an important block, before Doucoure's follow-up is deflected behind for a corner.
--- 61’ Substitution Moyes looks straight to the bench and Gibson is withdrawn to be replaced by Didier N'Dong. ---
(61’) That was Britos' first goal for Watford and it could prove to be a very important one in the context of their season. It is also the first time that the Uruguayan has found the net for over two years.
--- 59’ Assist Cathcart showed great awareness to pick out Britos at the far post. ---
--- 59’ Goal! WATFORD TAKE THE LEAD!!! Britos breaks the deadlock! Cleverley's corner is met by Okaka, whose deflected header crashes against the bar. Cathcart then heads the ball towards the far post, where Britos nods home to put the hosts in front! ---
(57’) Holebas embarks on a strong run down the left and cuts inside before trying his luck from quite a way out. However, the Greek's right-footed effort drifts aimlessly wide of the post.
(55’) Success arrived from Granada for £12.5 million at the start of this season, but has only found the net once in 14 appearances so far. However, having made his Nigeria debut against Senegal last week, will be buoyed and hopeful of scoring his first goal since October.
--- 53’ Substitution Amrabat has lasted 53 minutes on his first Premier League start for over two months. However, the Moroccan appears very unhappy as he is replaced by record signing Isaac Success, who makes his 14th appearance as a substitute this season. ---
(51’) The seventh-highest goalscorer in Premier League history with 157 to his name, Defoe has netted 14 times from 22 shots on target for Sunderland this season, and his endless threat will be highly important over these final 10 games in the Black Cats' bid for survival.
(49’) Defoe, who scored on his England return after four years away from the international scene last week, is yet to find the net against Watford in the Premier League. Although, he seems determined to do so after hobbling to the touchline before soon getting back onto the pitch.
(47’) WORRY! Defoe goes down clutching his leg following a fairly innocuous challenge with Doucoure. He and Sunderland will be desperately hoping that it is nothing serious and that the England striker is able to continue.
(46’) KICK-OFF! The referee blows his whistle and Watford get the ball rolling once more.
The teams are back out on the field and the second half is imminent...
Sunderland have now gone seven hours without finding the net in the Premier League, although Moyes will be happy to be going in at half-time with the score at 0-0. Both sides have looked good going forward, but you feel that the deadlock being broken after the break would see the contest truly burst into life.
HALF-TIME: WATFORD 0-0 SUNDERLAND
(45’) And, with that, Mr Probert blows the whistle for half-time!
(45’) Britos' last goal came against Juventus for Napoli in January 2015. The Uruguayan looks to end that spell by poking the ball towards the target after being found by Amrabat, but his effort is tame and easily gathered by Pickford.
(45’) There will be two minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half and now would be such a great time for either side to break the deadlock.
(44’) GOOD SAVE! Watford deal with Sunderland's corner and launch a very dangerous counter-attack, from which an unmarked Niang is found just outside the penalty area. He lets fly with his left foot, but Pickford gets down well to block.
(43’) NERVY! Januzaj's shot from outside the area takes a deflection off Cathcart, and a wrong-footed Gomes has to quickly scramble across to watch the ball drift just wide of the post.
--- 42’ Substitution Kaboul hobbles off to be replaced by former Newcastle United defender Daryl Janmaat, who is greeted by boos from the Sunderland supporters. ---
(41’) The Frenchman was in tears when Sunderland secured their survival at the end of last season, although he will want to cry for very different reasons after pulling up suddenly there.
(39’) OUCH! Kaboul suddenly pulls up clutching his hamstring and the medical team are immediately on the pitch to tend to him. However, it appears more than likely that the former Sunderland man will be departing earlier than planned against his former club.
(37’) The former Tottenham man made a very impressive scoring start to the season - netting four times in Watford's opening five matches. However, he has only managed one goal in his 23 appearances since then, which came against Leicester City back in November.
(35’) JUST WIDE! Capoue and Okaka combine down the left before the former lets fly with a powerful shot from just outside the area that flashes past the far post.
(32’) There was uncertainty as to whether O'Shea would play today after suffering the effects of that shocking challenge from Gareth Bale on international duty last week. However, he has shaken off the knock and his presence is important as he makes a well-timed challenge in the area to deny Okaka from getting in behind.
(30’) The 22-year-old, who is on loan here since arriving from AC Milan in January, said in the week that he will "work like a dog" to ensure a return to his highest performance levels, which saw him attract interest from the likes of Juventus, Manchester City and Tottenham Hotspur during his youth career at Caen.
(28’) GREAT RUN! Niang picks up the ball inside his own half and shows great footwork as he embarks on a strong venture deep into Sunderland territory. However, his threat is eventually snuffed out by the visitors, who gather in numbers to deal with the situation.
(26’) Watford work a short corner well before delivering the ball to the far post, where Kaboul climbs highest but is unable to direct it towards goal and Sunderland clear the danger.
(24’) Each of the last three meetings between the two sides at Vicarage Road have ended in draws and today's match appears to be following that trend so far, with neither side really dominating proceedings.
(22’) Sunderland snuff out the danger following a Watford corner and play some neat football inside their opponents' half. However, it all counts for nothing as Denayer overhits an attempted diagonal ball which goes aimlessly behind for a goal-kick.
(20’) FREE HEADER! Okaka should have put Watford in front there! He stole a yard on his marker to meet Capoue's inviting cross, but was unable to test Pickford and find the net for the second game running at Vicarage Road.
(18’) The Italian striker is only making only his sixth start of the season today with Deeney dropping to the bench, and that was good, positive play that will have pleased his manager.
(16’) Okaka receives the ball just inside the Sunderland half and takes on O'Shea and Oviedo, but his touch to get beyond Kone is just too heavy and Pickford is quickly out to gather.
(13’) Only Tom Heaton and Ben Foster have made more saves than Pickford in the Premier League this season. The England under-21 international showed very good reflexes there and showed why he is being tipped for a call-up to the senior team.
(11’) GOOD DOUBLE SAVE! Watford apply the pressure and Pickford does well to get down and beat away Niang's effort from a tight angle, before producing an equally smart save to deny Doucoure's shot shortly afterwards.
(10’) It has been a very open start to this match with both sides looking threatening going forward. This time, Britos is forced to come across and make a vital clearance with Defoe lurking around the penalty area.
(8’) Watford look to catch Sunderland out on the counter attack with Niang leading the charge. However, he is not on the same wavelength as Okaka, who does not read his attempted through ball and Pickford gathers.
(6’) Nothing comes of the corner but they were positive signs from Rodwell. Ironically, his most recent goal came here at Vicarage Road on the final day of last season and the former Manchester City man was not too far away there.
(4’) At the other end, Rodwell embarks on a strong run into the area before his left-footed effort deflects behind off Kaboul for a corner. This is a good early opportunity for the visitors...
(2’) VITAL CLEARANCE! Watford launch the first meaningful attack of the game with Amrabat's deflected cross looping dangerously towards the far post. However, Jones gets there ahead of Okaka to head to safety and nothing comes from the subsequent corner.
(1’) KICK-OFF! Lee Probert is our referee today and it is his first Premier League appointment since May 2015. He blows his whistle and Sunderland get the match underway.
HERE THEY COME! The teams are making their way out onto the field and kick-off is just moments away...
SUNDERLAND SUBS: Mannone, Djilobodji, Cattermole, Larsson, Khazri, N'Dong, Manquilo.
SUNDERLAND (5-3-2): Pickford; Jones, Kone, O'Shea, Denayer, Oviedo; Gibson, Januzaj, Rodwell; Borini, Defoe.
In the week that it was announced that David Moyes would remain in charge of Sunderland even if they are relegated at the end of the season, he makes just a single change from the 0-0 draw with Burnley. Lamine Kone returns from a knee injury to form part of a five-man defence alongside John O'Shea, who has shaken off a leg injury to captain the side. Sebastian Larsson makes way and is joined on the bench by Lee Cattermole, who is back in the squad following a six-month absence with hip and back injuries.
WATFORD SUBS: Pantilimon, Prodl, Mariappa, Deeney, Success, Zuniga, Janmaat.
WATFORD (3-4-2-1): Gomes (c); Cathcart, Kaboul, Britos; Amrabat, Doucoure, Cleverley, Holebas; Capoue, Niang; Okaka.
Walter Mazzarri makes four changes to the Watford side that were beaten 1-0 at Crystal Palace before the international break. Heurelho Gomes captains the side as Troy Deeney drops to the bench with illness, as does Sebastian Prodl after suffering a calf problem. Jose Holebas, Abdoulaye Doucoure, Nordin Amrabat and Stefano Okaka all return to the starting 11 alongside Tom Cleverley, who will join the Hornets from Everton on a permanent deal at the end of the season. Younes Kaboul faces his former club.
It may be April Fool's Day but only the winners will be laughing today as Watford aim to move further clear of the relegation zone, while bottom club Sunderland are desperate to move to within four points of safety and boost their survival chances.
