For the Gunners matters get worse on the pitch. They were embarrassing defending set-piece this afternoon and were duly put to the sword by Dawson. The pressure on Wenger grows, with the banners out in full force at the end of the match in the away end. They now face a serious battle to clinch a top-four place.
West Brom record their second home win on the bounce over Arsenal as second-half strikes from Hal Robson-Kanu and Craig Dawson's second of the game see them past Arsene Wenger's men. The result ends a run of back-to-back defeats for the Baggies, who will be aiming to consolidate eighth place in the Premier League.
FULL-TIME: WEST BROM 3-1 ARSENAL
(90’) The referee ends the match.
(90’) Field collects a ball over the top and heads to the corner to take time off the clock. The game is almost won for the Baggies.
(90’) A late chance for Arsenal to reduce the deficit is wasted as Xhaka sends his corner over the heads of everyone in the box and the follow-up cross from Iwobi is cleared.
(90’) There will be three minutes of added time.
--- 90’ Substitution Field replaces Chadli for the home side. ---
(89’) The banners are out in the away end against Wenger 'enough is enough' is one message.
(88’) Ramsey tries an ambitious effort from the edge of the box, but he hammers his effort straight of Livermore's legs and the attack peters out.
(86’) Xhaka makes an important clearing header at the back to steer Fletcher's cross away from Robson-Kanu. Arsenal have to be careful otherwise this could get out of hand.
(84’) West Brom are not giving up there hunt for more goals with McClean sending a dangerous cross to the near post. Mustafi clears, but Nyom picks the ball up on the left flank and earns a free-kick from Ramsey's challenge.
(83’) Oxlade-Chamberlain sums up his side's afternoon with a pass that misses every yellow shirt in the final third and heads out for a throw-in. Head down and a shake after the fact - the body language has not been good from the Gunners in the second half.
(80’) Giroud goes to ground in the box and there are mild claims for a penalty, but the Frenchman does not lead them.
--- 78’ Substitution Sanchez has not been the same player in the second half and makes way for Iwobi. ---
(77’) Arsenal have it all to do now. They came back late against Bournemouth earlier in the season, but have looked completely void of ideas in the second half over how to break the Baggies down.
--- 75’ Assist McClean's delivery is on the spot and allows Dawson to head home from clos range. ---
--- 75’ Goal! GOALLLLLL!!!! DAWSON NOTCHES A BRACE! West Brom take a huge stride towards victory with Dawson scoring his second of the game with a bullet header from close range. It's poor defending from the Gunners once again, allowing the defender a free run to meet McClean's corner and hand his side a two-goal cushion. ---
(73’) Sanchez lifts a threatening cross over the West Brom backline and it almost lands for Giroud, but it just sails over his head and into the hands of Foster.
--- 72’ Substitution Yacob replaces Brunt as Pulis bolster the defensive areas of his midfield. ---
(70’) BLOCK! Xhaka takes the set-piece, but he curls his effort straight into the wall and the Baggies boot the ball away. A disappointing effort from the Arsenal midfielder.
(69’) Welbeck is clipped by Brunt on the edge of the box and the Gunners have an excellent opportunity to threaten from the resulting free-kick. Xhaka stands over the ball on the right side of the pitch.
(67’) CHANCES! Robson-Kanu breaks in behind the Arsenal defence and only has Ospina to beat, but the keeper makes a fine save to smother his shot. Chadli gathers the rebound and rounds the keeper, only for Mustafi to get back and clear his effort away from goal. Finally, Brunt collects on the edge of the box, but he hammers his strike over the bar.
--- 65’ Substitution Giroud replaces Walcott for the visitors. ---
(65’) OFF THE BAR! Arsenal win a corner down the right flank and Xhaka launches a quality ball deep to the back post. Welbeck meets it with a thumping header, only to seee his effort crash off the bar before the home side clear the danger.
(63’) Arsenal probe the edge of the box, but are not gaining the success they experienced in the first half with their short-range passes.
(61’) The Gunners are looking short of ideas at the moment, with a lack of inspiration emerging from the middle of the park. Changes could be needed from Wenger to spark his team into life.
(59’) Mustafi floats a long ball forward and he gets too much on it to find a team-mate. However, it does cause Foster issues as it heads towards goal, but fortunately for West Brom it lands on the roof of the net.
(57’) Once again Arsenal are suspect at the back and the Baggies are in control of the contest now. Monreal was leading the complaints about the goal, but it's hard to see what he was complaining about.
--- 55’ Goal! GOALLL!!! ROBSON-KANU MAKES AN IMMEDIATE IMPACT! The Wales international scores almost with his first touch as he capitalises on a horrendous error from Ospina to slide the ball into the net. McClean's run in behind caused issues forcing the Arsenal keeper to slide and palm Chadli's ball away from goal. Unfortunately for him it went straight to Robson-Kanu, who slotted the ball into the net, with McClean leaping over it as it passed under him. ---
--- 54’ Substitution Curious change for the Baggies as Rondon is withdrawn. He goes straight down the tunnel after being replaced by Robson-Kanu - either the forward is not happy about the change or he's injured. Could well be the latter there. ---
(53’) The Gunners waste a chance to send the ball into the box as Xhaka's first delivery fails to beat the first man, while he is caught offside before he can send a second ball into the box.
(51’) CHANCE! Rondon almost caps a fine counter from the home side that he initially lead with a goal. He battles Monreal to send the ball out wide before continuing his run into the box. Brunt sends a pinpoint ball in for the striker to attack, but he sends his glancing header inches past the post.
(50’) Arsenal probe the edge of the box, but the Baggies throw men in at the ball to stifle any potential shooting chances as Sanchez and Walcott are both denied.
(48’) Role reversal between Dawson and Sanchez as the Arsenal man brings down the defender to give away a free-kick.
(46’) Fletcher is on hand to make an important clearance for the Baggies at the back to steer the ball away from the advancing Walcott in the box.

Arsene Wenger will be satisfied with his side's performance, although their defending for Dawson's header will have frustrated the Frenchman. Their response was empathic to level through Sanchez almost immediately, and since then Theo Walcott and Aaron Ramsey have gone close to handing the visitors the lead.
It's level at the break at The Hawthorns as Alexis Sanchez cancelled out Craig Dawson's opener for West Brom. Arsenal may have just shaded the first half on the balance of play, but the Baggies have been a threat on the break throughout the opening 45 minutes.
HALF-TIME: WEST BROM 1-1 ARSENAL

(36’) Trouble for Cech as he pulls up attempting to clear the ball downfield. It looks as though he may be forced off here.
(35’) CLOSE! Arsenal fails to thoroughly clear their lines from a throw-in and the loose ball is gathered by the Baggies. Dawson sends a teasing cross to the back post, but McClean and Brunt do not gamble, allowing it to trickle out for a goal-kick.
(34’) CHANCE! Fletcher drifts into space in the box and collects Livermore's throughball. He hammers an effort on the half-volley at goal, but Cech makes a brilliant save to turn it past the post.

(31’) CHANCE! West Brom go back to front within seconds as Dawson finds Chadli, who bursts down the flank. He slides a pass for Rondon's run into the right inside channel and the forward takes on the shot, only to pull his strike just wide of the post.
(28’) Rondon bodychecks Sanchez as he brings the ball away and the Chilean adds some theatrics after his falls. He does not seem happy with the ferocity of West Brom's challenges this afternoon.
(27’) McClean sends the ball into a dangerous area, but no player in a blue and white shirt can make solid contact, allowing the Gunners to clear.
(26’) The Baggies break the shackles of Arsenal pressure and win a corner down the right that will be delivered by McClean.
(25’) Arsenal build well in the final third, but the referee does not appreciate Welbeck's attempts to win a free-kick as he goes down under Dawson's challenge.
(23’) Sanchez almost carves out space for himself in the final third and an attempted offload to Bellerin, but he gets brought to the ground by Livermore. The forward is not awarded a free-kick and is far from happy with Swarbrick.
(21’) Brave defending from Nyom as he defends the back post well from Bellerin's presence after Ramsey sent a dangerous cross towards the Spaniard.
(19’) Sanchez beats McAuley with a neat turn, only for the defender to pull him back. However, the Northern Irishman is not booked by referee Swarbrick.
(17’) All the momentum was with the Baggies after Dawson's opener, but the equaliser appears to have taken the wind out of their sails and that of the home supporters.

--- 15’ Goal! GOALLLL!!! SANCHEZ EQUALISES! Arsenal level almost immediately as Sanchez is left unmarked in the box and Xhaka picks him out with a lofted pass. He takes a touch to get the ball out of his feet before hammering a right-footed into the net off the underside of the bar. ---
--- 12’ Assist Chadli fires the ball into the box and Dawson converts from close range. ---
--- 12’ Goal! GOALLLLL!!! WEST BROM TAKE THE LEAD! The Baggies have been a threat all season from set-pieces and go ahead from a corner as Chadli swings the ball into the box and Dawson heads home from close range. It was too easy for the defender as he stole a march on Koscielny to convert. ---
(12’) SHOT! Brunt sends McClean into the left inside channel and the winger goes for the blast towards the near post, but Cech beats his effort behind for a corner.
(10’) An even contest thus far, with both teams enjoying decent spells of possession in the final third and openings to threaten the back of the net.
(8’) Chadli swings a cross to the back post and McClean is able to get up above Bellerin to head at goal, but his effort is tame and straight at Cech.

(5’) CLOSE! Nyom skips through the Arsenal defence down the left flank and fires a great ball across the face of goal, but Rondon is on his heels and is not on the spot to convert the opening.

FULL-TIME! Man United take home three points, courtesy of a hard-fought 3-1 win over Boro. Rashford could have scored twice before Fellaini nodded home the opener, before Lingard smashed home brilliantly to make it two. Gestede made things interesting with a late consolation, before a slip from Valdes gifted Valencia the chance to secure the victory and move the away side temporarily into fifth. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
--- 90’ +4 Substitution Rashford is replaced by Darmian late on, as Mourinho looks to wind down the clock further. ---
--- 90’ +3 Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! VALENCIA MAKES IT 3-1! Valdes slips and gifts the away side the security that they were after. A back pass into the Spanish goalkeeper is easily controlled, but the former Barcelona shot-stopper loses his footing and allows the Ecuadorian winger to run the ball into an unguarded net. ---
(90’) The referee is forced to speak with both Bailly and Gibson, after a coming together between Gestede and the Ivorian defender. Eventually, a free-kick is swung in from deep on the right-hand side, with Smalling required to nod a defensive header behind for a corner.
(90’) There are four minutes of stoppage time at the Riverside.
(89’) Fabio clips a long ball forward which is flicked on by Gestede, but Man United mop up. They are essentially playing a back six at this point. Negredo tries an acrobatic effort after a good flick-on from Gestede, but the Spaniard's connection with the ball isn't quite right and he fails to test De Gea.
(87’) Carrick gets on the ball and slows the tempo right down, as Man United try to manage the dying minutes at the Riverside with care. Boro are throwing plenty of bodies forward now. Negredo battles beyond one challenge and gets into the penalty box, but a last-ditch sliding tackle from Jones comes at just the right time to deny the former Valencia striker.
(85’) Clayton tries to release Adama Traore into the right channel, but the pass isn't executed well at all and heads behind for a goal-kick. De Gea is happy to take his time over his kick. Only five minutes stand between Man United and a hard-fought three points.
(83’) Clayton lifts a cross into the box from the right-hand side, but Bailly and Carrick do just enough to half-clear and then earn a free-kick for the visitors. Boro are trying to ramp up the pressure and squeeze an equaliser out of this game, but Man United are trying every trick in the box to slow proceedings down.
(81’) Agnew's changes have given Boro a fighting chance of getting a share of the spoils in this contest, with Man United having a little less than 10 minutes to try and see out. Downing and Adama Traore are willing to pump plenty of deliveries into the box, with Gestede providing an extra bit of presence to challenge aerially.
--- 80’ Substitution Lingard goes off with a knock, with Martial coming into the game for the dying stages. ---
(79’) Downing bends in yet another inviting cross in from the left-hand side, but yet again Negredo is unable to get near it. Lingard goes down with a knock, but the goalscorer may well be looking to slow things down a little. Martial is readied as a replacement.
--- 77’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! GESTEDE MAKES IT 2-1! Adama Traore lifts in a cross towards Negredo, but the danger doesn't disappear despite the Spaniard not getting on the end of it. Man United fail to clear their lines through Smalling, with Gestede stroking home a close-range finish! ---
(75’) A cross from the left-hand side is missed by Gestede, but Negredo is unable to steal in at the back post to stab home a close-range finish. The Spaniard didn't appear to anticipate that his teammate wouldn't be able to rise to meet the Downing delivery.
(73’) Adama Traore breaks beyond Fellaini and to the right byline, but a back-post cross isn't turned goalwards by Negredo. The Spanish substitute just wants to drive at his man, and he has got targets in the box to aim for. Man United are settling in for a conservative last quarter of an hour.
(71’) Boro now have both Negredo and Gestede to aim for up top, with Downing and Adama Traore looking to give them ammunition from the flanks. Jones is forced to nod a dangerous cross from the left to safety, with the hosts turning the screw a little bit now.
--- 69’ Substitution Rojo is given the last 20 minutes, with Mata jogging off. Mourinho isn't taking any chance. ---
--- 68’ Substitution Ramirez is replaced by Traore for the last 20 minutes or so, as Agnew rolls the dice. ---
--- 67’ Substitution Leadbitter is replaced by Gestede, with Boro pushing an extra man up top now. ---
(67’) Negredo is picked out by a good cross from the left by Ramirez, but the ex-Manchester City striker can only stoop to nod a header wide of the far post. The Spaniard should have perhaps worked De Gea there.
(66’) Lingard strolls through the heart of the Boro midfield, as Man United continue to break with intent, but a pass into Rashford is cut out by Bernardo. One more goal would whack cruise control on for the visitors.
(64’) Boro have it all to do now, with that goal probably going some way to kill the contest off. Lingard has been electric on the counter and finally has his goal. Negredo is picked out by a cross from the right by Barragan, but the Spaniard's tame header is caught simply by De Gea.
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! LINGARD MAKES IT TWO! Bailly heads clear to deny a lofted throughball from bouncing into the path of De Roon, as Man United continue to defend well. Lingard leads a charge for the visitors, before cutting onto his right foot and slamming a brilliant finish into the top-right corner from around 20 yards out. ---
--- 62’ Assist Mata releases Lingard forward on the break, and Boro give the Englishman far too much space to pick his shot. ---
(61’) Ramirez is picked out on the edge of the penalty area for Boro, but Valencia tracks back well to recover and rob the Uruguayan of possession. The hosts enjoy a lengthy spell on the ball, but they're not shifting play quickly enough to ask questions of Man United's back five.
(59’) Carrick releases Lingard down the left, but the wind takes the ball curling out of play. Boro have half an hour to get back into this game, but De Gea has had almost nothing to do since the start of the second half. Everything is just a few seconds too slow from Agnew's men.
(57’) Young tries to drill in a low cross from the left-hand side, but Gibson scrambles the ball clear. Man United continue to find gaps, but Rashford has been very wasteful. The youngster takes aim from a tight angle on the right, but he blasts horribly over the crossbar.
(55’) Fellaini manages to slide a pass through Boro's lines, with Lingard opening his legs up on the break. He puts a throughball into the path of Rashford, who coasts past Bernardo yet again, but the Englishman is unable to work a shooting angle for himself.
(53’) Lingard goes down with a knock after being blocked off slightly by De Roon, but the England international is back to his feet quickly. Man United continue to offer a threat when they get forward at pace, but Boro are doing no such thing. Negredo doesn't have any support at all. The Spaniard is picked out by a cross from the left-hand side, but Young does just enough to flick the ball clear.
(51’) Valencia drives to the right byline and Gibson does brilliantly to slide in and deny the Ecuadorian winger without conceding a corner. Man United have retained the ball quite well since the restart, with Boro struggling to build up a head of steam.
(49’) Fellaini heads a dangerous corner delivery away for the visitors, before Fabio gets a warning for diving into an unnecessary tackle on Valencia to deny a counter-attack. Somehow the ex-Man United full-back avoids a booking for his troubles.
(48’) Negredo flicks a ball over the top, which Smalling makes a complete mess of by mistiming his header, but the Man United centre-back is fortunate to see De Gea hurry out to take control of the situation. Boro threaten down the left, but a terrible pass from Fabio is intercepted by Bailly.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Riverside! Man United have a narrow advantage, but due to their own wastefulness in front of goal Agnew's men are still in with a chance. All to play for over the next 45 minutes.
HALF-TIME! Fellaini's header is the only difference between these two sides, with Man United left wondering how they aren't home and dry already. Rashford has squandered two great chances, but Boro have barely mustered a save out of De Gea. Mourinho will want his team to go on and kill this contest as quickly as possible.
(45’) Rashford cuts in from the left before trying to play a little backheel through to Mata, but the Englishman's creativity doesn't translate into reality well. There is one minute of stoppage time.
(43’) Man United are happy to sit back and bide their time until the interval, with Rashford left to chase lost causes as a pacey outlet up top. Boro win a corner on the left-hand side, but Smalling is pushed and wins his team a free-kick to alleviate the pressure completely.
(41’) De Gea has had a couple of saves to make, but largely the Spaniard hasn't been called into action. Agnew will be pleased that Boro have got their foot on the ball and taken the game to their opponents, but they've not managed to cause problems in dangerous areas of the field. Mourinho's system hasn't been tested.
(39’) Fellaini almost tests his own goalkeeper, after a low cross cannons off the Belgian goalscorer and loops over the crossbar, but the resulting corner comes to absolutely nothing. Boro are putting pressure on and appear confident to carry possession, but it isn't quite clicking when they get into the final third. This contest isn't beyond them yet, however.
(37’) Leadbitter finds Ramirez on the edge of the box, with the Uruguayan immediately flicking a pass around the corner to the onrushing De Roon. The Belgian cuts a ball back square from the left, but Negredo is unable to gamble on it and Jones does just enough to usher the cross clear.
(35’) Smalling is picked out by a back-post corner delivery, but the former Fulham defender can only rise to nod a firm header some way wide of the target. With only about 10 minutes left in this first half, Man United are cruising to three points as it stands.
--- 33’ Yellow card Boro earn themselves their first yellow card of the afternoon, with Clayton penalised for a foul in the midfield third. ---
(32’) Mourinho's men deserve this lead, but they should truly be three or four to the good by now. The hosts' marking was very poor there, but the away fans don't mind. Barragan feeds a low pass into Negredo, but the latter can't spin and shoot. Moments later, Fabio swings in a cross, but Negredo can only glance a header back across goal and wide of the target.
--- 30’ Assist Young checks back onto his right foot from the left-hand side and dips an inviting ball over Fabio and to the back post. ---
--- 30’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! FELLAINI MAKES IT 1-0! The Belgium international is picked out by a great cross from the left-hand side and pulls off Fabio well. He nods a firm header into the back of the net and Agnew will be wondering how much more poor defending Boro can offer in this first half. ---
(29’) Bailly invites Valencia to the right byline, but a drilled cross skips through the Boro six-yard box and to safety. Man United could go on to rue missed chances if they can't take the lead before the break. Mourinho's men should be out of sight already, with the hosts leaking chances.
(28’) Man United link up beautifully in midfield, with Mata opening play out to Valencia brilliantly on the right-hand side. The former Wigan wide man drills a low cross into a dangerous area, but nobody is on hand to gamble and get deep into the opposition box. Boro go down the other end, but Bailly manages to outmuscle Ramirez just when the Uruguay international was trying to work a shooting angle.
(26’) Leadbitter bends in a cross from the deep on the right-hand side, but Fellaini rises well to head half-clear. Downing picks up the rebound and attempts to find De Roon lurking at the back post, but the English winger's delivery sails straight behind for a goal-kick. Boro haven't shown any cutting edge yet.
--- 25’ Yellow card Jones is penalised for clash with Negredo, with the England international blocking the ex-Valencia striker off blatantly. That's worth a booking, in the referee's eyes. ---
(24’) DOUBLE SAVE FROM VALDES! Firstly, the ex-Barcelona makes a brilliant stop to deny Rashford from close range, after a great cross from the left by Mata. He sticks out a foot to make an initial save, before scampering to cover his post to parry a second quick-fire effort. Rashford could have had two goals already this afternoon.
(22’) Lingard wins yet another corner for the away side, with Rashford's pace causing real problems when he is able to escape into the left channel. This time, the set-piece delivery is a little more inviting, but Negredo lashes clear at the near post. Man United are managing to show a bit of a threat on the counter, after a slow start.
(20’) De Roon tries to play Fabio in on the overlap, but Smalling covers across well to defuse the situation. Negredo hasn't been getting much service, with Man United keen to slow the contest down due to how Boro have started. Rashford drives to the left byline and cuts a pass back into the path of Lingard, but Barragan makes a good interception that concedes a corner - but Fellaini heads it wide.
(18’) Boro are continuing to dominate, with Leadbitter providing quite a bit of energy in the middle of the park so far. Mata opens plays the ball out to Lingard, who jinks in from the left wing and sees a shot charged down easily. Clear-cut chances have been rather hard to come by in this congested battle.
(16’) Bailly and Valencia try to play a one-two down the right, with the Ecuadorian wing-back doing brilliantly to catch up with a terrible pass and whip in a cross. Rashford can't get near it, however, as Man United are struggling to get options up in support of their attacks when one of their wide players makes a quick burst upfield.
(14’) Boro's first corner of the match sails harmlessly over the danger zone, with Ramirez's delivery being a real waste after his great work to win it initially. The visitors are struggling to get out of their own half, with Rashford rather isolated up top at present. Mourinho will want the likes of Carrick and Fellaini to try and grab this game by the scruff of the neck.
(12’) Fabio, Ramirez and De Roon play neat triangles down the left-hand side, but a final ball from the Boro left-back slides straight behind for a goal-kick. The hosts are combining well and look bright in midfield. They are dominating the ball early on, with Ramirez the first man to test De Gea. The ex-Hull forward forces his opponent to palm a powerful shot behind for a corner.
(10’) Leadbitter curls a cross in from deep on the left-hand side, but Jones heads half-clear. The Boro captain picks up the loose ball and has a go from long range, but his effort sails harmlessly over the crossbar. Agnew will be pleased with his players' reaction in these opening stages.
(9’) De Roon tries to play a searching ball into the right channel for Negredo to chase, but the two aren't on the same wavelength at all. Boro are looking to be as positive as they can when shifting possession in midfield. It isn't quite clicking yet, but there is some confidence about their play.
(7’) Lingard manages to slot Rashford in behind, with the young Englishman bursting into the penalty area with an injection of space. Victor Valdes is exposed, but the experienced Spanish goalkeeper sprawls low to his left to make a brilliant one-on-one save! That really should have been 1-0 to the away side.
(6’) Man United have been quite subdued so far, with Mourinho's men happy to rush ease their way into this contest slowly. Boro have had a good amount of possession, with it clear that Agnew hasn't made any alterations to the hosts' usual style of play. They'll keep moving the ball around to probe for gaps.
(4’) Ramirez outmuscles Bailly and drives down the left-hand side, but a cross from the Uruguayan is massively overhit and Negredo does well to even keep the ball in play on the far side. Downing whips a delivery in from that flank, with De Roon forcing Smalling to concede a corner.
(3’) A couple of long balls come to nothing in the early exchanges, with Boro keen to clear their lines and ensure that no quick mistakes are made. Given the tiny portion of goals that they've scored this season, they can't afford to go a goal down against a Man United line-up which can revert to a back five if needed.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Riverside! Boro will be hoping to stop the rot after Karanka's decision to leave the club, but starting to gather the required momentum to head towards Premier League survival will be tough against today's visitors.
Man United substitutes: Rojo, Martial, Romero, Mkhitaryan, Shaw, Fosu-Mensah, Darmian.
Man United starting line-up (3-4-3): De Gea; Jones, Smalling, Bailly; Valencia, Fellaini, Carrick, Young; Mata, Rashford, Lingard.
Boro substitutes: Guzan, Stuani, Fry, Guedioura, Gestede, Forshaw, Adama Traore.
Boro starting line-up (4-3-3): Victor Valdes; Barragan, Bernardo, Gibson, Fabio; Leadbitter, Clayton, De Roon; Ramirez, Negredo, Downing.
TEAM NEWS: Jose Mourinho opts for a back three for his Man United side, with the visitors rotating after playing midweek. Phil Jones, Eric Bailly and Chris Smalling are the central defenders, with Antonio Valencia and Ashley Young offering width. Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Ander Herrera are out suspended, with Paul Pogba injured. Marouane Fellaini starts in central midfield, with Jesse Lingard and Juan Mata looking to support Marcus Rashford up front. Anthony Martial is fit enough for the bench.
TEAM NEWS: Bernardo starts at centre-back for Boro, with Fabio continuing in the absence of George Friend at left-back against his former club. Captain Grant Leadbitter is deployed in midfield ahead of Adam Forshaw, with Stewart Downing and Gaston Ramirez flanking Alvaro Negredo up top. Cristhian Stuani, Forshaw and Adama Traore are likely to be the go-to options on the bench to liven things up.
Boro have scored just one goal in their last five Premier League outings, with their lack of firepower causing them huge issues. If the home side want to clamber out of the relegation zone with the two games in hand that they have over 17th-placed Swansea before a ball is kicked today, they'll need back-to-back wins to edge to safety. Things are not looking good at the Riverside.
Hello and welcome to Middlesbrough's first Premier League home game without Aitor Karanka, following the Spaniard's sudden departure earlier in the week. Steve Agnew takes the reins temporarily for the hosts, and he's got quite a test on his hands. Manchester United arrive off the back of a cup defeat against Chelsea and a narrow Europa League victory over Rostov, with bouncing back domestically at the first possible opportunity very much on their agenda.

Goals from Michail Antonio and Andre Ayew almost earned the Hammers a point, but the Cherries scored late in the game to secure the three points.
Josh King's day didn't look to be going too well after his penalty miss in the early stages of the match, but he has notched a hat-trick to guide Bournemouth to their first win in nine Premier League matches, alleviating their relegation worries.
FULL-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 3-2 WEST HAM
(90’) THAT'S IT! Bournemouth win a thriller here.
(90’) The Cherries take the ball into the corner with only seconds remaining in the contest.
(90’) Another cross is pumped long into the box - this time from Lanzini. However, Boruc makes an easy claim at his back post.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Cook is yellow carded for a foul on Carroll. ---
(90’) Carroll wins the header from Randolph's long ball into the box, but he cannot generate any power on his header, allowing Boruc to gather.
(90’) The visitors are throwing everyone forward now in their attempt to salvage a point.
(90’) Ayew gave the ball away in the build-up to Bournemouth's goal, allowing Wilshere to break and then create the situation for King to score.
(90’) There will be five minutes of added time.
--- 90’ Goal! GOALLLLLLLLLL!!! KING HAS HIS HAT-TRICK!!! Bournemouth may have the win sealed here as King pounces on a rebound from Wilshere's saved effort. He keeps his composure from close range, blasting the ball into the net. ---
(88’) PENALTY SHOUT!  Nervy moment for Smith again as he raises his arm when Carroll attempts to cross into the box. It does strike him, but referee Madley dismisses his claims from the visitors.
(86’) SHOT! Arter sees his opportunity from distance and strikes his left-footed effort towards the bottom corner, but it creeps just wide of the post.
--- 85’ Substitution Fraser makes way for Mousset late in the game. ---
--- 85’ Substitution Wilshere replaces Afobe for the home side. ---
--- 83’ Assist Byram makes a smart run before cutting the ball back to Ayew to find the net. ---
--- 83’ Goal! GOALLLL!!!! AYEW LEVELS! West Ham equalise with a fine team goal. Obiang starts the move with a pinpoint throughball to release Byram behind Daniels. The full-back cuts it back for an unmarked Ayew in the middle, who slots his strike into an empty net. ---
(81’) BLOCK! A great intervention at the other end denies West Ham. Cook won't know it but he may have saved his team a goal as he flies to the ball to block Antonio's goalbound effort. That was heading into the bottom corner.
--- 80’ Yellow card Gosling takes out Antonio on the left flank and goes into the book. ---
(79’) BLOCK! West Ham are putting bodies on the line at the back as Kings strikes twice on the edge of the box, but a wall of white prevents him from getting a shot on target.
--- 78’ Substitution Byram replaces Kouyate for the visitors. ---
(77’) PENALTY SHOUT! Carroll wants a penalty as his cross strikes the arm of Daniels, although the defender is extremely close to him. The referee dismisses his claim and the visitors have a corner only.
(75’) CHANCE! Fraser and Smith combine down the right and the defender lifts a good cross to the back post for Afobe to attack, only for the striker to head his effort over the bar.
--- 72’ Yellow card Afobe is booked for his challenge on Randolph. ---
(72’) Fonte plays an awful backpass to Randolph and Afobe almost latches on to it, but the keeper clears his lines. The Cherries striker wipes out the Irishman and the referee awards a free-kick to the visitors.
(71’) Antonio appears to be ok to continue this afternoon - just to tough out the final 19 minutes.
(69’) Antonio slips and hits the deck hard on his shoulder. He clutches his right shoulder as the physio races on to treat him on the pitch.
(68’) CHANCE! Lanzini and Antonio combine in the final third and the latter is able to fire at goal, only to see his effort saved by Boruc low to his left.
(67’) CHANCE! Afobe collects on the edge of the box and does well to carve out space for a strike under pressure from Reid. However, Randolph makes a comfortable save to claim the ball.
--- 66’ Yellow card Pugh goes into the book for a foul on Kouyate. ---
(65’) The Hammers have dominated possession over the last few minutes, although they've done nothing with it. First Cresswell fails to send in a cross, then Antonio sends his behind for a goal-kick.
(62’) West Ham are attempting to gain a foothold in the contest with a period of possession. They need a spark from somewhere.
(60’) Snodgrass is back on the pitch, but Arter is down now. These stoppages are just taking the pace out of the game.
(59’) Seconds after coming on Snodgrass turns his ankle and appears to be in some distress on the byline after challenging Daniels.
--- 58’ Substitution Feghouli has faded since the restart and is replaced by Ayew. ---
--- 58’ Substitution Noble makes way for Snodgrass. ---
(56’) Antonio collects a throw-in in the box and volleys the ball across the face of goal. It strikes Gosling and takes an awkward bounce towards goal, but Smith clears the danger.
(54’) CHANCE! The Cherries break with pace and have numbers on the visitors. Fraser collects Arter's pass and goes for goal, only to see his effort deflected into the hands of Randolph.
(54’) Feghouli makes a weaving run into the box, but a solid challenge from Francis stops him in his tracks.
(52’) King takes whack from Reid and requires treatment on the pitch before we can continue here.
(50’) WIDE! Smith links up with Arter and space opens up through the inside right channel. He strikes from the edge of the box, but sends his effort narrowly wide of the post.
--- 48’ Assist Afobe wins the header from the free-kick, sending the ball into the path of his team-mate. ---
--- 48’ Goal! GOALLLLL!!! BOURNEMOUTH TAKE THE LEAD! King makes full amends for his earlier miss as he converts from close range. Fraser lifted the ball into the box and Afobe headed it into his path. From six yards out he could not miss the target. There was an issue about offside as Madley went to his assistant to confirm, but King was offside in the first phase - but not the second stage of play. ---
(47’) Fraser's pace catches Reid out and it results in a free-kick for the home side - midway through the West Ham half.
(46’) We're back underway at Dean Court.
The players are back out for the second half, so we should be underway again shortly.
There are more goal in this contest for sure - so don't go anywhere!
Josh King has been hero and villain. First missing from 12 yards before notching an equaliser, while Benik Afobe is looking for redemption in the second half after also missing from the spot. Michail Antonio has been excellent in the first period and scored a fine goal, while Sofiane Feghouli has also impressed.
What a crazy game so far! It's level between the teams, which on reflection could be the fair score, although Bournemouth have missed twice from the spot. On the other hand West Ham have missed two good opportunities at the other end - so yes probably a decent reflection of the match.
HALF-TIME: BOURNEMOUTH 1-1 WEST HAM
(45’) The referee ends the first half.
(45’) Lanzini breaks the stalemate between the West Ham attack and the Bournemouth backline by hammering an effort at goal, only to find the stand behind the net.
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time.
(45’) BLOCK! Daniels collects a fine pass from Pugh and he sends a dangerous low ball into the box, but Afobe's shot on the turn is blocked by Reid.
(44’) A rare relative period of calm before the half as the home side enjoy a spell of possession in the middle of the park.
(42’) Antonio attacks the ball from the resulting corner and his header looks to be going goalwards, but it strikes an unaware Cook and is cleared by the home side.
(41’) CHANCE! Feghouli latches on to Kouyate's pass in the inside right channel and has space to fire at goal. It's heading towards the bottom corner, only for Boruc to make a fine stop with his feet.
(40’) Noble releases Antonio down the left and he almost gets the wrong side of Francis, but the defender just does enough to stop his strike.
--- 37’ Missed penalty MISS! INCREDIBLE! Bournemouth miss their second spot-kick of the match as Afobe tamely strikes the ball and it allows Randolph to make a comfortable save. An awful penalty. ---
(37’) Penalty Save Darren Edward Andrew Randolph
(36’) PENALTY TO BOURNEMOUTH! The Cherries have their second penalty of the day as referee Madley points to the spot as Pugh is brought down by Fonte.
(35’) Daniels lifts the resulting free-kick into the box, but it's a disappointing cross from the full-back, sending the ball straight down Randolph's throat.
--- 34’ Yellow card Obiang brings down King for the second time his afternoon and this time he does get booked. ---
(32’) Important time in the game for the Cherries - they cannot afford to switch off again.
--- 31’ Goal! GOALLLLL!!! KING EQUALISES! The forward atones for his miss from the spot as he gets his side back on level terms. It's a fine strike from King as he lifts the ball over Fonte in the box before fending off the West Ham defender to bury his left-footed strike past Randolph. ---
(29’) CHANCE! Cook attacks the resulting corner and has a free header 12 yards from goal, but Randolph is able turn his effort over the bar.
(29’) SAVE! Fraser goes for goal from distance and powers an effort towards the bottom corner, forcing Randolph into a fine stop low to his right.
(28’) The Cherries come forward through Fraser as he jinks past three West Ham defenders, but as he shapes to shoot the white shirts close around him, forcing a pass out wide to Pugh.
(26’) Lanzini lifts a ball over the top of the Cherries defence for Antonio to chase with Francis. However, the Bournemouth skipper does well under pressure to calmly bring the ball away.
(25’) CHANCE! Lanzini sends Antonio into the left inside channel and the winger cuts back to feed the Argentine. He goes for the first-time strike, only to lift his effort over the bar.
(24’) OVER! Boruc punches Lanzini's cross away from the six-yard box, but Feghouli is able to collect and fire a first-time effort at goal. However, his effort goes well over the bar.
(23’) Smith was penalised against United for a handball and is caught again as he blocks Cresswell's cross. Lanzini will get a chance to send the ball into the box.
(22’) Kouyate raids forward from the back, and although he beats three Bournemouth defenders, he cannot dig out a cross and is forced to settle for a throw-in.
(20’) CHANCE! Obiang finds Feghouli with a crisp pass upfield and the midfielder once again tees up Antonio for a strike. He meets the ball with a solid contact, but can only fire his strike wide of the post.
(19’) West Ham clear the danger from the resulting free-kick, but the Cherries are still continiuing to attack the visitors. There's been no let up since conceding the opener.
(18’) King goes on a surge through the middle, but he gets his ankles clipped by Obiang, who escapes a booking.
(16’) CLOSE! Pugh sends Daniels into the left inside channel and he fires the ball across the face of goal, but his cross proves to be too powerful for King to meet in the six-yard box.
(14’) A long ball over the top finds Afobe between the two West Ham centre-backs, but as he lobs his effort over Randolph - the referee spots that he used his hand to control the ball and awards a free-kick to the Hammers.
(13’) Daniels tries an ambitious strike from distance, but can only scuff his strike well over the bar.
(12’) Noble slides in late on Gosling, but does not receive a second booking. He's walking a fine line now though.
--- 10’ Goal! GOALLL!!!! ANTONIO PUNISHES BOURNEMOUTH! A hammer blow - forgive the pun. West Ham raid to the other end of the pitch after the penalty miss and Feghouli tees up Antonio in the box. He turns on his left foot to strike and his effort creeps into the bottom corner. ---
--- 10’ Assist Feghouli makes a strong run before finding Antonio on the edge of the box. ---
--- 9’ Missed penalty MISS! King sends Randolph the wrong way, but he fails to hit the target with his strike, sending it inches past the post. ---
--- 9’ Yellow card Noble goes into the book for his complaints to the referee. ---

Spurs close the gap back to four points on leaders Chelsea thanks to Christian Eriksen’s long-range goal 12 minutes from time. Mauricio Pochettino’s side were far from their best but Palace failed to create any meaningful chances at the other end, and Eriksen’s strike proved to be enough to secure an eighth straight Premier League win. That’s all from us for today folks, thanks for joining us and we hope you can join us again soon.
Full-time: Crystal Palace 0-1 Tottenham Hotspur
--- 90’ +7 Yellow card Zaha is now shown a yellow card for kicking the ball away in frustration after Spurs were awarded a free-kick. ---
--- 90’ +6 Substitution Spurs are going to make their third and final substitution as they look to see out the remaining minutes of this game with Kieran Trippier replacing Alli. ---
(90’) Eriksen and Sissoko take a corner short and keep it in the corner before the latter wins another one. Spurs have very little intention of taking this ball anywhere other than the corner here.
(90’) Puncheon spreads the ball wide to Zaha just inside the Spurs half and the winger knocks the ball past Walker and very nearly gets around him, but the right-back does well to get his foot on the ball and prevent Zaha breaking away towards goal.
(90’) There will be seven minutes of added time at the end of this game following that injury to Sakho earlier in the half.
(90’) Mauricio Pochettino is deep in conversation with his assistant as Eriksen casually rolls the ball backwards towards his defence who knock the ball around amongst themselves with very little intention of going forward.
(88’) Palace are really struggling to get on the ball at the moment which is making it extremely hard for them to get Campbell into the game in the final third, and Spurs are not committing too many men forward having got that goal which is making it even harder for them.
(86’) CLOSE!! Alderweireld does come close to getting Spurs’ second goal as he shoots left-footed on the turn from 15 yards out, but he drags his low shot wide of the right-hand post with Hennessey unmoved.
(84’) Despite having taken the lead Spurs still look the far more dangerous of the two sides as cries of ‘we’ve got Alli’ ring out around Selhurst Park from the Spurs fans.
(82’) Kane goes close once again for Spurs as he dances his way past Kelly and through a crowded penalty area to the edge of the six yard box, but Milivojevic sticks a toe in at a crucial time to divert the ball out for a corner, which subsequently comes to nothing.
--- 81’ Substitution A third and final change for Palace now with Fraizer Campbell coming on to replace Benteke, giving Palace a different sort of option up front. ---
--- 79’ Yellow card Milivojevic goes into the book for blocking Alli after he had knocked the ball past him. ---
--- 78’ Assist Kane did extremely well to hold the ball up once again before rolling a simple pass into Eriksen to his right. ---
--- 78’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAALLLLLLL!!!! Eriksen gives Spurs the lead!! Kane does well to hold the ball up before rolling the ball into Eriksen 30 yards out from goal, and the Danish midfielder takes a couple of strides forwards before drilling the ball into the bottom left-hand corner past the despairing dive of Hennessey. ---
(77’) Davies stands up a cross towards the far post from the left-hand corner of the box after a good tackle on Son by Townsend, and although Kane gets up well to win the header six yards out from goal, he can’t generate enough power to beat Hennessey.
(76’) Palace may look relatively well organised at the back, but they have no real outlet whenever they do win the ball back at the minute with Benteke looking extremely isolated up front, meaning the ball is coming straight back at them almost immediately most of the time.
(74’) A half-chance for Spurs once again as Eriksen whips in a corner from the right-hand side after good work from Kane to win it off Kelly, but Dier can only glance his header wide of the near post, although he was well in front of the near post so he would have done well to beat Hennessey had he got the header on target anyway.
(72’) Alli brings the ball out of the sky with a lovely touch close to the left-hand touchline before driving infield and laying the ball off to Son, but Son’s attempted back heel back to Alli is just behind the midfielder and Palace regain possession.
(70’) Sam Allardyce is deep in conversation with the fourth official who appears to be getting questioned by both managers. Allardyce will know that Spurs have started to take control of this game in the last few minutes but he will also be relatively pleased with the way his side have dealt with that.
(68’) Walker rolls the ball into Kane and continues his run forward into the Palace penalty area, but Kane ignores him and tries to cut inside onto his left foot and go for goal himself, but he’s crowded out by several Palace defenders and the chance passes for Spurs.

(62’) Spurs have just lifted their intensity in the last few minutes and Alli tests Hennessey once again with a well-struck effort from the edge of the penalty box after controlling a strong pass into his feet from Eriksen, but the Palace goalkeeper gets down well to his left to gather in the shot.

Sam Allardyce will be keen for his side to continue to get the ball into wide areas in the second half, with Zaha and Townsend having looked a threat throughout, while Spurs, who have already changed formation once, will want to get more support up alongside Kane who has looked pretty isolated for large parts of the first half.
Neither side have really got going in what has been a pretty lacklustre first half in truth, but Palace have been the better side without creating any clear cut chances while Spurs have failed to give Hennessey any problems in the Palace goal.
Half-time: Palace 0-0 Spurs
(45’) Alli now goes to ground midway through the Palace half but doesn’t get a free-kick and Palace break forward quickly before Townsend crosses towards Benteke from the right-hand side, but Alderweireld heads the ball behind for a corner, before Walker boots the ball out of the stadium in frustration.

Referee Kevin Friend was a critical figure in the contest as he did not send off Tyrone Mings, Harry Arter or Ibrahimovic, despite being solid cases for all three to be dismissed. Andrew Surman was the unlucky man that was sent off and Adam Smith was on the receiving end of a terrible penalty decision. Not a great game for the official.
Artur Boruc is the hero for the visitors as he made a number of fine stops, including a penalty save from Zlatan Ibrahimovic - who had a game to forget.
WHAT AN INCREDIBLE GAME! Bournemouth somehow secure a point from this fixture despite playing the second half with 10 men. Manchester United threw everything at the Cherries, but were unable to come away with the win.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-1 BOURNEMOUTH
(90’) THAT'S IT! Bournemouth have held out for the point!
(90’) SCRAMBLE!  Pogba collects the ball in stride in the box, but he cannot swivel to fire at goal, allowing the Cherries to clear the danger.
(90’) CLOSE! Arter robs Martial of possession deep in the United half and almost gets free of the Frenchman, but he recovers just in time to clear the danger.
(90’) MISS! Pogba has the chance to win the game for United, but he scuffs his effort at goal, wasting a golden opportunity unmarked at the back post.
(90’) Nervy times at the back for Cargill as he misjudges his header, but he just manages to clear ahead of Mata.
(90’) Mata stabs his cross forward into the box, but the ball hits the deck and rolls away from Ibrahimovic at the vital moment.
(90’) There will be five minutes of added time.
(90’) All hands on deck for Bournemouth at the back as Fraser makes an important challenge before Rojo slices his cross straight into the hands of Boruc.
(89’) Mata breaks down the left but excellent defending from Cook prevents the cross from reaching the box before he stops the corner as well.
--- 88’ Substitution Gradel replaces King for the visitors. ---
(87’) Cargill remains disciplined in his play in the box, refusing to jump into his challenge with Rashford before dispossessing the United forward.
(86’) Fellaini has joined Ibrahimovic in the forward line and United are simply throwing bodies into the box and hoping for the best at this stage.
(84’) Afobe has space to break into down the right, but his delivery is awful as he fails to even threaten to find the two team-mates that joined him in the box.
(83’) Pogba tries to do too much with his cross into the box and it allows Boruc to come off his line to claim with ease.
(82’) Bournemouth pile men forward for a corner, but United are able to clear their lines and break down the right.
--- 80’ Yellow card Rashford is booked for a shoulder barge on Smith. Who knows what the referee is doing now - there is no consistency in his decision-making. ---
(79’) OVER! Pogba takes the set-piece himself and hammers his effort over the bar. Frustration building for the home side.
--- 78’ Substitution Mings has suffered a serious injury here and is replaced by Cargill. ---
(78’) BAFFLING! Arter catches Pogba late and the referee awards a free-kick, but somehow the midfielder escapes a second booking.
(76’) BLOCK! From the resulting corner, Ibrahimovic collects at the back post and hammers his effort towards goal, only to see his strike blocked by Mings. The defender goes down and needs more treatment.
(74’) WIDE! Pogba goes for goal from the edge of the box, but he pulls his effort just past the post with the aid of a deflection. A crazy match continues as United were allowed to play on despite Arter being down on the deck after a collision with the Frenchman.
--- 72’ Missed penalty MISS! Ibrahimovic's poor display continues as he fires his effort low to the bottom corner, but Boruc makes a brilliant save to deny the Swede. ---
(72’) Penalty Save Artur Boruc
--- 71’ Yellow card Gosling is booked for his protest against the decision. ---
(71’) PENALTY TO MANCHESTER UNITED! Smith handballs the ball in the box and the referee points to the spot.
--- 70’ Substitution Rashford replace Shaw as Mourinho rolls the dice. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Rooney is withdrawn in favour of Lingard. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Fellaini replaces Carrick for the home side. ---
(67’) Mings goes down after a tussle with Ibrahimovic on the right flank. The home fans are not too sympathetic to the Bournemouth defender's plight.
(67’) Changes are coming for Manchester United...
(66’) King, Afobe and Fraser do well to take the sting out of the game by mustering a strong surge forward for the visitors. King has been excellent for the Cherries today.
(64’) BLOCK! Ibrahmovic takes the free-kick, but hammers his strike straight into the wall. He has not been at his best today.
(63’) Gosling loses possession on the half-way line and United surge forward in numbers. The midfielder then commits a foul in a dangerous area of the pitch by tripping Pogba 25 yards from goal. Ibrahimovic and the Frenchman are standing over the ball.
(61’) None of the 38 visiting teams that have been reduced to 10 men at Old Trafford have managed to beat Manchester United. Only eight of them have managed to take a point away from the stadium.
(60’) Rooney attempts to time his run behind the Bournemouth defence to latch on to Shaw's pass, but he is a fraction early and is caught offside.
(59’) Valencia bursts down the right flank and whips an early cross into the box, but it's straight down Boruc's throat.
--- 58’ Yellow card Carrick goes into the book for pulling back King. ---
(56’) SAVE! Pogba lines up a strike from distance as he attempts to curl his effort past Boruc into the top corner, only to be denied by a fine save from the Cherries keeper.
(54’) Boruc comes up big with two punches away from the six-yard box, but United come again as Martial wins another set-piece down the left flank.
(53’) OVER! United keep the pressure on even after the corner is cleared. Rooney collects on the edge of the box, but his strike is deflected over by Cook.
(52’) Mata lifts a dangerous cross to the back post, but Daniels takes action ahead of Valencia, heading the ball behind for a corner.
(51’) The Cherries are not backing down from the challenge, despite being reduced to 10 men and are continuing to play the ball out from the back.
(49’) Martial lifts a teasing cross into the box towards Rooney at the back post, but Cook just glances the ball over the bar and away from the United skipper.
(47’) Bournemouth assistant manager Jason Tindall has reportedly been sent to the stands for protesting to referee Friend at the break.
(47’) Bournemouth win a free-kick in  dangerous position down the left flank, but Fraser wastes the opportunity by sending the ball out for a goal-kick.
--- 46’ Substitution Gosling replaces Pugh for the visitors, which will see the midfielder drop into Surman's vacated position. ---
(46’) We're back underway at Old Trafford.
As the players emerge from the tunnel Mourinho lets his feelings known to Mings for his stamp on Ibrahimovic.
The referee appeared to acknowledge the incident by taking to him, but incredibly did not send the United forward off. If Bournemouth were not raging before then they were seconds later when Andrew Surman earned his second booking.
The drama did not end there as first Tyrone Mings decided to step on Zlatan Ibrahimovic's head after the Swede had fallen down in the box. Referee Kevin Friend did not spot the incident. Ibra retaliated by swinging his elbow straight into the defender's face a minute later.
Somehow the scores are level at the break. Manchester United have dominated this game and took a deserved lead through Marcos Rojo, but a foul by Phil Jones on Marc Pugh allowed Josh King to equalise from the penalty spot.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-1 BOURNEMOUTH
(45’) The referee ends the first half.
(45’) CHANCE! Ibrahimovic pulls into the left inside channel and shoots at goal, but Boruc makes the save before Daniels clears away the loose ball in the six-yard box.
(45’) Ibrahimovic collects in the box, but he is in on offside position. He's not happy about the decision, but on the other hand he's lucky to be on the pitch.
(45’) There will be three minutes of added time.
--- 45’ Red card! Incredibly Surman is the man to be sent off as he collects his second booking for his protests to Friend. ---
(45’) DRAMA! A lot to cover here. First Mings steps on Ibrahimovic's head - that should be a red. From the resulting corner - Ibrahimovic retaliates with a huge swing of his elbow against Mings - that should be a red. Friend talks to the Swede, but does not send him or Mings from the field.
(43’) CHANCE! Rooney peels off his man in the left inside channel and fires towards top corner, but once again Boruc is there to make the save.
(42’) CHANCE! Ibrahimovic turns in the final third and scoops a strike towards the top corner, but Boruc flings himself to his right to make the save.
--- 40’ Goal! GOALLLLLL!!!!! BOURNEMOUTH ARE LEVEL! King makes no mistake from the spot as he hammers his strike into the top corner. ---
--- 39’ Yellow card Ibrahimovic goes into the book for his protest against the penalty. ---
(38’) PENALTY TO BOURNEMOUTH! Jones brings down Pugh in the box and the referee points to the spot.
(37’) Ibrahimovic throws Mings to the ground off the ball and somehow escapes with only a talking to from the referee. Interesting decision.
(35’) United are dropping the tempo slightly in an attempt to gain better precision with their passing in the final third. The gaps are so huge in the Bournemouth defence there is no need to rush themselves.
--- 33’ Yellow card Surman wipes out Shaw on a surge down the left and goes into the book, despite his appeal to referee Friend. ---
(32’) For all of United's dominance, somehow Bournemouth are only one goal behind. Howe would be delighted to get into the break trailing by a one-goal margin. An important 13 minutes ahead.
(30’) Rooney and Ibrahimovic almost combine in the final third, but the Swede is just on his heels for the return pass allowing Mings to knock the ball back Boruc.
(29’) The Cherries make their first surge forward since Afobe's miss and Daniels gets around the back on the left inside channel, but his cross is claimed with ease by De Gea.
(27’) Mata steers the ball into Ibrahimovic's path on the edge of the box, but a good covering tackle from Smith dispossesses the Swede before he can threaten.
(25’) More concerns for the Cherries as Cook has sustained an injury and requires treatment off the pitch.
--- 23’ Assist Valencia drives a low strike at goal and he sees his effort diverted into the net by Rojo. ---
--- 23’ Goal! GOALLLLL!!! ROJO PUTS UNITED AHEAD! It has been coming since the opening seconds of the game, but the Red Devils finally take the lead as Rojo diverts Valencia's strike from the edge of the box past Boruc into the bottom corner. ---
(21’) Smith raids forward and loses possession giving Martial acres of space to raid down the left flank. Only a good covering tackle from Cook stops another threat at goal from United.
(19’) CHANCE! Martial breaks into the box after collecting Carrick's pass. Bournemouth desperately attempt to get men back, but are bailed out once again by a solid stop from Boruc.
(17’) WIDE! Pogba seizes possession in the final third and lifts the ball to the back post for Ibrahimovic to attack. However, the Swede fails to generate any power on his effort, sending it wide of the post.
(16’) Mata has the freedom of the right inside channel as no Bournemouth picks him up. He tries to find Ibrahimovic at the back post, but Mings comes across to make the block.
(14’) OFF THE LINE! Martial causes havoc down the left and sends a dangerous cross towards the near post, but somehow Ibrahimovic is unable to turn the ball home before Daniels makes the clearance at the vital moment.
--- 13’ Yellow card Arter goes into the book for a lunge on Carrick. ---
(12’) SAVE! Martial collects on the left flank and cuts inside on his right foot to fire a low effort at goal, but Boruc makes a solid stop to keep the ball out.
(11’) SLIP! Afobe breaks away from Rojo at the other end of the pitch and only has De Gea to beat, only to lose his footing at the vital moment, allowing the Spaniard to gather.
(10’) CHANCE! Rooney robs Mings of possession and tees up Ibrahimovic to shoot inside the box, but the Swede takes an uncharacteristically poor first touch and the opening is spurned by the Red Devils.
(8’) OFFSIDE! Mata breaks in behind once again and fires at goal, but his effort is saved by Boruc. It would not have mattered anyway had he found the net as the Spaniard was flagged offside.
(6’) Mata raids in behind the Bournemouth defence on the right flank, but his low cross into the box is cleared away by Cook. The Cherries are looking extremely vulnerable at the back in the early stages.
(5’) SAVE! Boruc makes a fine stop to keep the scores level as a simple ball over the top has the Cherries all over the place at the back. Pogba stabs his strike towards the bottom corner, but the keeper just gets a fingertip on the ball to send it wide.
(4’) United are cut open at the back by a long ball and King barges Jones off the ball, with referee Friend not awarding a free-kick. However, the forward is unable to pick out a blue shirt in the box.
(3’) A long ball over the top of the United defence has Jones struggling with Afobe. De Gea comes off his line to help his team-mate, only for the ball to strike Jones. Fortunately for United, De Gea reacts in time to stop it in its tracks.
(2’) CHANCE! Valencia snatches possession for the home side and he attempts to pick out Rooney in the box. The first ball is cleared but his second cross finds his skipper at the back post, but he can only head his effort over the bar.

That's all from us at the Hawthorns. Thanks for joining us throughout this Premier League clash between West Brom and Crystal Palace.
Full-time at the Hawthorns and West Brom lose 2-0 at home to Crystal Palace. The away side are truly deserving of their victory and clean sheet as the Eagles escape the relegation zone.
(90’) Robson-Kanu's deflected shot earns West Brom a late corner, but Brunt's cross falls to the floor and Puncheon manages to kick the ball away high and clear of any danger.
(90’) The physicality of Benteke has been a fantastic outlet for the visitors this afternoon and even as this match dies out. The Belgian has done so well holding up the ball for the attacking midfielders behind him.
(90’) West Brom have been reduced to almost nothing this half and only a bit more in the first. The home support are starting to leave the stadium as frustration gets the better of them.
(88’) Palace are looking to run the clock down now as Townsend had the opportunity to whip a cross into the box, but the winger opted to run the ball into the corner and shield the ball.
--- 86’ Substitution McArthur comes on for Zaha as Palace look to see out the match. ---
(86’) Allardyce said he'd be happy with a point before kick-off, but unless a miracle occurs for West Brom is looks like they're going to have all three. The visitors have been fantastic this afternoon.
--- 84’ Goal! GOAL! It's game over, Townsend and Zaha find themselves up against McAuley and Evans but the former of the Palace duo steps the ball wide of the defence and then fires past Foster at the near post. ---
(83’) Palace are being really careful on the attack now as they desperately try and hold onto this result, which would be a fantastic win to take back to London and escape the relegation zone.
--- 81’ Substitution Pulis gives 17-year-old Leko the chance to be the hero by bringing him on for Fletcher. ---
(81’) Frustration may be settling into the West Brom side as Morrison tries his luck from range but smashed his shot far over Hennessey's crossbar.
(79’) CHANCE! Foster keeps West Brom in the match by denying Townsend who was one-on-one with the goalkeeper following a fantastic pass from Milivojevic.
(77’) Soon-to-be a social media sensation, Livermore pushes the referee to the ground as he got in the way of Sakho and the midfielder battling for possession, much to the delight of the spectating home fans.
(75’) A dangerous free-kick for West Brom allowed Brunt to deliver a powerful cross into the Crystal Palace box, but it's too high for the blue and white shirts to attack and Hennessey comes out to collect.
--- 74’ Substitution Dann comes on for Cabaye in a defensive move for Palace. ---
(73’) The West Brom support are trying really hard to get their side back in this by turning up the noise levels inside the Hawthorns, but Palace aren't committing many men forward in order to remain sturdy at the back.
--- 71’ Substitution An attacking sub for West Brom as Robson-Kanu comes on for Nyom. ---

(69’) Pulis is desperately looking for a way to turn this match back around, as if anybody looks like scoring the next goal in this match it's Crystal Palace.
(67’) A corner broke to Townsend on the edge of the box and the winger smashed a volley towards goal but McClean put his body on the line to deflect the effort over the crossbar.
(65’) A delivery into the box from Brunt on his weak foot caused issues at the back for Hennessey, who was unable to get a hold of the floated cross. Luckily for the Welsh goalkeeper his defence managed to sweep up the danger.
--- 63’ Substitution A tactical change for West Brom as McClean comes on for Chadli. ---
(63’) A stoppage in play as van Aanholt goes down injured and fails to get back up. The left-back received some medical attention on his ankle and his afternoon of football is over.
--- 62’ Substitution Schlupp comes on for the injured van Aanholt. ---
(61’) A big risk from Livermore as the midfielder tried to bring a ball down from out of the air in his own penalty area, with his poor touch allowing van Aanholt to snap a volley towards goal but fortunately for the home side it goes over the crossbar.
(59’) CHANCE! Almost 2-0 as Zaha skipped through McAuley and Dawson to get into the box, but Foster managed to prevent the shot by charging off his line.
(57’) The intensity is being turned up from Palace as the belief runs through them. West Brom are in such fine form, but the Eagles are truly deserving of their lead after commanding large spells of this fixture.
--- 55’ Goal! GOAL! Glorious goal from Palace and it's deserved! A long ball over the top from Cabaye is brought down by Zaha and drilled across goal to leave Forster helpless. ---
--- 55’ Assist Cabaye gets his second assist in as many game with a wonderfully weighted pass across the pitch to Zaha to find the winger in room behind Brunt. ---
(54’) Palace are just pumping long balls forward to Benteke, but the West Brom defence are struggling to deal with the strength of the striker. Frequently in this match the hosts have put both Evans and McAuley on the Belgian to prevent him from winning the ball in the air.
(52’) An innovative corner from West Brom almost catches Crystal Palace out as a low cross from Brunt is hit by Chadli on the penalty spot, but the winger is unable to keep his shot beneath the crossbar.
(50’) Palace are starting the half much better! The London side are taking to this fixture very well and could well be on course to take something from this match if they continue to play well.
(48’) A signal of intent from Palace straight away as Townsend gets down the right side and cuts the ball back to Zaha, but the effort into the middle is just behind his teammate and West Brom clear the play.
(46’) Palace get the second half underway!
Half-time and the scores are level at 0-0. Benteke has come the closest, with Brunt heading off the line, but West Brom have crafted a couple of chances for themselves. Goals are coming.
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card Benteke talks himself into the first yellow card of the match. ---
(45’) Just the one minute of stoppage time at the Hawthorns as this half continues to die out. It looks as if both teams are just after the whistle now and discuss their plans for the second half.
(43’) A brief stoppage in play as Evans and Benteke clash heads for the second time in this match, but it appears as if both of them will be okay to continue the game.
(41’) Half-time is approaching the Hawthorns and the score is still level. Neither goalkeeper have been called into any fantastic saves, but chances have been there for both sides in this half.
(39’) Cries for a penalty from West Brom! A fantastic switch from Dawson finds Rondon on the left and as the striker skips between Cabaye and Ward he goes to the ground, but the referee judged he went down too easily.
(37’) A long ball into the box is headed down brilliantly by Benteke as the striker used his strength, but despite Cabaye's best effort to meet with the pass McAuley did well to hook the ball away from the Frenchman.
(35’) CHANCE! A small chance for West Brom as a drilled pass to the edge of the box is connected with by Brunt, but the winger turns his effort over the crossbar.
(33’) West Brom must try and take some sting out of Crystal Palace by getting hold of the ball, as they can't allow the visitors to gain confidence and start dominating this fixture.
(31’) Palace are really starting to take control of this match now, by no means do West Brom have their backs up against the wall, but the London side are enjoying their best spell in this fixture.
(29’) Wonderful football from Palace around the West Brom box almost allowed Benteke to turn away from the Baggies' defence and get a shot off on goal, but McAuley did really well to get a tackle in on the Belgian striker.
(27’) Pulis is getting rather animated on the sideline as the referee awards a free-kick to the visitors on the half way line, which the West Brom manager clearly disagreed with!
(25’) A clipped pass from Townsend is almost met by Zaha in the box, but Dawson judges the weight on the delivery correctly to shield off the winger and allow the play to run out for a goal kick.
(23’) Brunt's delivery into the box has been really good today as the winger almost finds Rondon at the back post with a dangerous cross, but the ball is eventually turned behind by the Palace defence.
(21’) A brief scare at the back for West Brom as a long ball forward was allowed to bounce by Dawson, but the hosts eventually do well to play their way out of their own box.
(19’) CHANCE! A fantastic delivery from Cabaye into the middle from a corner allows Benteke to turn a header on goal, but Brunt clears the ball off the line to keep the scores level.
(17’) CHANCE! A clever corner from Morrison finds Livermore on the edge of the box in plenty of room, but the midfielder was unable to make a clean connection with the ball and get a decent shot off on goal.
(15’) Dawson manages to find some room on the right side as the ball gets shifted across to the pitch to the full-back, but his delivery into the middle was poor and Sakho was able to head clear on the near post.
(13’) Palace are being forced into lofted passes out wide, which isn't serving them too well currently. The away side have enough players to run the ball at West Brom's full-backs, but they're yet to do that this afternoon.
(11’) Palace are in control of the ball at the moment with West Brom looking patient and not pressing too high. It appears as if the hosts are confident in their ability to keep out the Eagles.
(9’) A bit of pressure from Crystal Palace almost ends in a great opportunity for the visitors as a cross from Townsend into the box was teasing Benteke to attack, but there was a bit too much on the delivery.
(7’) Nobody yet to test either goalkeeper, but the match has started at a good tempo with clear intentions from both sides. It seems as if Palace have gone to the Hawthrons with an attacking mentality
(5’) McAuley with a fantastic interception to prevent an attack for Palace. Townsend cut inside onto his left to feed the ball into Benteke, but the Northern Irish defender raced in front of the striker to launch a counter-attack.
(3’) Brunt tries to test Hennessey early on with a long, driven shot from a free-kick approximately 30 yards from goal, but Cabaye does well to charge down the effort on goal.
