And that wraps it up here at Anfield. Liverpool get the win they deserve thanks to goals from substitute Origi and Milner from the spot. They move top of the table for two hours at least, with Chelsea soon to kick off against Tottenham. That's all we've got time for, thanks for joining us.
--- 90’ +2 Substitution First appearance in the Premier Leaue for Ben Woodburn, as Wijnaldum departs. ---
--- 90’ +1 Goal! MILNER SEALS IT! The makeshift left-back steps up to the spot and buries it, sending the keeper the wrong way. Fifth EPL penalty for him, and game over. ---
(89’) LIVERPOOL HAVE A PENALTY! Mane's searing pace takes him past Denayer down the wing, and Ndong comes across with a late challenge in the area to foul him. Easy decision.
--- 87’ Substitution Firmino will be substituted late on, and Lucas enters the game. ---
(85’) Liverpool are now closing the game out in a far more disciplined manner, only attacking when they have the numerical advantage after winning the ball in midfield. Five minutes to go.
(83’) Determined work by Mane sees him win the ball in midfield and turn defence into attack. He plays it to Origi who then lays it off for Can, who just about executes a roulette before losing the ball.
(81’) Liverpool have taken their foot off the pedal for a moment as they put more focus on keeping the door locked at the back. It's now or never for Sunderland you feel, with less than 10 minutes remaining.
--- 79’ Substitution The Scot follows that up by summoning Adnan Januzaj off the bench, with Watmore making way. ---
--- 79’ Substitution Double change here for Sunderland. Moyes' first move is to take off Pienaar and introduce Lynden Gooch. ---
(77’) Klopp is still urging his team forward late on here, as the last thing they want is to sit back and allow Sunderland encouragement to commit numbers in attack. Offense is the best form of defence.
--- 75’ Assist Henderson will be credited with the assist. ---
--- 75’ Goal! WHAT A GOAL FROM THE SUBSTITUTE! Liverpool finally have their breakthrough as Origi cuts inside of Watmore and curls a lovely effort inside the far post from a considerable angle! ---
(72’) WASTED! Henderson takes charge of the free-kick, but he fails to find the target. It was such a good position too, and the way the Sunderland defence set up it was almost like they expected that to hit the target!
--- 70’ Yellow card The yellow cards are coming thick and fast in the second half, and Pienaar is cautioned for bringing down Firmino right on the edge of the Sunderland penalty area. ---
(69’) HUGE SCRAMBLE! From the free-kick, Sunderland play their way into the penalty area, with Anichebe getting the ball to Watmore at the back post, but Karius is again quick to snuff out the danger! The visitors keep the ball alive with the keeper out of position, but fail to get a shot on target.
--- 67’ Yellow card Lovren is the latest player to get booked after fouling Defoe. ---
(66’) INCHES AWAY! Firmino cuts onto his right boot and curls an in-swinging cross towards the head of Origi. The forward nods it back into the path of Can, who pummels the ball the wrong side of the post.
--- 64’ Yellow card Origi has done well to draw fouls in the second half, and O'Shea takes one for the team, bringing down the substitute. ---
(62’) Klopp is clearly not content with matters out on the pitch, and takes it upon himself to wave his hands like a madman to pump up the crowd. It's had the desired effect as the noise levels raise.
--- 60’ Yellow card Kone takes a piece out of Origi from behind and duly gets booked. ---
(59’) PICKFORD CALLED INTO ACTION AGAIN! Firmino takes matters into his own hands, beating Pienaar with some trickery before taking aim, but the goalkeeper, who has not put a finger out of place, is all over it.
(57’) It's all Liverpool in the second period as they set up camp outside the Sunderland penalty area. THe ball keeps getting thrown back at them whenever they penetrate into the 18-yard box though.
(54’) OOOH SO CLOSE! Can sets that play in motion with some keep-ups before lobbing a terrific ball over the back four for Wijnaldum, who lashes it across the face of goal, where James Milner is inches away from tapping it in.
(52’) Karius has to be on his toes to get to a long ball before Duncan Watmore. The keeper has hardly had anything to do in this game, but he showed good concentration there to spot that danger.
(50’) That's twice now that some dangerous balls have been flashed across the face of goal by the home side. We've seen that fairly often this game - a Liverpool player getting to the byline but his teammates slow to arrive in support.
(48’) Liverpool pick up where they left off, controlling the ball and the tempo of the game, but they continue to find the door locked at the back. Second game in a row that they're struggling for clear-cut chances.
(46’) Off we go again!
And that will do it from Anfield for now as Liverpool fail to break down a resolute Sunderland in a stalemate. Despite all of their possession, Pickford hasn't been troubled as much as he would have expected. To compound matters, Coutinho has gone off with a nasty-looking ankle injury, which has deprived them of some creativity. I'll be back soon.
(45’) There's just no room for Liverpool at the edge of the area as both Wijnaldum and Firmino find the door shut. The Brazilian eventually clips one in to Emre Can, who tries to do too much with his header as it drops wide of the post with Mane failing to catch up.
(45’) Anichebe is back defending to show good anticipation to intercept Origi's throughball intended for Clyne. You have to admire the way that Sunderland have worked for each other as a team.
(43’) Clyne and Wijnaldum try to link with a one-two down the right, but O'Shea is out to greet the former. He gives away a corner which he swore was a goal-kick but his arguments are moot as Liverpool fail to make anything of it.
(41’) Sunderland started the game in a 4-4-2 formation, but Anichebe has quickly shifted out to the left-hand side to form a 4-5-1. It's providing an extra man to keep Clyne occupied out wide and prevent him from overlapping.
(39’) SHOULD HAVE HIT THE TARGET! Jordan Henderson stands over a free-kick, and Lovren sneaks around to the back post to get his head to it, but he flashes it the wrong side of the post.
(37’) Coutinho's departure has coincided with a dip in the tempo of the match, which will suit Sunderland just fine. It's been a committed defensive effort from Sunderland so far in this one.
--- 34’ Substitution That will indeed be the end of the game for Coutinho, who is strapped to the stretcher with his right ankle in a brace. He's applauded off the pitch as Divock Orgi replaces him. ---
(32’) Doesn't look very good for Coutinho, who has stayed down following a challenge with Didier Ndong. He's in some pain, and the stretcher is out on the field. Klopp is active on the bench to ready a substitute.
(30’) Not sure what that was about from Dejan Lovren. It was neither a shot or a long diagonal into the area. What it ended up being was catching practice for Pickford, who has looked confident this afternoon.
(28’) WIDE OF THE MARK! Nathaniel Clyne pops up deep on the right but his teammates are a little slow to get forward in support. He squares to Georginio Wijnaldum eventually, whose shot doesn't trouble the keeper.
(26’) Terrible decision from Sadio Mane. The winger initially beat Pienaar down the right and then benefited from a missed interception to scamper into space. He had time to pick his spot or set up Roberto Firmino, but rushed it and sent the ball harmlessly into Pickford's territory.
(24’) Patrick van Aanholt takes the ball on his chest and lashes it towards goal from range, but he cuts across it and it goes wide. He's scored a few this season, and has looked good on the left flank.
(22’) Composed defending in the air from the visiting team once again. Mane's in-swinging cross is headed away by Ndong. Henderson picks up the pieces, but his lofted return ball is plucked out of the sky by Pickford.
(20’) Milner has the opportunity to cross twice in quick succession, but both times, they're gobbled up by the Sunderland defence. It's not an attacking approach that Klopp would be too happy with.
(18’) FINE SAVE! Billy Jones whacks the ball forward from his own half and Joel Matip hesitates, which allows Steven Pienaar a pocket of space to charge into. However, Karius is off his line to block the finish and spare his defender's blushes.
(16’) Jermain Defoe collects the ball up front, but lacking support, he decides to go for goal, with Loris Karius not troubled by that effort. Rare respite for the visiting side after spending most of the game so far defending.
(14’) INTO THE ARMS OF PICKFORD! A nifty move from the home side sees Coutinho link with Henderson before playing the ball to Wijnaldum. He takes it on the turn but the Sunderland keeper is well positioned.
(11’) Moyes wasn't kidding when he promised to park the bus. All the visiting players are back in their own half, and are looking very disciplined to prevent Liverpool with a clear route forward.
(9’) Liverpool continue to press high up the field in typical Klopp fashion. Clyne picks the pocket of Watmore and gets the ball to Firmino who tries his luck from 20 yards, but it's swallowed by Pickford.
(7’) Anichebe uses his upper body strength to momentarily hold off Henderson, but he then loses out and doesn't get a foul call. Coutinho springs onto the loose ball and tries to let fly from the top of the box, but Kone makes a good challenge.
(5’) Van Aanholt does well to drive into space down the left flank, before dropping it off to Anichebe and continuing his run down the wing. However, the striker runs into trouble as he has three defenders for company.
(3’) Recently retired Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard is in attendance tonight. The next step for the ex-Reds skipper is unclear, but Klopp has promised that the door is always open for him to have a role at the club.
(1’) We're off!
Despite the goalless draw with Southampton last time out, Klopp sticks with the same XI. Daniel Sturridge and Adam Lallana are both injured. For the visitors, Papy Djilobodji's suspension sees John O'Shea return, while Steven Pienaar steps in for long-term casualty Paddy McNair.

--- 54’ Yellow card Within minutes of coming onto the pitch, Townsend has picked up a yellow card for pulling Routledge's shirt and giving away a free-kick. ---
(54’) Kelly is still struggling to deal with the pace of Barrow. The Swans is trying to take him on at every opportunity and wins another Swansea corner.
--- 52’ Substitution Connor Wickham comes off on the stretcher with Andros Townsend replaces him, who has had a hand in three goals in his last three league games versus Swansea (two goals, one assist). ---
(49’) Break in play at the moment as Wickham is down for Palace and he looks to be in a lot of pain with a knee injury. Looks like he is coming off.
(48’) Sigurdsson is certainly a key player for Swansea and he has now had a hand in 38 Premier League goals (22 goals, 16 assists); 24 more than any other player for the club in this period.
(46’) We're back underway!
The teams are back out and almost ready to get the second half underway here at the Liberty Stadium.
Palace took the led early on after a great piece of play by Zaha and finish past Fabianski, however Swansea rallied and a terrific free-kick by Sigurdsson gave them their equalising goal. Just moments later Palace hit the bar but the score finished 1-1 heading into the half-time break. This key game for both sides could go either way now.
HALF-TIME: SWANSEA 1-1 PALACE
(45’) That's the half-time whistle!
(45’) There will be a minimum of three minutes added on here...
(44’) Good end to the half by Swansea. Barrow is again doing well down the right side, this time he finds himself in a very good position just ten yards from goal after a great ball in form Cork, but he slices his shot well wide of the Palace goal. He should've done better.
--- 42’ Yellow card Hennessey goes into the book for time wasting. Alan Pardew is not happy with that decision at all! ---
(40’) What a game we have on our hands now! There is a great atmosphere now inside the Liberty Stadium and both sides look dangerous in attack.
(38’) PALACE HIT THE BAR! The visitors almost re-take the lead just moments after conceding, Cabaye rounds Fabianksi but is forced wide so crosses the ball back to Zaha whose header hits the crossbar, then the rebound almost falls to Wickham but he and Benteke get in the way of each other and Swansea just about manage to clear.
--- 36’ Goal! HE'S DONE IT! What a strike by Sigurdsson! A super free-kick fired into the top left-hand corner which left Hennessey with no chance. It was a poor free-kick for Puncheon to give away and Sigurdsson is always a threat when it comes to set pieces, and he has got his side back into the game with a fantastic strike. ---
(36’) Two consecutive corners for Swansea come to nothing but then Cork wins a free-kick right on the edge of the box after a foul by Puncheon, giving away a needless free-kick. This is a great opportunity for Swansea and it is Sigurdsson who is going to take it...
(33’) Swansea manager Bob Bradley is having a deep conversation with his coaching staff in the technical area at the moment, are they debating an early change?
(31’) This is better from Swansea, they are dominating the possession but are struggling to create any chances, with Palace easily dealing with any aerial balls that come their way.
(28’) CHANCE PALACE! Wickham comes very close to doubling the visitors lead but Fabianksi makes a terrific diving save to his right to deny him, after it looked like the Palace forwards header was creeping into the bottom corner of the goal.
--- 27’ Yellow card Another yellow card awarded to a Swansea player, this time to captain Jack Cork for another poor tackle. ---
(25’) Their is a nervous atmosphere here at the Liberty Stadium now, Swansea need to start really threatening the Palace goal if they are to get the crowd going again. However Palace still look the more dangerous side going forward.
--- 22’ Yellow card The first yellow card of the game goes to Routledge after a late tackle on Cabaye. ---
--- 19’ Assist Benteke rose highest to easily beat the Swansea centre-backs in the air and nod the ball onto Zaha who then fired home the Palace goal. ---
--- 19’ Goal! PALACE TAKE THE LEAD! It's Zaha with the goal. The Palace winger latched on to Benteke's flick on and then used his pace and power to beat Neil Taylor in the box and fired a low shot past Lukasz Fabianski into the back of the net. ---
(18’) First corner of the game for Swansea! The defenders have come forward but once again anything in the air is being cleared by the Palace defence. The visitors certainly have a big advantage when it comes to aerial battles.
(16’) Barrow once again causing problems down the right-hand side against Kelly, the Swansea man just has too much pace for the Palace defender to deal with, and the hosts are trying to exploit that.
(14’) CHANCE SWANSEA! First real opportunity of the game for the Swans and Sigurdsson should've done better with his effort at goal. It came through Barrow beating Kelly down the right and then he pulled the ball back to Sigurdsson in the box, but he couldn't get enough power behind his shot to really trouble Wayne Hennessey, who easily gathers.
(13’) Palace are just missing that final ball at present, they are enjoying possession in front of Swansea but are struggling to create any clear-cut chances.
(11’) Palace are slightly edging the game so far, they are coming out of tackles with the ball and look more dangerous going forward through the likes of Zaha, Puncheon and Benteke, however Swansea are well organised at the moment which is limiting these players.
(9’) STAT: Palace are on a five-game losing streak in the Premier League; they haven't lost six in a row in the competition since November 2013.
(7’) Now it's Swansea's turn to test the Palace goal. Modou Barrow earns a free-kick in a good position down the right after beating Martin Kelly, the free-kick is taken by Sigurdsson but Dann rises to meet it and clears the danger.
(6’) CHANCE PALACE! Great opportunity for Benteke to give the visitors the lead. Palace won a corner which was taken by Yohan Cabaye and met by Scott Dann, the ball then bounced around the Swansea box before it fell to Benteke just yards from goal, but he fires well over the bar from close range.
(4’) It looks like Gylfi Sigurdsson is once again playing as the main striker for Swansea today, whilst Palace are set up in a 4-4-2 formation with Christian Benteke and Connor Wickham both up front but Wilfried Zaha and Jason Puncheon are constantly charging down wings.
(3’) Swansea with the early possession, they will be eager to get the home fans on side here, after a poor start to the season which has led to supporters voicing their disappointment from the stands.

Head-to-head: The three previous Premier League meetings between these sides at the Liberty Stadium have all ended in a 1-1 draw. The Swans are also unbeaten in their last five home league games with Palace, although four of those games have ended in draws.
Swansea were unlucky to just come away from Goodison Park with a point last weekend, when a Seamus Coleman goal late on made the score 1-1. However they need to start picking up victories if they are to avoid a relegation fight. Meanwhile, Palace have lost their last five Premier League games, which has seen the slip down the table, both teams will be eager to take away all three points today.
TEAM NEWS: Perhaps surprise change for Palace as Alan Pardew has elected to drop Andros Townsend to the bench, with Connor Wickham coming in to the starting line-up, after he came off the bench to score against Manchester City last weekend. Southampton see off the late pressure from Everton to clinch a 1-0 victory here at St Mary's after a goal from Charlie Austin after just one minute. The Toffees were well off the pace for large periods of the game but came close late on, however the Saints defence stood firm and clinched all three points.
FULL-TIME: SOUTHAMPTON 1-0 EVERTON
(90’) That's the full-time whistle!
(90’) There will be a minimum of three minutes added on here at St Mary's.
--- 89’ Substitution Final substitution of the game as the Saints goalscorer comes off to be replaced by Shane Long. ---
(88’) Mirallas has done well since coming on for Everton, he is adding a different dimension to this Everton side as they pile on the pressure. Still, the Saints defence clear any danger that comes their way.
(87’) Everton are certainly still in this game, but Southampton are doing everything to deny them an equalising goal and Everton need to be wary of a Saints counter-attack.
--- 84’ Yellow card Yellow card Ashley Williams ---
--- 84’ Substitution The 19-year-old receives a standing ovation as his comes off to be replaced by another Saints youngster Sam McQueen. ---
(84’) Everton are really piling on the pressure now, throwing everything at Southampton but the hosts are standing firm.
--- 83’ Substitution Third and final Toffees substitution as Baines sprints off to be replaced by Enner Valencia. ---
(80’) ANOTHER SAINTS CHANCE! Steklenburg pulls off a great save to deny Ward-Prowse from close range after another ball into the box by Cedric, and then Jagielka needs to clear the rebound off the line to prevent a second Southampton goal. The Everton is just about keeping his side in the game.
--- 79’ Substitution Saints make their first substitution of the game with Redmond coming off and Jordy Clasie replaces him. ---
--- 78’ Yellow card Yellow card Romelu Lukaku Menama ---
(77’) Now it is Southampton's turn to attack! Once again it is Sims who breaks down the right, he beats Baines and shoots at goal but it is blocked and Austin can't reach the rebound. Just seconds later Austin finds Ward-Prowse in a good position on the six-yard box after capitalising on a spill by the Everton goalkeeper, but Ward-Prowse puts his effort wide.
(76’) CLOSE! Everton are knocking on the door now! Baines swings a dangerous free-kick deep into the box which is almost met by Williams, but Saints just about clear the ball for a corner. The corner into the box is superbly headed away. Danger cleared.
(74’) Everton are certainly pushing more players forward now in an attempt to grab an equalising goal. It is now the visitors who are controlling possession and are threatening the Saints goal as we enter the final 15 minutes of the game.
(73’) Redmond tries his luck with a cheeky chip from the edge of the box after the pull back from Bertrand, but he gets it all wrong and it flies high and wide over the Everton net.
--- 71’ Substitution Another change by Everton as Barkley is replaced by Kevin Mirallas. ---
(68’) Sims does very well to beat three Everton players through his terrific pace down the right but he then appeared to be caught in two minds, he tries to play a ball across to Austin but it is intercepted. Perhaps he would've been better trying his luck with a shot a goal.
(66’) Southampton will all the possession at the moment, they are camped inside the Everton half trying to work an opening to goal.
--- 65’ Substitution Everton make their first substitution of the game with Lennon coming off to be replaced by Gerard Deulofeu. ---
(64’) CHANCE EVERTON! Forster pulls off a brilliant save to deny an acrobatic attempt by Bolasie, that would've been a great finish but the linesman has his flag up for offside so it wouldn't have counted anyway.
(61’) Sims has been outstanding for Southampton today, a great full first-team debut for the 19-year-old, constantly causing Baines problems down the left flank and linking well with Austin.
(58’) CHANCE SAINTS! It's end to end stuff here now at St Mary's. Austin comes incredibly close to doubling his tally for today and Saints lead. Cedric whips a excellent cross into the box from the right and Austin rises above Jagielka and fires a header towards the bottom corner but it is superbly saved by Steklenburg. Fantastic save.
(56’) CHANCE EVERTON! Lennon finds Bolasie, who shows the defender a clean pair of heels, but his fierce drive goes narrowly wide of Forster's post. Everton are getting closer.
(53’) Everton free-kick in a great position after Romeu clumsily brought down Gueye just outside the box. However Lukaku fires it well over the crossbar, it doesn't come close to troubling Forster.
(51’) Not the best start to the second half for Everton who really need to improve if they're to get back into this game. Perhaps a couple of changes are needed as Southampton look comfortable.
(49’) OFF THE POST! Saints almost double their lead immediately. Thanks for joining me for this afternoon's game, I hope you all enjoyed the action!
A major win for strugglers Sunderland who record their second win in as many games, and in some style to boot. Jermaine Defoe opened the scoring, with his 150th Premier League goal coming in the form of a wonderful individual effort. Victor Anichebe was the provider of the Black Cat's other two goals as the former Everton man capitalised on both the major chances that came his way. The Nigerian was unremarkable at times today and looks a different player to the one who struggled at West Brom last season. Hull City were by no means passengers in this game and may feel aggrieved not to have been awarded at least one penalty. They also came up against a goalkeeper in wonderful form, and Jordan Pickford was rewarded for his performance with a first clean sheet of the season.
FULL-TIME: Sunderland 3-0 Hull City
(90’) Elmohamady delivers a fine ball into the box in search of Mbokani, but Kone rises well to clear the ball.
(90’) Hull have by no means been turned over here today, but Sunderland have been clinical when it counted. This is a massive result for David Moyes and his team.
--- 89’ Red card! A mistimed challenge from Djilobodji sees the Senegalese defender pick up a rather unnecessary second yellow, taking the shine ever so slightly off this Sunderland win. ---
--- 88’ Substitution McNair goes down again holding his knee and he will have to make way now. Donald Love is his replacement. ---
--- 85’ Assist Defoe did well to hold the ball up and fizz the pass into Anichebe's feet. ---
--- 84’ Goal! GOOOAALL!!! ANICHEBE SECURES A SUNDERLAND WIN! Victor Anichebe has looked a man reborn today, as he grabs his second goal of the game. The big forward once again backs up his marker before spinning off to receive the ball. his touch is good and his finish is even better as he slams the ball past Marshall and in off the near post. Surely three points in the bag for David Moyes? ---
--- 83’ Substitution Denayer has been fairly solid in front of the back four today and he makes way for John O'Shea. ---
(81’) ANOTHER PENALTY APPEAL!!!! Mbokani slips the ball into the path of David Meyler who slams the ball goalwards. Djilobodji slides across and appears to have his elbow raised as he blocks the ball with his arm. Still no penalty!
(79’) AMAZING SAVE FROM PICKFORD! He reacts rapidly to get down low to Davies' header from a Hull corner. He can only tip the ball back into play and onto the head of Mbokani. The Hull striker loops the ball over the keeper but van Aanholt is on hand to clear off the line.
--- 78’ Substitution Mason makes way after a fairly anonymous turn in midfield. David Meyler is his replacement. ---
(76’) YET ANOTHER PENALTY APPEAL! Bowen breaks into the box beyond Jones and Jason Denayer. The winger looks to be beyond the pair but goes to ground and it looks like Jones has clipped his heels.
(75’) Defoe concedes posession in his own half and Hull drive forwards desperate to find a way back into the game. Clucas forces a throw-in.
--- 72’ Yellow card Jones dives in with a rash challenge on Clucas and deserves his yellow card. Studs showing and up on the ankle, that was not a nice tackle. ---
(69’) BIG PENALTY APPEAL FOR HULL! The ball makes its way to the left of Sunderland's box and into the path of Clucas. He takes it on and looks to be clipped by Paddy McNair, but once again Lee Mason waves it away.
--- 68’ Substitution An impressive debut for the 17 year old who has done very little wrong at left back today. Jarrod Bowen will move onto the left wing dropping Clucas into left back. ---
(67’) An ambitious attempt from Jake Livermore, who strikes from just inside the Sunderland half. Picford looked momentarily panicked and scampered across his box, but the ball bounces out for a goal kick.
(64’) FANTASTIC SAVE FROM THE OVERHEAD KICK! The ball bounces up at Sunderland's back post and Snodgrass adjusts his body brilliantly to twist and fire off a bicycle kick. The athleticism of the winger is matched only by that of Pickford who backpeddles and leaps up to touch the strike over the bar and keep his clean sheet in tact.
--- 62’ Assist Excellent work from the dutch right back, who plays a one-two with Watmore before finding Anichebe in the box. ---
--- 61’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALL!!! Another wonderful goal for Sunderland and this time it is the rejuvenated Victor Anichebe who gets his name on the score sheet. The Nigerian received the ball from van Aanholt just inside the box, shifted into space and fired past David Marshall to double Sunderland's lead. Perhaps the keeper should have done better but Sunderland worked that goal very well. ---
(59’) The Black Cats almost cut Hull open with some incisive passing. Kone finds van Aanholt who in turn looks for Defoe, but there is a mix up in communication as Defoe holds his run. Davies is left with time to clear.
(56’) It's been a fairly end-to-end second half so far with plenty of cut and thrust from both sides. Sunderland charge forward now, but the excellent Tymon is once again on hand to challenge Anichebe.
(54’) CHANCE! Jordan Pickford gets a let-off after his miskick lands at the feet of Mbokani. Hull sense a chance and surge forward with the ball finding the feet of Ryan Mason. The midfielder steadies himself but fluffs his strike which trickles wide.
(53’) Sunderland looking to extend their lead as Anichebe uses his size to pin the youngster Tymon. The Nigerian international twists and turns but cannot escape the Hull left back who gets his block in and concedes the corner.
(51’) A nice one-two between Livermore and Snodgrass allows the former Spurs midfielder to break into the box. His cross is cut out though, and there's a bit of a sly elbow thrown by Snodgrass in the direction of Watmore as Sunderland clear. The referee awards the host a free-kick.
(49’) Lee Mason is back with the ball under his arm and we're ready to get back to the action. The referee drops the ball at the feet of van Aanholt and the Dutchman boots it back to the Hull defence to get the game re-started.
(48’) Mason makes the call though and the players are headed back down the tunnel for what we hope is a brief interlude.
(48’) All eyes are on Lee Mason here as we await his decision. A voice from above confirms there has been a power cut and that the lights will be back on shortly.
(48’) BLACKOUT! A strange series of events here as the lights go out here at the Stadium of Light. Somebody's forgotten to put 50p on the meter!
(46’) BIG CHANCE FOR WATMORE! Anichebe finds space on the right and swings the ball in. Defoe flicks it on well and it looks like a tap in for Watmore at the far post. But he is denied by Marshall who scrambles across his line to block the strike with his chest.
(45’) Defoe rolls the ball back and the game is back on.
The players are out on the pitch and we're about to get back underway.
Hull City have done little wrong throughout the first half, and Mike Phelan may well argue his team had the better of the 45 minutes. But Jermaine Defoe has once again proved to be the difference for Sunderland, with the striker scoring his 150th league goal in great style. His individual effort separates the two teams, but some shaky defending from Kone and Djilobodji suggests there may be a way back into this game for Hull.
HALF-TIME: Sunderland 1-0 Hull City
(45’) McNair is back out on the pitch and finds Defoe in the Hull box. The striker pops the ball off to the onrushing Jones who forces an excellent last ditch challenge from Michael Dawson, who stops Sunderland extending their lead.
(45’) Elmohamady looks to catch Sunderland out with an early cross, but it causes Pickford no problems. The young keeper gathers the ball comfortably annd falls down upon it as the countdown to half-time begins.
(43’) Play comes to a halt while Paddy McNair receives treatment. The Northern Irishman looks to have sustained a painful knee injury off the ball after changing direction a bit too rapidly.

Early goals from Sam Vokes and Johann Berg Gudmundsson had the hosts cruising, but Palace substitute Conor Wickham pulled one back on the hour mark. Christian Benteke then levelled matters late on after Lowton gave away a penalty for handball, but Barnes snatched the points late on for the Clarets.
WHAT A GAME! Burnley secured a thrilling 3-2 win over Crystal Palace thanks to a late Ashley Barnes injury-time winner.
FULL-TIME: BURNLEY 3-2 CRYSTAL PALACE
(90’) PALACE HIT THE POST! Almost more late drama as Townsend hits the post from the edge of the box, so close by Palace!
--- 90’ +4 Goal! BURNLEY HAVE THE LEAD! What an incredible game! Burnley have come back and Barnes could have just scored the winning goal! Another goal from a counter-attack as the Clarets clear their lines from a Palace free-kick. The swift counter ends with the ball being played into the area for Barnes, who volleys the ball high into the back of the net. ---
(90’) There will be another five minutes of added time. Plenty of time for someone to grab a winning goal.
(89’) Palace are looking the far more dangerous side in the final moments of the this game. Can Burnley hang on to a point or will Palace round off a remarkable comeback?
--- 88’ Substitution Final Palace substitution sees James McArthur replaced by Joe Ledley. ---
--- 86’ Substitution Final substitution for Burnley sees Jeff Hendrick replaced by Ashley Barnes. ---
(84’) What a game this has been! There is still plenty of time left on the clock for either side to nick a winning goal, Palace are full of confidence now and look the most likely to score again.
--- 81’ Goal! BENTEKE CONVERTS! IT'S 2-2! A great penalty by Benteke, as he rolls the ball into the back of the net, sending Heaton the wrong way to level the scoreline for Palace. ---
(81’) PALACE PENALTY! What a chance for Palace to equalise! It was a blatant handball by Lowton in the box from Zaha's cross and the referee has no hesitation in awarding the spot-kick.
(80’) This is better from Burnley. They are starting to make progress up the pitch and have had a couple of free-kicks in decent areas to try and ease the pressure on themselves.
--- 78’ Yellow card Yellow card is awarded to Damien Delaney for tripping up George Boyd. ---
(77’) Nervous times here for Burnley, they are sitting very deep and that is allowing Palace to keep on moving forward and put the Clarets defence under huge amounts of pressure.
--- 74’ Substitution Second Burnley substitution of the game is a defensive one, as Steven Defour is replaced by defender James Tarkowski. ---
(73’) It's all Palace! Shot after shot is being fired at the Burnley goal, first through Benteke and then Cabaye, but the Burnley players a throwing their bodies in the way of these attempts and are just about keeping Palace out.
(71’) Mee and Keane are going to have to remain strong at the back here, especially with the added threat of having Wickham and Benteke both upfront now.
(69’) Burnley need to slow the pace of the game down and start passing the ball around with confidence again. We could be in store for a thrilling final 20 minutes.
(67’) The momentum is all in favour of the visitors now. The Burnley players don't look as confident as they did 10 minutes ago, and the crowd can sense that.
--- 65’ Substitution First Burnley substitution of the game is made by Sean Dyche, as Scott Arfield is replaced by George Boyd. ---
(64’) CHANCE PALACE! Another good piece of play down the right by Zaha, and his cross is met by Cabaye on the volley some 10 yards out, only for Mee to make a vital goal-saving block. Cabaye looked shocked to see that not hit the back of the net.
(62’) It is all Palace at the moment! The Burnley supporters have gone quiet and it is the away fans who are making all of the noise.
--- 60’ Goal! GAME ON! What a great substitution by Alan Pardew. Wickham has been on the pitch for less than a minute and he has pulled one back for Palace! It was a brilliant finish by the striker, with his first touch of the ball! The striker met Zaha's cross from the right with a sweetly struck volley that left Heaton with no chance, although there was a slight hint of offside. ---
--- 60’ Assist Wilfried Zaha has moved over to the right now, and it was his perfect cross into the box which was met by Wickham to pull one back for Palace. ---
--- 59’ Yellow card McArthur receives a yellow card for pulling Defour back and giving away the free-kick. ---
--- 59’ Substitution First change of the double substitution by Palace sees Martin Kelly replaced by Zeki Fryers. ---
--- 59’ Substitution The other substitution sees Jason Puncheon come off in replace of Connor Wickham. ---
(56’) Palace need to score soon if they are to get back into the game, and it looks like they are about to make a double substitution. The momentum is all in favour of Burnley at the moment, following Vokes' chance to add a third goal.
(54’) The atmosphere is electric here, the Burnley fans are creating a lot of noise as their team are putting on a great performance.
(51’) AND ANOTHER! Mandanda is called upon to keep out Vokes's shot at his near post, not once but twice from a close-range after Burnley again catch Palace out with another pacy counter.
(49’) CHANCE BURNLEY! Another good opportunity for Burnley to add a third goal here. Again it is Vokes with the chance, he shows good skill to beat a couple of Palace defenders on the edge of the box but he then pulls his shot narrowly wide of the goal.
(49’) With the likes of Townsend, Zaha and Benteke, Palace have a wealth of attacking talent and they could prove vital in this second half.
(47’) Despite the scoreline it has been a fairly even game here at Turf Moor. Two briliant counter-attacking goals from Burnley have given them the lead, meaning that Palace have a lot of work to do to get back into this game.
(46’) We're back underway here at Turf Moor. Can Palace get themselves back into the game?
HALF-TIME: BURNLEY 2-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
And that's half-time at Turf Moor, where Mandanda's mistake has contributed to the hosts taking a commanding 2-0 lead. Palace have plenty of work to do after the break if they are to turn this one around.
(40’) This game has been non-stop since we kicked off here at Turf Moor. Both sides have played the game at a terrific pace which has been great to watch.
(38’) CHANCE BURNLEY! Almost three for the Clarets! It was a great ball into the box by Arfield that was brilliantly taken down by Defour, he then lays the ball off to Hendrick but the Irish international takes too many touches and his shot is eventually blocked by the recovering Palace defenders.
(35’) STAT: Burnley are aiming to win back-to-back home games in the Premier League for the first time since they were last in the top division, seven years ago. They are certainly on track to repeat that feat today.
(33’) CHANCE PALACE! Townsend comes within inches of getting Palace back into the game. The wingers volley from the edge of the box goes narrowly wide of Heatons goal with the keeper rooted to the ground. A couple of inches the other way and that would've been in.
(32’) Ben Mee has been terrific for Burnley so far this afternoon, he has been solid at the heart of the Clarets defence, making vital tackles and headers to keep the visitors at bay.
(29’) Burnley are well on top at the moment, they're controlling possession and are looking likely to score a third against this Palace defence.
(26’) There could be more worries for Palace as it looks like centre-back Dann is limping, the skipper has struggled with injury in the past couple of weeks.
(24’) The visitors can't match their counterparts exploits as Townsend box into the box is a poor one and Heaton easily gathers. That was a good opportunity for Palace to pull one back.
(24’) First Burnley corner of the game. Up come the defenders from the back in an attempt to bag a third goal. The corner is a poor one and now Palace have a chance to break forward!
(21’) The England manager Gareth Southgate is here today, casting an eye over both sides. It is Burnley's English contingent have looked far more impressive so far.
(19’) STAT: Crystal Palace's 3-2 victory at Turf Moor in 2014/15 ended a run of seven trips there without a win in league competition. They need to score another three goals today to come away with a win.
(17’) Palace look shocked to be 2-0 down here! They have started the game well in an attacking sense but have been undone by two fantastic counter-attacks by Burnley! The Palace defence could've done better for both goals.
--- 14’ Assist The first goalscorer turns provider this time, it was his ball into the path of Gudmundsson that led to the second goal of the afternoon. ---
--- 14’ Goal! ANOTHER BURNLEY GOAL! It's come from another counter-attack as well! Burnley broke forward fast following the save by Heaton to deny Zaha. Guðmunds­son ran clear down the left-hand channel, and then fires a fierce shot at goal which beats Mandanda from just outside the box. The France keeper gets a hand to it, but just cannot keep out. ---
(14’) Great save by Heaton! Again you see another Palace threat. The Burnley skipper is in terrific form at the moment and he is at it again, making a brilliant close-range stop to keep out Zaha's stinging volley.
(11’) Both sides are battling for possession at the moment, Palace look dangerous going forward through Benteke, Zaha and Townsend but they will have to wary of another Burnley counter-attack.
--- 10’ Yellow card The first yellow card of the game goes to Dean Marney for a late challenge on Cabaye. ---
(7’) The goal by Vokes is his fourth goal of the season so far.
(5’) Palace look threatening going forward, as they try to get back into the game straight away. Puncheon has just shot from the edge of the box is well saved by Heaton down to his right.
--- 2’ Goal! WHAT A START! Sam Vokes has given Burnley the lead! The Clarets counter-attacked from the Palace corner through Gudmundsson, who plays the ball to Hendrick, he chips the ball to the unmarked Lowton at the far post who has a shot parried by Mandanda. Vokes is the quickest to react to the bouncing ball and he slots home from just a yard out. ---
(1’) Fast start by Palace! Andros Townsend is always a threat going forward and he does well to force a corner for his side within the first minute of the game. However the corner is a poor one and Burnley can clear and start a counter-attack of their own.

It wasn't quite as straight-forward as they would have liked, but Liverpool managed to get there in the end and deserved to pick up all three points. They were scintillating when attacking, with Firmino, Mane and, in particular, Coutinho all causing Palace plenty of problems, but at the back they were suspect to say the least, resulting in the home side constantly making life tough for them with a high balls into the box. They just about managed to hold on, however, and remain equal on points with Manchester City and Arsenal at the top of the table.
FULL-TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 2-4 LIVERPOOL
(90’) Puncheon and Campbell link up well midway inside the Liverpool half of the pitch before the latter sends a through-ball into the path of Benteke, but the striker is beaten to the ball by Klavan and the defender does well to poke the ball back to Karius before he can meet it.
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Mane has made way for Klavan in the final alteration of the night. ---

(87’) Palace win the ball back quickly and work it forward to Puncheon on the edge fo the penalty area. The substitute takes a quick touch before spinning and shooting, but there's slightly too much power behind the strike and it ends up clearing the crossbar.

He rises high and initially seems to do well to win the ball, but the referee isn't happy with a flailing arm that makes contact with Matip's neck and he awards a free-kick to the visitors, which the home fans aren't at all happy about.
(81’) Coutinho charges down the left flank on a marauding run before whipping a dangerous cross into the heart of the Palace box, but it's sent a few yards too far in front of Firmino and the goalscorer is unable to meet the ball in a good position in front of goal.
(79’) Great play by Coutinho! The Brazilian weaves his way through a group of Palace players as he penetrates the penalty area on a great run, but he's unable to beat Mandanda at the near post and instead sends his shot into the hands of the Frenchman.
(77’) The pace of the game has slowed down somewhat, and it's Liverpool who are controlling the game as they try to keep the ball as far away from Palace as possible. The home side look tired and have dropped off slightly, as that fourth goal seems to have killed their enthusiasm to get forward.

--- 74’ Substitution Palace have made another attacking alteration, with Puncheon coming on to take the place of Ledley. ---

--- 72’ Yellow card Firmino removes his shirt as he celebrates his side's latest goal and receives a yellow card as a result. ---
--- 71’ Assist That was a gorgeous pass from Henderson, who picked out Firmino perfectly, but questions have to be asked of the Palace centre-back's, who were out of position and failed to deal with the run forward from the Brazilian. ---

Well, what an exciting opening 45 minutes that has been! Both sides have looked incredibly open at the back, resulting in the two sets of attackers finding plenty of joy every time they push forward. All but one of the goals scored have come from headers, showing just how much trouble high balls into the box have been causing. As it stands, Liverpool head into the half-time break in front, but anything could end up happening in what is sure to be a fantastic second half.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
One of today’s most intriguing battles will be between Christian Benteke and a Liverpool defence that could struggle to deal with his strength and power. The former Reds striker flopped at Anfield but seems to be enjoying life in South London, where he has already scored three goals. He hasn’t yet managed to score at Selhurst Park, however, and would surely love to bag his first home goal against his former employers.
As for Palace, it’s been a relatively solid start to the campaign for them, and one that has seen them shake off the disappointment of finishing last season in such poor form. A wonderful September saw them win three consecutive games for the first time since April 2015, but since then it’s been slightly tougher for the Eagles, who are now without a victory in their previous three encounters.
Seven of those 10 unbeaten games have come in the Premier League, and during that time Liverpool have bagged an impressive 16 goals. Jurgen Klopp’s men have also looked far more solid at the back than they did last season, resulting in no side managing to score more than one goal against them in a league game since Burnley won 2-0 in August.
For the first time since the frantic and action-packed 2013-14 season, people are starting to talk about Liverpool being legitimate title contenders. The Reds have enjoyed a wonderful start to the season, and they head into today’s clash unbeaten in their last 10 games and with a chance to move equal on points with both Manchester City and Arsenal once again if they’re victorious.

Leicester extend their unbeaten home run in the Premier League thanks to goals from Ahmed Musa, Shinji Okazaki and Christian Fuchs. Yohan Cabaye pulled one back for Palace late on but Alan Pardew’s side struggled to get into the game until the final ten minutes and suffer their second straight league defeat.
Full-time: Leicester City 3-1 Crystal Palace
(90’) WHAT A SAVE FROM MANDANDA!! Leicester break away and Vardy finds Mahrez with just the goalkeeper to beat 12 yards out, but Mahrez tries to place the ball rather than blast it and the French keeper leaps to his right to keep the score at 3-1.
(90’) Palace are throwing everything at Leicester now and Benteke brings down a Cabaye corner 12 yards out from goal and shoots on the turn, but Leicester throw several bodies in the way to block the effort.
(90’) Four minutes of added time will be played.
(88’) Leicester break quickly on the counter attack through Vardy and Okazaki who then finds Mahrez on the right, but having cut inside onto his favoured left foot the winger fires high over the bar.
--- 87’ Substitution Andy King is down with a knock and Ranieri isn't willing to take any risks and brings Daniel Amartey on in his place. ---
--- 85’ Goal! GOOOAAALLL!!! PALACE PULL ONE BACK!! Zaha shows clever footwork and a sharp turn of pace to get down the outside of Fuchs and put a cross in towards Cabaye at the near post, who turns the ball across Schmeichel and into the far corner! ---
--- 85’ Assist Zaha has looked as threatening as anyone in a Palace shirt today and showed a wonderful bit of skill to get away from Fuchs before getting the cross away. ---
(83’) HUGE CHANCE FOR BENTEKE!! Zaha plays a lovely through ball into the path of Benteke who runs clean through on goal but can only strike the ball straight into the chest of Schmeichel who came quickly off his line to close the Belgian down well.
--- 81’ Substitution Claudio Ranieri is making another change now and Ahmed Musa is given a standing ovation by the home crowd as he's replaced by Demarai Gray. ---
--- 80’ Goal! GOOAAAALLLLL!!! WHAT A GOAL FROM FUCHS!!!! Benteke gets up well at the near post to head away a Mahrez corner, but the clearance goes straight into the path of the left-back who hits a ferocious first time volley into the bottom corner from 25 yards out. ---
--- 77’ Substitution Alan Pardew is making his third and final change now as Martin Kelly is replaced by Zeki Fryers. ---
--- 75’ Substitution The first change of the game for Leicester sees Islam Slimani replaced by Jamie Vardy. ---
(74’) OFF THE LINE!! Benteke gets his head to the resultant corner and headers the ball downwards towards the left hand corner, but Simpson is there to clear the ball off the line and out of danger!
(74’) HUGE CHANCE FOR CABAYE!! Zaha puts in a low cross towards Cabaye at the near post who misses the ball completely with his first effort before it bounces off Huth and back into the path of the Frenchman, but he can only volley straight at Schmeichel from six yards out!
--- 72’ Substitution Alan Pardew is making a double change now in an attempt to get back into this game as Frazier Campbell and Lee Chung-yong come on in place of Andros Townsend and Joe Ledley. ---
--- 72’ Substitution Substitution Joe Ledley Chung-Yong Lee ---
(70’) Musa wins the ball back after a poor pass from Ward inside his own half, but the winger's first touch is too heavy and Ledley is able to get a toe in and roll the ball back towards Mandanda to prevent the counter attack.
(67’) Chance for Zaha! The winger gets down the outside of Fuchs inside the Leicester area and fires a fierce shot on goal from a tight angle which Schmeichel has to turn behind for a corner. Palace force a repeat set of corners but Schmeichel comes out to catch the second with ease.
(66’) Leicester look happy to let Palace have the ball now and are defending with everyone but Slimani behind the ball.
--- 63’ Goal! GOOAAALLLLLLLL!!! OKAZAKI MAKES IT 2-0!! Drinkwater plays a low driven cross towards Slimani at the back post after Michael Oliver had played a superb advantage following a foul on Musa. Delaney intercepts the cross on the stretch but can only divert the ball into the path of Okazaki who drills the ball into the near corner from 12 yards out. ---
(60’) Referee Oliver awards Palace a free-kick for a foul on Zaha, much to the displeasure of the home fans who greet the decision with a loud chorus of boos.
(55’) Zaha does well to draw a free-kick from King close to the right hand corner flag. Townsend puts the resultant cross into a superb area and the ball is allowed to bounce on the edge of the six yard box but there are no Palace players on the end of it and Leicester scramble the ball clear.
(52’) Musa once again looks to use his pace to break forward into the Palace half, but Ledley brings him down from behind and referee Oliver awards the home side a free-kick close to the centre circle. Drinkwater takes it but it's comfortably headed clear by Delaney.
(49’) First half chance of the second half for Palace as Townsend picks out James Tomkins at the back post with a deep inswinging corner, but the centre-back is going away from goal and Schmeichel can safely watch his header go out for a goal kick.
(48’) CLOSE FROM SLIMANI! Simpson finds space for a cross right next to the corner flag on the right and picks out Slimani who's unmarked at the near post, but the striker can only direct his header into the side netting. The Leicester fans behind the goal thought that was in when they saw the net ripple.
(47’) Leicester starting the second half in the same manner in which they finished the first as Okazaki is fouled by Ward close to halfway. Mahrez launches the free-kick towards Slimani but Mandanda does well to come off his line and punch clear.
(46’) Kick-off! The home side get us underway in the second half, with neither side having made any changes at the break.
Palace started the brighter of the two sides and dominated the opening quarter of an hour, and Alan Pardew will know that if his side can get back to that level in the second half and keep providing good service up towards Benteke then his side are more than capable of getting back into this game.
Ahmed Musa's first goal in English football has given Claudio Ranieri's side a deserved half-time lead here at the King Power Stadium after Christian Benteke hit the bar earlier on with Palace's only clear cut chance of the half.
Half-time: Leicester City 1-0 Crystal Palace
(45’) One minute of added time will be played.
(45’) Slimani showing his confidence now as he has an ambitious shot on goal from 35 yards out but the ball goes high over the bar and into the stands.
--- 42’ Assist Slimani held the ball up superbly well with defenders surrounding him before laying the ball into the path of Musa. ---
--- 42’ Goal! GOOOAAAALLLLLLLLL!!!! MUSA GETS HIS FIRST LEICESTER GOAL! Musa drives towards the Palace penalty box from the half way line and plays the ball into Slimani who has his back to goal. Slimani exchanges passes with Okazaki before returning the ball to Musa who drills the ball into the right hand corner from the edge of the box. ---
(40’) The tables have turned completely from the opening 20 minutes here with Benteke now looking extremely isolated as the lone striker whenever he gets the ball.
(38’) The ball breaks to Drinkwater 30 yards out from goal and he drives forwards with Delaney backing off ahead of him, but with support arriving Drinkwater stumbles over the ball and loses control allowing Delaney to recover and clear the ball towards Benteke.
(35’) CLOSE FROM OKAZAKI! Mahrez cuts inside Kelly and onto his favoured left foot just inside the Palace area and shoots. His well struck effort looks to be heading towards the far corner but Okazaki gets his head to it and looks to divert the ball towards the near post but can only turn it just over the bar!
(34’) Michael Oliver does this time award Leiceser a free-kick for a foul on King by Benteke, which is greeted by ironic cheers from the home fans.
(32’) The home crowd at the King Power cry for a free-kick as Mahrez is crowded out by Ward and McArthur close to the corner flag but referee Oliver waives play on. Mahrez's influence on this game is certainly growing.
(29’) Mahrez whips in another dangerous corner from the left and this time Slimani does get his head to it, but can't get over the top of it and Mandanda watches it sail over his bar.
(26’) Leicester have suddenly got a foothold in this game and Delaney has to be on his toes to head clear a Mahrez corner with Huth and Slimani lurking behind him.
(25’) Mahrez goes on an outstanding run down the right and gets past Kelly with ease before driving into the box but there's no one on the end of his cross and Ward can hack the ball clear.
(24’) Leicester make a rare break forward and Musa gets a cross in towards Slimani from the left hand edge of the box, but the striker is under pressure from both centre-backs and can only loop his header straight up into the air making it easy for Mandanda to gather.
(22’) Townsend once again has plenty of space to whip in a left footed cross from the right hand touchline towards Benteke, but this time Morgan gets his head to it first to clear the danger. Claudio Ranieri won't be too happy with the amount of time and space Palace are getting out wide here.
(19’) Leicester are really struggling to get out of their own half here as referee Michael Oliver gives Musa a talking for a foul a few moments earlier on Joe Ledley. Musa perhaps lucky to escape a yellow card as it was a pretty late challenge.
(17’) Townsend gets down the outside of the Leicster defence on the right and pulls a deflected cross back towards Benteke on the penalty spot, but King does well to get his head to the ball and prevent the Palace striker getting an effort on goal.
(15’) Palace are finding their feet in this game now and the ball this time breaks to Townsend on the edge of the box, but the winger is off balance as he shoots and his effort goes high over the bar.
(13’) OFF THE BAR!! Benteke gets his head to a superb inswinging cross from Martin Kelly from the left, but can only divert his header onto the bar with Schmeichel well beaten!
(10’) Zaha gets on the ball in a dangerous area on the left hand side and cuts inside onto his right foot just inside the area, but Wes Morgan throws himself in front of the low driven shot.
(9’) Riyad Mahrez drifts infield to try and get into the game and is fouled by Joe Ledley inside the centre circle, much to the frustration of the Palace midfielder who doesn't look too pleased with that decision.
(6’) Palace's first real venture into the Leicester half sees Wilfried Zaha find Yohan Cabaye with space to shoot 25 yards out from goal, but his well struck effort is always curving the wrong way and goes wide of Schmeichel's left hand post.
(5’) Islam Slimani links up well with Andy King inside the Palace half and feeds Musa on the left hand edge of the Palace area, but Joel Ward tracks back well to make the tackle and clear the danger.
(2’) Chance for Okazaki!! Steve Mandanda makes a horrible mess of a clearing kick and the ball goes straight to Shinji Okazaki just outside the penalty box, but his attempted lob balloons wide of the goal with Mandanda stranded 12 yards out from his goal.

FULL-TIME! Man City drop points in the Premier League during successive matchdays, with a goal from Lukaku frustrating the hosts at the Etihad. Nolito grabbed an equaliser, but Stekelenburg was the hero, with two penalty saves ensuring that Koeman's men left with a share of the spoils. That's all that we have time for, we hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Fernandinho lifts a cross in towards Kompany, but the Belgian defender can only flick a header straight out of play for a goal-kick. The substitute is being used up top as a target man for the dying embers of this contest.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution Cleverley is withdrawn for the away side, with Funes Mori adding into the mix as an extra defender by Koeman. ---
(90’) There are four minutes of stoppage time. Stekelenburg is forced to make a simple catch, following a flicked header from Kompany.
--- 90’ Substitution Gundogan is replaced by Kompany, who gets a great reception from the home fans. ---
(89’) Nolito tries to cut a cross back from the right byline, but Williams makes a good interception. Mirallas is then penalised for a tug on Fernandinho's shirt, with Everton desperately trying to scrape their way through the next few minutes unscathed.
(87’) Anywhere will do for Everton at the moment, with Lukaku being left alone up top to try and lead counter-attacks. Aguero tries to flick a pass around the corner for Nolito to chase, but Jagielka makes an interception. Moments later, Aguero is found by a De Bruyne pass, with Oviedo appearing to push his man, but the referee isn't interested.
--- 85’ Yellow card Williams now picks up a caution for a foul, which gifts Man City yet another opportunity to fill the box. ---
--- 84’ Substitution Bolasie is replaced by Mirallas, as the visitors try to freshen things up. ---
(84’) Gundogan drives down the left, but Coleman comes across to slide in and make a great tackle. Everton are on the back foot yet again, with Koeman's men sat deep and looking to frustrate.
(82’) GREAT SAVE FROM STEKELENBURG! The Netherlands international gets up brilliantly to push a thunderbolt from De Bruyne onto the post and wide! Unbelievable stuff, his opponent thought that was certainly a goal!
--- 81’ Yellow card Coleman picks up the first booking of the evening. ---
(80’) De Bruyne is fouled by Barry, meaning that Man City have another chance to whip a ball into a box loaded with bodies. This time, however, with both coaches patrolling their technical areas, the pressure is building. Everton clear with ease via Jagielka.
(78’) A mix-up at the back for the hosts means that Lukaku nearly has a chance to steal in behind, but Fernandinho steps in at a vital moment. Narrowly over 10 minutes remain in this contest at the Etihad.
(76’) Sterling wastes another half-chance for the home side, as Guardiola's men look to try and force a second goal of the evening. Lukaku and Bolasie try to combine on the break for Everton, but a mistimed pass from the former betrays his team-mate.
(74’) De Bruyne is found down the left-hand side, but his eventual cross in from out wide is caught easily by Stekelenburg. Man City only have 20 minutes to find a winner, so they can't afford to be wasteful in front of goal.
--- 72’ Assist Silva bends in a good cross from the left-hand side. ---
--- 72’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! NOLITO MAKES IT 1-1! The substitute has barely been on the pitch, but grabs the all-important goal! He directs a firm header into the bottom-left corner with basically his first touch. ---
--- 71’ Substitution Sane takes his leave after a bright first-half showing faded slightly, with Nolito coming into the fray. ---
--- 70’ Missed penalty Penalty Miss Sergio Leonel Agüero del Castillo ---
(70’) PENALTY TO MAN CITY! Jagielka gives away his second of the afternoon and he looks like he wants the ground to swallow him up. A mistimed challenge on Aguero gives the hosts a chance to equalise.
(70’) Penalty Save Maarten Stekelenburg
(68’) Silva wins yet another corner for the home side, but Williams heads clear of the danger zone, before hoofing another cross away moments later. Cleverley is released forward on the break, but plays backwards to slow the game down a little.
(66’) Lukaku tries to cause problems down the right yet again, but Clichy stands up to the Everton goalscorer well. Sterling tries to escape from Gueye and Oviedo down the right-hand side, but the latter sticks out an important leg to deny the former Liverpool wide man.
--- 64’ Assist Bolasie slots an inviting pass down the line for Lukaku to chase. ---
--- 64’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! LUKAKU MAKES IT 1-0! The Belgium international is fed down the left-hand side and races into the penalty box, before slotting a low finish across Bravo and into the bottom-right corner. ---
(64’) Sane bends in a cross from the left, but Stekelenburg claims with ease. Jagielka is then forced to make another rushed clearance within his six-yard box, with a clearance releasing Lukaku forward on the counter.
(62’) Sterling shows an unbelievable turn of pace to get in behind Oviedo and drive into the box, but a cross from the Englishman is then denied by some good defending from Jagielka. If Everton push on too much, Man City are able to cause plenty of problems in behind.
(61’) Gundogan drives into space on the edge of the penalty area, before exchanging a one-two with Silva, but the former can't take the ball back under his spell. Aguero then tees up Fernandinho on the periphery of the box, but a cross from the Brazilian is blocked.
(59’) Sterling drives to the right byline and cuts back a cross, but Williams is once again there to concede a corner. Everton haven't taken any chances at the back today. The resulting set-piece finds Otamendi at the near post, but Jagielka gets in ahead of the Argentine - before shoving the ex-Valencia defender to the floor during the next passage of play.
--- 57’ Substitution Deulofeu takes his leave, with McCarthy injected into the fray to shore up the midfield. ---
--- 56’ Substitution Iheanacho is replaced by Aguero for the home side, showing that Guardiola's men really do mean business this afternoon. ---
(56’) Sane breaks down the right-hand side, before getting into the box and drilling in a low cross, but Williams turns a clearance behind for a corner. De Bruyne delivers, but Man City fail to cause any problems, with Fernandinho eventually placing a terrible pass straight out of play for a goal-kick.
(55’) Bolasie races forward at pace and tries to slot a through-ball into Lukaku's path, but the pass is too heavy and Bravo collects. Sterling is found on the right-hand side, but a flicked header from Silva only finds the Everton goalkeeper.
(53’) Iheanacho is picked out by a great cross from the left-hand side by Silva, but the Nigerian striker is only able to flick an improvised finish straight at Stekelenburg! Man City go close again, but the opening goal of the contest is proving elusive.
(51’) Bolasie finds Deulofeu on the left-hand side, with the former Barcelona winger cutting infield onto his stronger right foot. He shoots with power, but his dipping effort is palmed over the crossbar comfortably by Bravo. Jagielka heads the resulting corner wide of the target.
(50’) Coleman breaks down the right and tries to feed a pass into Lukaku, but Fernandinho makes a timely interception. De Bruyne tries to lead the charge and dance beyond Gueye, but the ex-Aston Villa midfielder robs the Belgian of possession brilliantly.
(48’) Stones makes the first important intervention of the second half, sliding in to deny a cross from the left by Bolasie. Man City try to cause problems on the counter, but a header from Sane is blocked with ease.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at the Etihad! De Bruyne was unable to break the deadlock from the spot, but Guardiola's men still have 45 minutes to make their dominance count.
HALF-TIME! Both sides go in goalless at the interval, with De Bruyne denied by Stekelenburg from the penalty spot late on! Man City have had all of the chances, with Sane causing all kinds of issues down the right-hand side. Plenty of time to find the back of the net yet!
(45’) There are two minutes of stoppage time in this first half.
--- 43’ Missed penalty De Bruyne puts his effort at a good height for the ex-Fulham goalkeeper to save. ---
(43’) Penalty Save Maarten Stekelenburg
(42’) PENALTY TO MAN CITY! Silva dances into the area, but Jagielka is present yet again to make a good block. However, the England defender is then penalised for sticking out a leg and tripping the Spain international.
(40’) Otamendi tries to lift a cross in from the right, but his cross is far too close to Stekelenburg, who claims. Only five minutes remain in this first half, with Everton continuing to try and tinker and set themselves up to prevent this free-flowing football from the hosts.
(38’) Bolasie races down the left, and bends in a low cross, but Stones makes a timely interception ahead of Lukaku. The ex-Toffees defender has looked solid against his former employers so far.
(36’) De Bruyne tries to flight in a cross from the left, but it can only find Silva on the edge of the area. Iheanacho dances around two defenders, but can't open up the space required for a shot. Neat, tidy stuff from the hosts, but clear-cut chances are proving elusive, with another Sane delivery deflected to safety by a combination of Williams and Gueye.
(34’) Williams flies into a full-bodied challenge on Sane, as Everton continue to try and assert themselves in this match. Man City are playing neat, two-touch stuff, but the away side are camped comfortably on the edge of their penalty area for now.
(32’) Sane continues to be the main outlet for this Man City side, with Deulofeu being asked to track right back to help out his left-back. Everton's breaks have become much more irregular, with Koeman probably happy to try and close out this half without conceding.
(30’) There is a stoppage in play, as Sterling goes down heavily, with the physios called on following a horrible high tackle from Coleman. The Republic of Ireland international flew in, planting his studs onto the ankle of his opponent. Terrible challenge.
(28’) Sane uses his pace to hurtle down the right flank, with Iheanacho and Silva then combining to give De Bruyne a chance to shoot. The former Chelsea midfielder rattles an effort straight at Oviedo's chest. That might have winded the Costa Rica international a bit!
(27’) Iheanacho tries to turn and shoot on the edge of the penalty area, but the Nigerian striker loses his footing. Man City then break upfield with intent, as De Bruyne tees up Silva, but the Spaniard can't keep his strike down and watches the ball rise over the bar.
(25’) Man City win a corner on the left, but Lukaku does his defensive duty well to head clear. Everton try to lead a break as a result, but Clichy snuffs out a run from Bolasie. Koeman's men are getting deeper and deeper, with Bravo having an early first-half outing thus far.
(23’) Silva is released to the left byline, but Jagielka does brilliantly to make a tidy block. Everton keep their pressure on, before Sterling is felled by a scrappy challenge from Cleverley. The ex-Valencia midfielder finds Iheanacho with the free-kick delivery, but the Nigeria international can't head goalwards.
(21’) Man City play some lovely expansive football to release Sterling down the left, but the ex-Liverpool winger can only cut inside and shoots straight at Stekelenburg. Guardiola will be pleased that his players have currently held the upper hand against his former Barcelona mentor. All of the chances are falling the home side's way.
(19’) De Bruyne shoots into the wall from the resulting free-kick, with Sane then able to win a corner with a deflected header moments later. The aforementioned Belgian midfielder tries to whip a cross towards Stones at the back post, but his ball sails over the England international's head. Sane is causing havoc down this right flank.
(17’) Iheanacho is thwarted by Jagielka, after a good ball was drilled in from the left-hand side, with Man City then able to win a free-kick on the edge of the box following a foul on Sterling by Barry. Everton's defending is getting quiet desperate, and we're less than 20 minutes into the action.
(15’) Over from De Bruyne! Oviedo does just enough to deflect a shot from the ex-Wolfsburg midfielder above the crossbar, with the resulting corner sent off-target by Fernandinho. The pressure is building on the Toffees.
(13’) Oviedo is forced to slide in and deny Sane a goalscoring opportunity, with a last-ditch interception that stops the German from getting behind and into the clear. The home side are creating all of the dangerous opportunities so far.
(11’) De Bruyne finds Sane on the right yet again, with the Germany international able to get beyond Oviedo yet again! The youngster goes down, claiming a penalty, but the referee isn't interested. Everton half-clear, with Fernandinho picking up the scraps, but the Brazilian sees a shot blocked, before a second delivery from Sane fails to find Sterling at the back post.
(9’) Otamendi gives away a free-kick in a dangerous area, which gives Lukaku a chance to test Bravo for the first time today. The Belgium international lines up a shot, but bends the ball high and wide of the target, picking out the stands rather than the back of the net.
(8’) Deulofeu is found by a hopeful ball down the line, with the Spaniard then able to swing in a cross from the byline. Lukaku rises highest, but the ex-Chelsea striker can't direct a header goalwards. Everton keep their pressure on, with Bolasie able to put another delivery into the area, but Stones clears.
(7’) Everton respond with a break down the right, but a cross from Bolasie is cut out easily by Fernandinho. Already, the pace in both of these sides is making for some end-to-end action. Deulofeu tries to combine with Lukaku moments later, but an errant pass from the ex-Sevilla winger fails to find its target. Man City respond with a counter, but Jagielka slides in to clear a dangerous ball in. All-action start in Manchester!
(5’) Man City are dominating possession from the off, with Sane found out on the right again. The ex-Schalke man leaves Oviedo bamboozled and dances into the penalty area, before forcing Stekelenburg into an easy save at his near post. From the resulting corner, the hosts fail to cause any problems, with Silva then penalised for a foul on the edge of the area.
(3’) De Bruyne fizzes in a low cross from the right-hand side, but Williams scrambles a close-range clearance away from the danger zone. Sane has already looked bright down the right-hand side, and will be looking to impress on his first Premier League start.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Etihad! Man City and Everton both want to get back on track this afternoon, after suffering some poorer results in recent weeks.

Everton starting line-up (4-3-3): Stekelenburg; Coleman, Jagielka, Williams, Oviedo; Barry, Gueye, Cleverley; Deulofeu, Lukaku, Bolasie.
Man City substitutes: Kompany, Zabaleta, Fernando, Nolito, Aguero, Kolarov, Caballero.

TEAM NEWS: Bryan Oviedo gets a rare start at left-back, with no other big surprises in the back four for Koeman's side. Gareth Barry and Idrissa Gueye offer industry in midfield, with Tom Cleverley bound to get a little further forward. Gerard Deulofeu and Yannick Bolasie offer pace on the break, and will be key to feeding lone striker Romelu Lukaku.
TEAM NEWS: Kevin De Bruyne makes a miraculous comeback from injury to start in midfield, with Kelechi Iheanacho flanked by Raheem Sterling and Leroy Sane. Ilkay Gundogan and Fernandinho are sitting in defensive midfield, leaving De Bruyne and Silva to drift into pockets of space in advanced areas. Gael Clichy, Nicolas Otamendi and ex-Toffees defender John Stones make up a back three.
Everton still find themselves in the top five of the league, but need to get some momentum going before their form slips into complete mediocrity. Man City are on the hunt for another three points, as their loss last time out has left Spurs' only one point off the title race.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Manchester City and Everton, as two of the league's high fliers meet at the Etihad. Pep Guardiola's men will want to bounce back from a 2-0 defeat to Spurs last time out, while the Toffees are on a three-game run without a win in the Premier League.
