(90’) STAT FLASH - There have now been eight yellow cards in this match – the joint most seen in a Premier League match this season alongside Middlesbrough v Stoke and Spurs v Liverpool.
(90’) Top-class defending from Delaney, who has been immense tonight. Twice he beats Jagielka to the ball, and twice Palace escape from danger.
(90’) We’re into stoppage time now at Goodison, and Everton have a corner. Mirallas will take it...
--- 88’ Yellow card It’s a late, crunching tackle from Bolasie, who picks up a yellow card against his former club after diving in on Ward. The winger did get the ball, but caught the man afterwards. ---
(87’) Another opportunity now for the hosts, as Coleman gets free and lofts in a cross. Cleverley is racing on to meet it, but Tomkins times his header perfectly, with Funes Mori unable to gather in the rebound.
(85’) Bolasie hammers in a low cross that rebounds up into the path of the onrushing Coleman, who dives in head-first, half-expecting a foul from Kelly, but the ex-Liverpool defender had pulled out of the challenge.
(84’) Everton have simply not stopped Palace’s crosses at source so far, with Jagielka and Williams having been bombarded with delivery after delivery into the area. Just under 10 minutes to go now...
(82’) MISS! Brilliant from Lukaku, who flicks on a sublime pass to Coleman, but the Republic of Ireland skipper cannot direct his strike on target.
--- 81’ Substitution A second substitution in quick-sucesion for Everton - Bryan Oviedo making way for Ramiro Funes Mori. ---
--- 79’ Substitution A change for Palace now, as before Townsend has chance to take the free-kick, Yohan Cabaye replaces James McArthur. ---
--- 78’ Yellow card Huge jeers now from the Goodison faithful, as referee Moss deems Gueye’s challenge on Townsend worthy of a booking. It’s a harsh call, to say the least... ---
--- 77’ Substitution A first change of the game now, as Kevin Mirallas replaces Ross Barkley. The home side really need to step up their attacking intent now. ---
(76’) CHANCE! Slack play from Everton as, after Jagielka clears initially, their defenders allow Tomkins time and room to get free in the area, but his header is well saved by Stekelenburg.
(75’) Palace are winning every second ball at the moment, and are looking bang on form at the moment, winning corner after corner...
(72’) Everton twice fail to clear their lines, allowing Townsend to loft in another cross, but Stekelenburg does well to come out and punch it clear. The hosts are really struggling here!
(71’) Zaha does well here, winning a free-kick on the right-hand side of the area. Palace have looked so threatening from crosses, and now Puncheon will deliver another one...
(70’) Townsend’s effort is poor, but Palace maintain the pressure. Puncheon manages to pick up possession close to the area, but Barry does well to usher the ball towards his goalkeeper.
--- 68’ Yellow card A real chance now for Palace, with Townsend having been scythed down by Barry 30 yards out. The Everton man picks up a booking for his troubles. ---
--- 67’ Yellow card Townsend has picked up a caution now, this time for a tug on the shirt of Barkley. ---
(67’) OFF THE LINE! So close for Everton, as Barry nods Barkley’s corner goal-wards, but Puncheon is on hand at the back post to hook it clear.
(65’) STAT FLASH -Since Benteke’s PL debut in September 2012, only Olivier Giroud (also 19) has scored as many headed goals in the Premier League as Benteke.
(64’) Everton have managed to get something of a foothold on proceedings now, but Palace look a real threat going forward. Koeman has options on the bench, and really could do with making a change sooner rather than later.
(62’) Chance! Townsend whips in a delightful cross, but Zaha cannot take the ball under his spell. Meanwhile, it has come to light that Palace’s second goal was ruled-out due to a movement towards the ball from McArthur, who was in an offside position when Delaney made contact with his header.
(60’) CLOSE! An audacious effort from Bolasie now, who latches onto the end of Gueye’s floated cross with an acrobatic attempt, but his volley sails wide.
(58’) Well, it isn’t a goal, with Moss sticking by his assistant’s call. However, it appears as though it may have been the incorrect one. Either way, Everton survive, but they are under severe pressure at the moment.
(57’) IS IT A GOAL!? Delaney has headed in, but the linesman has flagged for offside. However, Jon Moss has now gone over to speak with his assistant…
(55’) Palace are really on the front foot now, with Everton pinned back somewhat. Coleman will be fuming with his side, who are allowing Townsend and Zaha too much space down the flanks, with Benteke looking on top form now.
--- 52’ Yellow card Benteke has picked up a booking, though it is not yet clear what the Belgian - who now has five goals in six appearences against Everton - has been cautioned for. ---
(51’) WHAT A CHANCE! Great work from Bolasie, who gets down the left and slides a perfect pass into the feet of Gueye, but the former Aston Villa man cannot apply the finish despite being presented with what was almost an open net.
--- 50’ Assist Barkley's decision to go short from the free-kick merely put Everton on the back foot, but Palace's attack was well-worked, with Ward putting in a great cross for Benteke to get on the end of. ---
--- 50’ Goal! GOOOOOALLLL!!! AND BENTEKE MAKES EVERTON PAY! Well, that goal can all be pinned back to Everton conceding the ball from their own free-kick, as Palace work a move forward before crossing into Benteke, who powers a sublime header into the left-hand corner. ---
(49’) Another opportunity now for Everton to get the ball into the box, as Oviedo is felled by McArthur. However, Barkley elects to go short and the hosts only end up losing possession. That’s a poor decision by Everton’s playmaker.
(47’) There haven’t been any changes for either side at the interval, and Koeman will be looking for his Everton side to quickly turn on the style as they look to seal the win.
(46’) Welcome back! Palace have got the second-half underway! Pardew’s side, who were 2-0 down against Sunderland last week before coming back to win 3-2, have come from behind to win in two successive Premier League matches just once before - January 2015.
Palace have played well, though, and will not be downcast about their chances of picking up a result this evening. However, they must look to get Christian Benteke more involved in the final third.
It has been a closely-fought, but entertaining, affair at Goodison Park so far, with Romelu Lukaku’s sublime free-kick having put the hosts ahead. However, there is some debate as to whether it should not have been a foul the other way, with Phil Jagielka appearing to inadvertently handle the ball under pressure from Damien Delaney.
HALF-TIME! Barkley takes the free-kick, but is a poor one, and referee Moss quickly sounds his whistle. At the break, it is Everton 1-0 Crystal Palace.
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card And they may well have the chance to do just that, with Bolasie drawing Ledley into a clumsy foul. Tomkins doesn’t agree with the decision, and is duly booked for dissent. ---
(45’) Despite Everton’s goal, Palace still look a threat, with the long passes into Benteke proving particularly effective. However, the hosts are moving urge all around nicely, looking to double their tally before the interval.
(42’) Superb last-ditch defending from Coleman, who gets back to prevent Benteke latching onto Ward’s diagonal. Everton quickly kick-start a counter, with Cleverley eventually drilling a pass into the feet of Barkley, who in turn feeds it into the onrushing Coleman, with Kelly well-placed to make the intervention.
(40’) Lukaku has now netted four goals in his last five top-flight appearances against Palace. Only Tim Cahill and Duncan ferguson have scored more Premier League goals for Everton than the Belgian.
(38’) STAT FLASH - That was Lukaku's 65th Premier League goal but the first to have come from a direct free-kick.
(36’) A hint of controversy about that opener, perhaps, as Jagielka clearly handled the ball during that earlier collision with Delaney. However, it was purely instinctive from Everton’s skipper, who was running the risk of a kick straight to the face. Palace may well feel aggrieved, though.
--- 35’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLL!!!!! LUKAKU FIRES HOME THE FREE-KICK! What a strike from the Everton forward! He gets his free-kick up and over the wall, but the effort is flat enough to leave Mandanda helpless as it nestles into the back of the net. ---
(34’) Dangerous play from Delaney, who is penalised for a high-boot in the face of Jagielka, who had made a lung-bursting run to the edge of Palace’s area. Barkley and Lukaku are stood over the ball.
(33’) Good defending from Oviedo, as he denies Zaha getting a cross in. The corner duly comes in, with Stekelenburg flapping at the ball - though referee Moss quickly signals that Everton’s goalkeeper had been fouled by McArthur.
(31’) Palace have been impressive so far, as Pardew’s slide have worked their way into this game, with Townsend and Zaha offering plenty of threat from either flank. Everton have just eased off the pressure somewhat, however, and Koeman will be looking for his side to up the tempo again sharply.
(29’) The corner routine is a peculiar one, with Barkley picking out Coleman on the edge of the area. The full-back dummies to his right before switching onto his weaker left, but his resulting effort flashes well wide.
(28’) Barkley’s cross is a good one, but Palace clear it. Barry latches onto the loose ball, threading it through to Coleman, but Tomkins is over to make the block.
--- 26’ Yellow card A free-kick for Everton now, as Lukaku is brought down by McCarthur. Though it is Puncheon who goes into the book, albeit for dissent. ---
(24’) BLOCKED! Townsend drives the free-kick straight into the wall, with Coleman quickly out to regain possession for Everton and set Bolasie away. The forward bursts through Palace’s retreating ranks, but rather than going for goal, he elects to pick out Lukaku, but the pass is a poor one and the chance eventually breaks down.
(23’) A really good chance now for Palace, as Coleman fouls Townsend 25 yards out from goal, in a central position. The ex-Tottenham winger is standing over the set-piece...
(22’) STAT FLASH - Benteke has scored four and assisted one more in five Premier League appearances against Everton. His impact has been limited so far, though.
(20’) Everton work a neat move forward towards Lukaku, who sets himself before hitting a low strike goal-wards, but it does not trouble Mandanda.
--- 17’ Yellow card Oviedo’s issues with Zaha are continuing, and the defender will now have to be extra careful for the remainder of this game after picking up a booking for a robust challenge on the England forward. Puncheon floats in the free-kick, but Benteke’s header goes wide. ---
(16’) Again, Zaha presents a real danger down the right, with Oviedo unable to match the pace of the former Manchester United winger, who drives towards the byline before drilling in a low cross, but Stekelenburg is equal to it.
(15’) UNLUCKY! Superb play from Cleverley, who picks out Oviedo with a brilliant lofted pass. The Costa Rica defender is scythed down by Delaney but, fortunately for Palace, he had just strayed offside.
(13’) Palace do look a threat on the counter, with Oviedo in particular failing to close down Zaha, who is consistently looking to get a cross in. Everton manage to forge a break themselves, however, but Barkley is too sluggish on the ball and ends up thumping a strike well over.
(11’) Palace have won more Premier League games at Goodison than any other away ground. It is a raucous atmosphere at the moment on Merseyside, with the hosts having started brightly, albeit without any reward as of yet.
(9’) CLOSE! To the chagrin of the Palace fans, Bolasie curls in a wonderful cross from the left. Lukaku rises to meet it, but the Belgian cannot quite make the necessary contact.
(8’) Everton are keeping up the pressure, with a second corner from Barkley again picking out Williams. The ex-Swansea City man looks to tee up Bolasie, but the DR Congo winger is somewhat flat-footed, and cannot get his shot away.
(7’) More patient build-up play from Everton, as Zaha is forced to track back and deflect Coleman’s cross out of play. Williams wins the header from the resulting set-piece, but it is deflected out of play.
(6’) Good work from Coleman, who manages to get around Kelly and sprint into the box. However, Delaney - captaining Palace on his 600th career appearance - is on hand to prevent the Irishman getting through on goal.
(5’) It’s certainly more of a 4-3-3 system from Everton, with Cleverley doubling up with Oviedo. However, the duo both switch off, allowing Ward to whip in a cross, which Williams clears. Townsend drills in the resulting corner, but the Wales skipper is again on hand to head it away.
(4’) Tonight’s game marks Koeman’s 100th fixture in the Premier League. The Dutchman has garnered 49 victories so far, and will be looking to make it 50 this evening. As I type, Zaha manages to drive down the right, but his path is blocked by Williams.
(2’) A quick start from the hosts, as Bolasie looks to make an immediate impact against the club he left in August. The winger twice picks up room down the left, but he sees successive crosses blocked.
(1’) KICK-OFF! We are underway at Goodison Park, with the hosts getting proceedings off to a start at the sound of Jonathan Moss’s whistle.
There’s plenty of pace in Palace’s line-up, with Zaha, Jason Puncheon and Andros Townsend all operating behind the figurehead of former Liverpool striker Christian Benteke, making his first return back to Merseyside since leaving Anfield in the transfer window. History is on the visitors’ side coming into this fixture, with Palace unbeaten at Goodison in the last three campaigns - having won 3-2 in two of those meetings.
It’s a bit more of a compact system from Koeman by the looks of it this evening, who was not impressed by his side’s display in the first-half against Bournemouth. Cleverley seems likely to start on the left-side of midfield, either in a central three or out on the wing, and that should offer Bryan Oviedo, in for the injured Leighton Baines, more protection down the left flank. There is of course a start for Yannick Bolasie against his former club.
Likewise for the visitors, there is only one alteration from Pardew - who has been one of the names linked with the now vacant England job - compared to the starting XI from the last-gasp win over Sunderland, and it comes in midfield, as Yohan Cabaye makes way for Wilfried Zaha, who has overcome his recent injury to start at Goodison. They are however without the injured Scott Dann who netted in the corresponding fixture last term.
So, just the one change from Koeman who, after praising the impact of Tom Cleverley in last week’s defeat to Bournemouth, hands the England midfielder his first start of the Premier League season in place of Kevin Mirallas. However, there has also been a switch on the bench, with youngster Tom Davies coming into the squad and, rather surprisingly, Gerard Deulofeu missing out.

The referee blows his whistle for the final time and each and every Tottenham fan erupts with delight! The home side were excellent from start to finish and helped make a City side full of attacking flair and talent look incredibly average. The league leaders just couldn't find a way through the wall of white in front of them, with Silva, Aguero and Sterling all failing to have the impact that they normally do. At the other end, Tottenham constantly caused a poor defence problems with their intelligent passing and movement, and they could have left with a 3-0 win if it wasn't for a poor penalty from Lamela.
FULL-TIME: TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR 2-0 MANCHESTER CITY
(90’) Janssen goes close! Wanyama manages to thread a deft pass into the path of Janssen, who skips into the left-hand side of the City penalty area completely unmarked. The ball is slightly ahead of the Dutchman so he sticks out a foot to try and reach it, but he's unable to and the ball rolls out for a goal-kick. Any sort of contact surely would have caused Bravo problems at the near post.
(90’) Another opportunity for Aguero! Stones pushes all the way up to Tottenham penalty area and shows great skill to beat two Tottenham players. He then plays a quick one-two with Iheanacho before setting up Aguero, but the Argentine scuffs his shot straight into the hands of Lloris in the middle of the goal.
--- 90’ Substitution Janssen comes on to replace Son, who receives a rousing round of applause from the Tottenham fans as he makes his way off the pitch in his side's final substitution of the day. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be four minutes of added time.
(89’) City keep pushing forward, but they just can't seem to test Lloris, no matter what they try to do. Aguero, who has run his socks off trying to carve out chances on goal, picks up the ball on the edge of the penalty area once again before unleashing a thumping strike, but Vertonghen is there to throw his body in the way of the shot to stop it from reaching Lloris.
(88’) Son and Lamela link up well on the edge of the City box before the South Korean tries to tee up the Argentine with a smart pass into the penalty area, but it's slightly overhit and the winger is unable to meet it before the danger is eventually cleared by Bravo.
--- 87’ Substitution City have made their final alteration of the afternoon, with Sane coming on to replace Sterling. ---
--- 86’ Substitution Alli receives a standing ovation from the Tottenham players as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Nkoudou for the final few minutes of the game. ---
(85’) It's all City at the moment as they desperately try to find a way back into the game, but no matter what they try to do they just can't seem to find a way past the sea of white shirts camped in front of them. Tottenham have plenty of bodies back as they try to hold on to their lead, and, if things stay this way, they are set to be able to.
(83’) Wonderful tackle by Rose! Sterling gets himself into a great position on the right-hand side of the Tottenham penalty area after weaving his way towards goal, but Rose is there to dispossess his England teammate with a brilliant sliding interception at the vital moment.
(82’) Iheanacho breaks into the left-hand side of the Tottenham penalty area and latches on to the ball in a good position at the near post, but he completely scuffs his attempted strike and ends up falling over instead of making contact with the ball.
(81’) Wonderful stop by Lloris! City embark on their best series of passes of the game before Aguero tries to test Lloris with a thumping strike from the left-hand side of the Tottenham box, but the Frenchman pulls off a lovely diving save to push the effort over the crossbar and out for a corner.
(79’) Chance for Gundogan! The German, who has seen little of the ball after coming on to the pitch, gets himself into a good position just outside of the Tottenham penalty area before firing a curling shot, but there's far too much power behind the strike and it ends up sailing over the top of the crossbar.
(77’) A poor attempted clearance from Otamendi flies out of play for a corner over on the left wing. Lamela's corner fails to cause too many problems for City before Tottenham come back through Son, but the South Korean is unable to muscle his way into the box and the visitors just about hold on.
(75’) Great save by Lloris! Silva, who has started seeing more of the ball over the last five minutes, breaks towards the edge of the Tottenham penalty area before threading a lovely through-ball into the path of Iheanacho. The striker meets it well and quickly unleashes a low strike at the near post, but Lloris is there to smother the danger.
(74’) A lofted pass towards the edge of the Tottenham penalty area initially causes problems for the home side after Wanyama is unable to fully clear the danger, but the ball bounces over to Vertonghen and the Belgian is then able to thump the ball up towards the halfway line.
--- 72’ Substitution Sissoko limps off the pitch to be replaced by Dier for the final 20 minutes of the game. Can the midfielder help his side hold on to what would be an excellent victory? ---
(71’) There's a brief break in play as Sissoko receives treatment over on the right wing. The Frenchman looks to be struggling with some sort of muscle injury and it looks as if his game may be over. He's put in a great shift this afternoon and will be sorely missed if he does have to make way.
(70’) City come back once again and do well to pick out Sterling on the edge of the Tottenham penalty area, but the winger has a lack of options available around him and he ends up firing a low shot bouncing straight into the hands of Lloris in the middle of the goal.
(69’) Silva and Aguero link up well over on the left wing before the latter tries to muscle his way into the penalty area, but he's quickly closed down by Sissoko and is dispossessed by the Frenchman before he's able to pick out a teammate with a pass forward.
(68’) City move the ball around nicely over on the right flank before Iheanacho slips through the Tottenham back line as he latches on to a pass forward, but the youngster's run is poorly timed and the linesman's flag is quickly raised for offside as soon as the striker makes contact with the ball.
(67’) Rose is clattered into by Sterling once again, leaving the full-back on the floor and in serious discomfort. He protests to the referee and seems to ask for a second yellow, but the referee doesn't agree and only gives the winger a talking to.
--- 65’ Substitution City have made an attacking change, with Navas making way for Iheanacho. ---

(62’) It just isn't working for City, who have looked bereft of ideas in advanced areas and are struggling to cause Tottenham many problems on the rare occasions that they're able to push forward. Aguero has been trying his hardest to carve out chances on goal, but the absence of De Bruyne really seems to be hurting his side.
(60’) The ball pinballs around the edge of the City penalty area as Tottenham try to find the way through the sea of black shirts camped in front of them. The home side are unable to do so, however, before a pass from Rose down the left wing fails to find Alli and instead rolls out of play for a goal-kick, which, not for the first time this afternoon, Bravo sends straight to a white shirt.
(58’) Chance for Eriksen! A poor throw out from Bravo is easily cut out by Wanyama, who then pokes the ball forward to Eriksen. The City defence are completely asleep and allow the Dane to test Bravo from 25 yards out, but the Chilean is able to save the curling effort.
(57’) Aguero cuts inside from the right wing and tees up Gundogan, who is in a pocket of space midway inside the Tottenham half of the pitch. The German spots a good run forward from Sterling and tries to pick him out, but his pass forward is overhit and fails to find the winger before rolling out of play for a goal-kick.
--- 56’ Yellow card Sterling and Rose come together once again, but this time it's the winger who charges into the full-back and upends him as he tries to break down the left wing, resulting in a free-kick for Tottenham and a yellow card for the former Liverpool man. ---
(55’) Navas sprints down the left wing and takes on Walker before heading towards the byline, but the Spaniard holds on to the ball for slightly too long and ends up running it out of play before he can whip a cross into the penalty area, resulting in a free-kick for Tottenham that Lloris clumsily fires out for a throw-in.
--- 53’ Substitution City have made their first substitution of the afternoon, with Gundogan coming on to replace Fernando in the heart of midfield. ---
(52’) Sterling battles with Rose deep down the right wing before being dragged to the ground by the full-back, who is lucky to escape a second yellow card. Navas chips a clever cross over to Fernandinho, who is in acres of space on the edge of the box, but the Brazilian's first-time volleyed shot is poor and sails well wide of the goal.
(51’) Aguero hits the post! Fernandinho charges forward before threading a nice through-ball into the path of Aguero. The Argentine striker meets the ball on the left-hand side of the penalty area and immediately fires a low shot towards the near post, but Lloris is just about able to tip the effort on to the woodwork. That was City's best chance of the game!
(50’) Tottenham come back once again as Sissoko breaks down the right wing and skips past Kolarov far too easily. The Frenchman then reaches the penalty area and fires a thumping low cross towards the penalty spot, but it's just about dealt with by the visitors before it can find a white shirt.
(49’) Another opportunity for Son! The South Korean weaves into the left-hand side of the City box on a wonderful run as he heads towards the near post, but he holds on to the ball for slightly too long and is unable to release it before being dispossessed by Zabaleta.
(48’) Great strike by Wanyama! The Kenyan muscles his way past Fernando far too easily and breaks towards the City penalty area before unleashing a thumping low strike, but it's one that Bravo is just about able to tip round the post with a smart diving save.
(47’) Early chance for Son! An awful pass from Kolarov fails to find Fernando and instead rolls straight to Son, who takes a couple of quick touches before unleashing a curling strike that flies a few yards wide of the far post.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The home fans erupt with delight as the two teams make their way off the pitch, and it's no wonder why. Tottenham deserve to be two goals up after putting in a wonderful performance across the pitch, leaving City looking open at the back and bereft of ideas up front. Alli, Lamela and, in particular, Son have all looked incredibly bright inside the final third, whilst at the other end, the league leaders have struggled to find a way through Tottenham's well-organised and resolute defensive line.
HALF-TIME: TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR 2-0 MANCHESTER CITY
The two teams are making their way back out on to the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.

City take the resulting free-kick quickly and work it over to Aguero, but Lloris charges out to dispossess the Argentine just as he's about to shoot. The ball rolls over to Navas and the Spaniard quickly tries to beat the goalkeeper with a first-time chipped strike, but Alderweireld is able to head the ball away from danger at the vital moment.

(23’) Tottenham immediately break away on a quick counter-attack after dealing with the danger. Son does well to muscle his way into the City box before taking on Bravo, but he fires his low shot straight into the body of Bravo before the linesman's flag is eventually raised for offside.

In recent years, it’s been City who have enjoyed the vast majority of joy in this particular tie, but Tottenham will fondly remember back-to-back victories from last season’s meetings. The North London side came from behind to thump their opponents 4-1 almost exactly a year ago today, and they then went on to win 2-1 in Manchester thanks to second-half goals from Harry Kane and Christian Eriksen.
City did suffer a slight wobble during the week, however, as they were tested by an extremely determined Celtic side and ended up drawing 3-3 in their Champions League game in Glasgow. Pep Guardiola’s men were forced to come from behind three times to salvage a point, and there’s a worry that such a tough runout could negatively impact their performance here today.
As for City, they have dominated the Premier League thus far, with only two of their games failing to see them win by a margin of at least two goals. The Citizens have already hit the back of the net 18 times this season, with their +13 goal difference comfortably the best of any team. They also boast a striker in excellent form in Sergio Aguero, whose two goals against Swansea City last weekend took his tally to five in four games.
Stoke City, Sunderland and Middlesbrough have all fallen to Mauricio Pochettino’s impressive side in recent weeks, whilst Tuesday evening saw them pick up their first Champions League win of the season with a 1-0 victory away to CSKA Moscow. The game saw Heung-Min Son score his third goal in two outings, and the in-form South Korean will be looking to make a similar impact this afternoon as his team try to close the gap at the top of the table to just one point.
Today’s big clash not only pits first against third but also brings together the only teams that remain unbeaten in the league this season. For City, it’s been an excellent start to the campaign that has seen them win all of their opening six games, whilst Tottenham have dropped points only twice, with each of their previous three Premier League clashes ending in victories.

That's all from us here at The Hawthorns today, thanks for joing us and we hope to see you again soon.
It’s all over here at The Hawthorns and for the second week running West Ham have been beaten 4-2! A wonderful result for West Brom at the end of a week where speculation over the future of Tony Pulis has been rife, while problems mount for Slaven Bilic after just one win in five league games to start this season.
(90’) Full time: West Bromwich Albion 4-2 West Ham United
(90’) West Brom break on the counter attack and have numbers flooding forward, but Phillips goes for goal himself but drags his shot wide from 20 yards out.
(90’) We're into five minutes of stoppage time now as Payet puts in another dangerous cross and once again it's Antonio who gets his head to it but this time he can only head wide!
(89’) CLOSE FOR ROBSON-KANU!! So nearly a debut goal for Robson-Kanu as Phillips whips a delightful ball across the face of goal and the Welshman is inches away from getting a touch on it as he slides in behind Collins.
--- 87’ Substitution Tony Pulis makes his third and final change as Salomón Rondón is replaced by debutant Hal Robson-Kanu! ---
--- 86’ Yellow card Nyom may have thought he'd escaped caution but referee Clattenburg goes back to book him for a foul on Feghouli earlier in the move. ---
--- 86’ Yellow card Sofiane Feghouli is booked for protesting against Mark Clattenburg's decision not to award West Ham a penalty after Payet went down in the box. There didn't look to be much contact! ---
(85’) Morrison finds McClean on the left hand corner of the box as West Brom look to seal the win, but his shot is straight at Adrian, who makes a bit of a mess of the save but the danger is easily cleared.
(82’) WHAT A SAVE BY FOSTER!!! Wonderful skill from Antonio to dance past McClean and drill a low cross towards James Collins, but the centre-back's clean connection is superbly saved by Foster diving to his left. Tony Pulis would have been furious had that gone in as he felt there was a West Ham handball in the build-up.
(81’) Lanzini has a go from 30 yards out but hits it with little power and it's comfortably blocked by McCauley. West Brom won't mind too much if they can keep West Ham to long range efforts in the last 10 minutes.
(79’) HUGE CHANCE FOR PHILLIPS!! Big chance for Matt Phillips to wrap it up at the back post having been picked out by McClean's deep cross, but he takes too long over the shot and West Ham are able to get enough defenders across to smother the shot.
--- 77’ Substitution Slaven Bilic is going for broke now as he replaces left back Arthur Masuaku with young striker Ashley Fletcher. It's been a tough afternoon for Masuaku! ---
(77’) Feghouli lays the ball off for Payet to run onto on the edge of the box, but the shot isn't one of the Frenchman's best and Foster watches it go high over his crossbar.
--- 75’ Substitution James Morrison is now going to come on to make his first appearance since the opening day of the season, replacing the scorer of two of West Brom’s goals Nacer Chadli. ---
(73’) Nyom makes a good tackle inside his own half but runs out of options as he looks forward and West Brom are back on the back foot again. They're really struggling to get out of their own half now!
(72’) Dimitri Payet is all of a sudden popping up everywhere, this time finding half a yard of space outside the box to shoot, but Evans gets out well to block the ball out for a corner, which is headed comfortably away by Yacob.
(71’) Payet twists and turns his way down the outside of Craig Dawson and gets a cross away, but Foster is easily able to catch the ball and drop on it to waste a few more seconds.
--- 68’ Substitution Tony Pulis makes his first substitution as Brendon Galloway is replaced by Allan Nyom. James Morrison looked to be coming on as well but Pulis appears to have changed his mind and Morrison is sent back to the bench. ---
(67’) The game has suddenly come alive and West Brom look rather panicky now!! Feghouli and Calleri, the two half time substitutions for West Ham, may not have been involved in the goals directly but they've changed the complexion of this game!
--- 65’ Goal! GOOOAAALLLLLL!!!! It really is game on now as Lanzini strikes the ball low and hard from the spot past Ben Foster, who went the right way but couldn’t get a hand to it. ---
(65’) PENALTY TO WEST HAM!!!!! Payet gets inside Galloway and is brought down by the on loan left-back as he bears down on goal.
--- 61’ Assist Having come so close from the free-kick moments earlier, Payet shows hisquality with an inch perfect cross for Antonio! ---
--- 61’ Goal! GOOOAAAALLLLLL!!!! Just when you thought it was game over West Ham pull a goal back. Feghouli’s cross is kept alive by Payet down the left hand side of the box and he stands up a wonderful cross which Antonio heads in to reduce the deficit back to 4-1! Game on!! ---
(60’) SO CLOSE FROM PAYET!!!!! Payet is fouled 25 yards out from goals by Jonny Evans, and the Frenchman picks himself up to rattle the free-kick against the post!!!
--- 56’ Assist Rondon could easily have taken the shot on himself, but delayed shooting until Chadli arrived and left the Belgian an easy tap in. ---
--- 56’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLL!!! IT’S FOUR!!!!!! West Ham throw almost everybody forward for a corner, but having taken in short Antonio gives the ball away to Darren Fletcher, who feeds Rondon on half way and the striker has a clean run through on goal and squares the ball for Chadli to tap the ball into an empty net and put West Brom 4-0 up with more than half an hour to play. ---
(54’) As you might have expected West Ham have started the second half on the front foot and there are appeals for a penalty from the travelling fans behind the goal as Calleri goes to ground but the referee waives play on.
(51’) Anontio drives into the West Brom area and from a tight angle fires straight at Foster who can only parry the ball up in the air, but gratefully grabs it on the second attempt.
(49’) Slaven Bilic is deep in conversation with the fourth official as Foster comes out and punches the ball and appears to catch Calleri in the process but the linesman had his flag up to signal that the ball had gone out of play.
(47’) The two new men involved straight away for West Ham as they both get themselves into the box, but neither can jump high enough to get on the end of Antonio's cross from the left.
(46’) West Ham get us underway in the second half, big half needed from them if they're to take anything from this game.
--- 46’ Substitution Slaven Bilic has wasted no time and makes a double change at half-time with Sofiane Feghouli and Jonathon Calleri coming on in place of Zaza and Noble. ---
Slaven Bilic will have the consolation of knowing his side enjoyed lots of comfortable possession in that first half, and had Michail Antonio taken his chance with the score at 1-0 it could well be a different story, but he will know that breaking down Tony Pulis's well organised defence will be tough and an early goal could be key to his side getting back into the game.
West Brom have only scored two league goals all season prior to today, but goals from Chadli, Rondon and McClean have given them a 3-0 lead at the break, while West Ham looked shell-shocked!
Half-time! West Bromwich Albion 1-0 West Ham United
(45’) Two minutes of added time are being played as cries of 'olay' ring out around The Hawthorns.
--- 44’ Assist Chadli had acres of space inside the box and while his shot wasn't the cleanest of strikes, McClean got the vital touch to ensure it evaded Adrian. ---
--- 44’ Goal! GOOAAAALLLLLLLLL!!!! MCCLEAN MAKES IT 3-0!!!!! West Ham fail to clear Phillips’s inswinging corner, and as Chadli drills the ball back towards goal, McClean sticks out a boot and diverts the ball into the corner for his first Premier League goal in a West Brom shirt. ---
--- 43’ Yellow card Craig Dawson is shown a yellow card for an earlier foul on Masuaku. ---
(42’) Payet has two goes at shooting from just inside the box, but both times he is surrounded by black and white shirts and the ball doesn't get through to Foster in the West Brom goal.
(40’) Zaza fails to control the ball on the edge of the penalty area once again, but the ball breaks for Lanzini 25 yards out but he can can only fire an ambitious volley high over the bar.
--- 37’ Assist Ogbonna's attempted clearance from close to the left hand corner flag is a poor one and deflects straight to Chadli who could have taken the shot on himself, but unselfishly rolled the ball to Rondon in a much better position. ---
--- 37’ Goal! GOOAAALLLLLLL!!!! RONDON DOUBLES WEST BROM'S LEAD! Ogbonna’s poor clearance goes straight to Chadli inside the box, and the Belgian rolls the ball into Rondon who turns James Collins and drills the ball low and hard across Adrian and into the far corner. ---
(35’) HUGE CHANCE FOR ANTONIO! Payet drives at the West Brom defence before playing a delightful chip over the top for Antonio, but Foster does superbly to come off his line and block the winger's shot with his chest at close range.
(34’) CLOSE!!!! Manuel Lanzini gets away from Yacob on the edge of the box and fires inches wide of the West Brom goal. Foster looked to be well beaten had that been on target there.
(32’) West Ham can't find any way through the middle and are looking to get the ball wide as often as possible, particularly down the right hand side, but West Brom are remaining resolute so far.
(30’) Nordtveit swings in another cross, this time from the left hand side, but Zaza opts to go for a spectacular bicycle kick from 18 yards out and completely misses the ball.
(28’) Masuaku is enduring a torrid time out there today, first conceding a free-kick just inside his own half for a foul on Phillips, before attempting a wild clearance inside his own box which goes straight up in the air causing chaos for Adrian, who eventually gathers on the second attempt.
(26’) Chance for West Brom! The home side counter attack down the left and McClean puts a dangerous cross towards Phillips at the back post, but the former Queens Park Rangers winger fluffs the volley horribly from eight yards out.
(24’) West Ham are knocking the ball around with ease inside the West Brom half, and Nordtveit finds some space for a cross from the right hand side, but Antonio doesn't get enough contact on the header and it flashes across the face of goal.
(22’) The home crowd have quietened down since the early goal as West Ham have started to enjoy more of the ball, but their side are sitting deep and look comfortable without the ball.

Palace see things out to claim their first win of the season and end Boro's unbeaten start to 2015-16. Zaha was the star of the show, setting one up for Benteke before converting early in the second half to seal the points. Ayala's header was not enough for the home side. That's all from us, thanks for tuning in.
(90’) The set-piece is headed clear and Boro can't get it back in the box in time!
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card FREE-KICK! Boro win a set-piece right on the edge of the box that will surely be the last kick of the game. That was inches away from being a penalty, and Zaha gets booked for the foul on Friend. ---
(90’) Deep into the five minutes of added on time shown by the fourth official and Boro continue to hammer at the Palace door. Downing takes aim from long range once again, but can't find the target.
(90’) Traore tries to conjure something out of nothing as he skips around Kelly, but runs down a dead end. Boro throwing everything at Palace but for the moment, the visitors are hanging on.
(88’) MAGNIFICENT SAVE! Mandanda has responded with flying colours whenever he's been called upon, and he parries a stinger from Ramirez on the left-hand side, before Kelly just about bundles the rebound over before Negredo can pounce! Boro want a handball against the defender but the referee waves play on.
(86’) Not a whole lot happening out on the pitch in terms of goalmouth action. This will suit Palace just fine, as they look to close out their first three points of the new Premier League season.
--- 84’ Substitution Jonathan Benteke comes on for his Palace debut but doesn't get a chance to play alongside his brother Christian - since that's the man he replaces. ---
--- 84’ Substitution Double sub from Pardew, and we finally see Flamini enter the fray to shore up the midfield for the last few minutes. ---
--- 82’ Yellow card Strange situation here. Flamini was set to come on as a sub, but he was instructed to take his wristband off. That held things up, which Boro saw as timewasting. Ward, who was next to the fourth official, was infolved in that muddle and comes out of it with a yellow card. ---
--- 81’ Substitution Traore is on and off goes Stuani. Karanka makes his last change. ---
(79’) Middlesbrough are pushing more men forward, but they're being frustrated at every opportunity by the visitors - who still have to be a little mor composed in possession here.
--- 77’ Substitution Lee has been called upon to replace Townsend. ---
(76’) BAD FIRST TOUCH! Friend had time and space arriving on the ball at the back post, but he pushes it too far ahead of him and the defence is allowed to get themselves in the way. Great work from Ramirez to set that chance up.
(74’) Another penalty claim that goes unheeded by the referee. This time it's Middlesbrough who are appealing as it appeared that Dann used his arm to intervene on the ball, but play went on.
(72’) Chance down at the other end now as Ramirez finds space on the left-hand side to attack, but his cross towards Negredo has too much mustard on it and goes out of play. The striker was in a good position too.
(70’) ONTO THE ROOF OF THE NET! Puncheon lifts a corner to the near post where Dann gets the step on Friend and flicks it towards the back post, where Delaney charges in to meet it, but can't keep it down!
(68’) Palace try to build an attack but are forced to play it all the way back to Mandanda to rebuild. Boro are holding a better defensive shape and preventing the easy service to Benteke for now.
(66’) Ramirez invites Ayala forward, and the defender nearly picks out the substitute with a hooked cross, but it's cleared well by the defence. Signs of life again from Middlesbrough here in the second half.
(64’) Negredo looks to be alright and ready to continue. Less than half-hour to go here and it's still Boro trailing Palace thanks to that early second-half goal from Zaha. Subs are warming up on the sidelines.
(62’) Negredo collides with Ward and goes down in a heap. It looks like there's some blood, and the game is stopped temporarily to tend to the striker. The medical staff try to patch him up.
--- 60’ Yellow card Ramirez has only been on the pitch for a few minutes but he's already recieved a booking after tossing the ball away angrily. He thought he had won a corner, but only a goal-kick was awarded. ---
(58’) Dann has been active in the box when attacking set plays, but he hasn't found the target much. Another Puncheon delivery finds him creeping at the back post, but he again fails to trouble the kepeer.
--- 57’ Substitution Substitution Adam Clayton Marten de Roon ---
--- 57’ Substitution Ramirez is introduced for Fischer. ---
(56’) STINGER! Boro, having failed to pass their way into the box, have opted to try their luck from long range, with Gibson sending a piledriver Mandanda's way from all of 30-35 yards, which is diverted away from goal!
(54’) Not many chances now as the game becomes bogged down in the middle of the park. Palace are still the side looking more poised on the ball, but they're unable to move it into the final third for now.
(51’) Downing, who we haven't seen much of from open play, bursts into life with a 25-yard effort that skims wide of the mark. Boro came back once from a goal down, can they do it again?
(49’) Crystal Palace wasted no time in restoring their advantage on the scoreboard to match their dominance on the pitch. What will bite at Boro is the fact that both goals came as a result of defender mistakes.
--- 47’ Goal! IT'S ANOTHER ONE FOR PALACE! McArthur sprays a pass inside of Friend, but the defender seems to have it under control. However, Zaha nips in behind him to swipe possession and convert! ---
(46’) And we're back!
And that will do it here for now as both sides enter the half-time break all square at one apiece. Benteke opened the scoring deservedly for the visitors with a thumping header over Ayala, but the defender struck gold at the other end with an aerial goal of his own to bring the hosts level against the run of play. It's finely poised for the second half, so stay tuned!
(45’) NEARLY A STUNNING END TO THE HALF! Negredo is put through on goal just outside his man, and uses all of his pace to gather half-a step to shoot, but his finish is thwarted by the keeper!
(44’) Barragan and Stuani exchange passes to open up space on the flank, and the latter storms into a great position, but is caught in two minds and eventually delivers a soft cross that is gobbled uo by Mandanda.
(42’) Palace force the issue again from the high ball as a corner is picked up by Townsend, whose shot is thwarted by the defence. Ward attacks the loose ball but it's well over. Boro living dnagerously.
(40’) Middlesbrough got some wind in their sails from that goal, but were nearly chopped back down to size after Townsend's free-kick causes problems deep in the area, before they eventually clear.
--- 38’ Assist Downing's corner set that one up for Ayala. ---
--- 38’ Goal! AYALA TIES IT UP! The defender was outjumped for the opener but showcases his ability in the air with a towering leap to direct a corner into the back of the net! ---
(36’) Somewhat ironic cheer from the home fans as Mandanda comes off his line to clear away a shoddy back-pass from Kelly. That's about as good as it has been for them in this game so far.
(33’) Middlesbrough really haven't been able to get Negredo involved in the game, in complete contrast to the way that Palace are using Benteke. Both strikers will be key to their team's respective seasons.
(31’) Palace still have all the momentum in this game, and it's clear that they're looking to utilise Benteke's mismatch against the Boro defence at every opportunity. He's winning all of the high balls.
(29’) Middlesbrough finally start to come out of their shell, putting some pressure on the opposition down the right-hand side and winning a free-kick in a good position, but it comes to nothing.
(27’) From a corner, Benteke wins the initial ball again, but his flick across the face of goal finds no takers among his teammates. There's danger every time that Palace get the ball into the box.
(25’) GREAT SAVE BY VALDES! Zaha is excellent on the right-hand side, taking two defenders out of the equation before squaring a low ball for Benteke. The goalscorer holds off his man before laying it off for Townsend to hammer on goal from the top of the box, but it's pushed wide by the keeper!
(22’) Dann and Ayala battle for a corner, with claims of a penalty by the Palace defender, but doesn't get any call from the referee. The visitors are dominating things in the final third here.
(20’) Boro finally manage to work a spell on the ball, but not much comes of it. There's always the danger too that Palace will break at pace the more the home side get sucked into the opposition half.
(18’) In basketball, you would call that being posterised. Benteke was a foot above Ayala to attack that cross. Boro need to sort themselves out as their adherence to a defensive shape has not worked.
--- 16’ Goal! THERE IT IS! Benteke powers the visitors into the lead as he positions himself at the back post, leaps all over Ayala and plants a header into the back of the net! ---
--- 16’ Assist Great vision by Zaha to float that cross to the back post. ---
(13’) Palace are looking the better side here in possession, but Christian Benteke hasn't had a whole lot of luck despite being the target for virtually every ball launched into the penalty area.
(10’) Middlesbrough are keeping a very disciplined shape as Palace begin to get into their stride. Apart from that opportunity for Negredo, the home side really haven't had a sniff at goal so far.
(8’) Palace do a shoddy job of clearing a ball into the box, which falls kindly to Negredo on the edge of the area. However, the forward can't process that in time and rushes a shot off the mark.
(5’) Now there's a chance for Palace as they win their first corner of the match. Puncheon flights in a corner that finds Dann relatively unmarked, but the defender can't direct his header on target.
(3’) Good start here from the home side, who are passing the ball with zip, already forcing an early corner that puts the Palace defence under pressure. The fans are enjoying themselves as well.
(1’) Off we go!
Connor Wickham makes way for Wilfried Zaha, while Jonathan Benteke, brother of starting striker Christian, is on the bench ahead of a possible debut. Mathieu Flamini, picked up on a free, is also among the substitutes.
Victor Valdes returns from a hamstring injury to take Brad Guzan's place between the posts for the home side, while Emilio Nsue makes way for George Friend in defence. Viktor Fischer is also in for Gaston Ramirez, who returns from international duty struggling for full fitness.

Middlesbrough subs: Guzan, Rhodes, Traore, Ramirez, De Roon, Nsue, Chambers.
Middlesbrough (4-2-3-1): Valdes; Barragan, Ayala, Gibson, Friend; Forshaw, Clayton; Stuani, Downing, Fischer; Negredo.
Palace needed an injury-time leveller from Joe Ledley to scrape a draw against Bournemouth right before the international break - their only point of the new Premier League season. They've never won in their previous five visits to the Riverside Stadium.
Boro drew with Stoke and West Brom either side of a 2-1 victory over rivals Sunderland to make it three games without losing on their return to the top flight. They have lost only one of their last 10 home games in the Premier League.

Palace dominated play in the second half and you could just see it coming. Perhaps Palace will continue to rue their penalty miss in the 16th minute of the match. Literally a game of two halves has come to an end, with the scores all tied up at 1-1. ---

--- 90’ +3 Goal! GOOOAAAAALLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!!Scott Dann with a bullet like header sliding it past Boruc and finding the back of the net. The scores are level at 1-1. Scott Dann may have saved the game for Palace. ---
--- 90’ +3 Assist Assist Jason Puncheon delivers it into the box, as he looks for someone inside the box and he finds the captain, Scott Dann. ---
(90’) Bournemouth clear the ball long from defence, as they want to take it out of the danger zone.
(90’) We have four minutes of additional time to play, as we may be in for some nervous moments for Bournemouth and their goal keeper Artur Boruc.

(85’) Adam Smith takes his time with the ball as he finally releases his cross into the box for Fraser, but his shot on goal just misses to the right.
(84’) Bournemouth are starting to play more of a defensive game now, as they look to steady the ship and run down the clock.
(82’) A drinks break is called for, as the players from both teams use it as a way to manage the conditions on the ground.
(81’) Townsend with a left footed shot on goal, it is very close, but it is away to the left.
(80’) Benteke is bought down inside the box by Adam Smith, but the referee waives away the appeals of a penalty from the Crystal Palace players.
(78’) Souaré with a left footed shot on goal from just outside of the box, but it is wide and away to the left.
(76’) There is still plenty of time for Palace to equalise, but it is not looking too likely at the moment, as they have struggled in attack in the last few minutes.
(75’) Zaha delivers the ball on a platter for Chung-Yong Lee, but his right footed shot at the centre of the box is just a tad bit high.
(73’) Souaré tries a through ball for Benteke, but he hears a whistle, he look over to the sideline and his fears are realised, the offside flag has been raised.

(62’) Souaré with a cross into the box, McArthur rises up with a header but the shot on goal ends up being blocked.

A Shay Given own-goal is enough to secure another three points for the Toffees who enjoy their best start to a Premier League season in 10 years. Stoke are left with just one point from their first three matches, and have their work cut out for them heading into the international break.
(90’) FULL-TIME: EVERTON 1-0 STOKE CITY.
(90’) Simple in the end from Given, as he doesn't have much ground to make up to turn aside Baines' effort from the set-piece. Stoke down to their final 60 seconds...
(90’) Everton are on the front foot, working the ball around excellently in the final third as they milk the clock. Holgate does so well to ride out a challenge before winning a free-kick in a prominent area for the Toffees.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on at the end of this match. Is there to be a sting in the tale?
--- 88’ Yellow card Barry is booked for a cynical foul in midfield. That's a professional challenge, however, from the midfielder to break up a decent move from the Potters. ---
--- 88’ Substitution A third and final change for Everton as they look to milk the final minutes off the clock. Tom Davies replaces Bolasie. ---
(86’) More panic at the back! Everton scramble to clear following a clever bit of play on the left from Sobhi and a deflected cross from Pieters that so nearly found its way through for Arnautovic! It just doesn't fall kindly for the Austrian and the hosts manage to clear their line.
--- 84’ Substitution Koeman brings on defensive reinforcements as Barkley is replaced by centre-half Ramiro Funes Mori for the final five minutes or so. ---
(82’) Everton are bossing possession now, doing their best to deny Stoke another opportunity to get back into this game. They're looking rather comfortable and clinical on the ball, but it will be a tough ask for them to keep this up for another 10 minutes with an inevitable push to come from the Potters.
(80’) THAT WOULD HAVE ICED IT! Three points in the bag had that been a few feet to the left! Bolasie places a terrific first-time strike back across the grain, but he can't find the back of the net with Given nowhere close to getting across to meet it!
--- 78’ Substitution Bojan does come on for the final 12 minutes, replacing Imbula. ---
--- 78’ Substitution Ramadan Sobhi replaces Diouf, the second Stoke appearance for the Egyptian. ---
(78’) OH MY! WAS THAT THE CHANCE? Arnautovic is slipped through on goal and unselfishly squares for Walters after Stekelenburg commits. The substitute is staring at an empty net, but he's late to react and fails to get the decisive touch in the end! Unbelievable!
(77’) Lukaku cannot buy his goal today! The striker is turned aside by Given from point-blank range, following a quick, decisive break from Everton after a strong bit of goalkeeping from Stekelenburg!
(76’) Fighting back are Everton now, providing some much-needed respite for their defence. Hughes has prepared another substitution, and it looks like it will be Bojan who comes on for them.
(74’) STAT: Stoke have secured just two wins in their last 12 Premier League fixtures (W2, D4, L6), picking up only 10 points from a possible 36.
(72’) Everton are doing their best to take the sting out of the match, trying to stray from the frantic, fast-paced 70 minutes we have bore witness to up to this point. They've got a bit of a nervous feel about them as they try to hang on to this slender lead.
--- 70’ Substitution Arouna Kone is the first Everton substitute to enter the fray, with Mirallas the one to be removed. ---
(67’) Stoke have upped the urgency as they search for an equaliser. They're getting more bodies forward as the Toffees drop deeper in defence, which has seen the tension rise a great deal in this ground.

(64’) STAT: Jonathan Walters has appeared 11 times against Everton in the Premier League without scoring; his joint-longest such run against an opponent in the competition.
(62’) PARRIED BY GIVEN! The Stoke keeper will be reeling still over how the penalty went in, but that should help quell his frustrations for the time being. Barkley does brilliantly to tee himself up for a shot with his first touch, before letting fly with his second, but Given dives across in a hurry to keep it out!
(60’) Outstanding match here in Merseyside! These sides go back and forth, pushing the tempo with an unquenchable thirst for goals. There's been no real sticky spells or tedious periods in the entirety of this contest thus far, as we pass the hour mark here at Goodison.
(58’) OFF THE BAR AND OUT! How have Everton survived this one?! Arnautovic reads play perfectly to get on the end of a header and through on goal. He lifts a finish over Stekelenburg from in close, but it rattles off the bar before being cleared off the line by Jagielka! Fine margins here at Goodison!

--- 51’ Goal! EVERTON LEAD AT GOODISON! Baines doesn't miss many, but he's very lucky here! His spot-kick is stopped by Given, before it's turned onto the post, back off the head of Given and into the back of the net! ---
(51’) Penalty Save Shay Given
(50’) PENALTY TO EVERTON! Bardsley is unlucky as his feet get tangled with Williams inside the area, accidentally, but it sends the centre-half to ground and Oliver points straight to the spot!
(50’) HOW HAS THAT STAYED OUT?! Sensational bit of interplay from the Toffees, as Lukaku is played through on goal by Holgate's wonderfully cushioned header. The striker pokes through the legs of Given, but his final effort is blocked behind by Shawcross!
(48’) AGONISINGLY CLOSE! Barry steals possession from Allen and feeds Barkley forward. The midfielder twists and turns his way a bit sloppily past a pair of Stoke defenders before lashing an impressive strike across goal in the end, but it misses by mere inches at the far post!
(46’) Back underway at Goodison!
No shortage of entertainment in the first half at Goodison, but no goals to speak of as the teams head into the interval scoreless. A pair of goal-line clearances from Ryan Shawcross and Peter Crouch have kept Everton off the scoresheet, while Stoke have not been able to take their chances at the other end.
(45’) HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 STOKE CITY.
(45’) There will be two minutes added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Arnautovic limps off the pitch very gingerly, to a chorus of boos from the Everton supporters. Seconds later the Austrian is back out onto the pitch, as the boos only intensify.
(41’) Arnautovic is down on the ground, writhing in pain after being caught from behind by Bolasie. There wasn't any intent in that from the DR Congo winger, but it doesn't make it any less painful for the Austrian, as Mark Hughes nervously awaits word from the medical staff.
(39’) Perfect delivery! Wonderful work from Holgate to get forward and into acres of space on the right. He lashes a terrific delivery across the face of goal, but Lukaku arrives just too late at the near post, while no one is following up behind him to turn it into the empty net!
(37’) STAT: Stoke have scored just one first half goal in their last seven Premier League matches, with five of their six goals in this period coming after half-time.
(35’) TIPPED OVER! Strong wrists from Given to knock Mirallas' powerful strike over the bar. It was well-struck from the Belgian, but the Stoke keeper was wise to it. Everton have upped the intensity as they search for the breakthrough before the interval.
(33’) It's incredibly back and forth right now! There's hardly time to take a breath. These sides are exchanging attacks at a remarkable pace, as the two defences are left stretched. From a neutral point of view, this has been a joy to behold.
(31’) It's been a frenetic opening 30 minutes at Goodison, but somehow the match remains scoreless. Both teams have had their chances, and the tempo has been lively throughout, suggesting the scoreline will not remain this way much longer.
(29’) He's got the appetite! Barry, hardly known for his prowess in front of goal, has got a rejuvenated hunger for goals following his tally last week against West Brom. The midfielder is getting forward with real intent, and finds himself with a pair of chances to shoot, but neither effort finds its way through the crowd of bodies in the centre.
(27’) STAT: Lukaku has not scored or assisted a single goal in any of his last 10 Premier League appearances for Everton, a run stretching back to March 19th. It is his longest goal drought in his Premier League career.
(25’) CLEARED OFF THE LINE! Celebrations throughout Goodison as Williams gets on the end of Mirallas' cross to head past Given, but Crouch is in the right place at the right time to hook it off the line! Mark Oliver has a look at his watch, and goal-line technology confirms the initial call on the field.
(23’) BACK COME STOKE! End-to-end action at Goodison, but somehow it remains scoreless! Imbula weaves his way through into the area, but indecision plagues him in the end! The midfielder had a clear look at goal but waited too long to pull the trigger! He has to do better there.
(21’) SHAWCROSS TO THE RESCUE! That's the sort of effect Lukaku has! Cameron and the rest of the Stoke defence simply cannot deal with the pace and physicality of the Belgian striker, who powers his way through on goal. He has Given beaten with his finish, but Shawcross is there to back up his keeper and turn the effort aside!
(19’) Wasteful! Gueye breaks impressively as Everton commit bodies forward on the counter. The midfielder has time and space to run at the defence, but instead opts to play an early ball through for Mirallas, who failed to time his run properly as the flag goes up for offside.
(17’) Williams protests fervently after a late whistle awards Stoke a free-kick. The Toffees have entered a sticky spell and they're allowing the visitors to push them around. The Potters were on the ropes early on, but they're very much on the front foot now - though there's been nothing to test Stekelenburg as of yet.
(15’) Imbula is looking lively for the Potters, who have enjoyed the bulk of possession over the last five minutes. The midfielder links up with Arnautovic as Stoke get into a good area, but in the end a hopeful shot from Bardsley, from about 30 yards, drifts harmlessly wide and relieves the pressure on the Everton goal.
(13’) Stoke have responded very well, managing to take back some momentum following the strong start from Everton. The Potters have a real foothold in the contest now, imposing themselves nicely in midfield.
(11’) Speculative, but impressive! The ball breaks for Arnautovic following a slide from Gueye, and he tries his luck from a long way out. It sails over rather comfortably in the end from Stekelenburg's point of view, but that was struck nicely.
--- 9’ Yellow card Cheap yellow for Barkley to pick up here, for what was a bit of a soft foul, but it certainly was a cynical one as his tug prevents what was shaping up to be a dangerous counter. ---
(7’) STAT: Victory would give Everton their highest points tally after their opening three matches of a season in 10 years.
(5’) FIRST CHANCE: TOFFEES! Great improvisation from Mirallas who uses the run of Bolasie to his right as a decoy, before turning smartly around Whelan, cutting in on his left and trying to squeeze a finish in at the near post. It's a well-struck effort, but Given has it covered in the end.
(3’) Everton start positively and it's got the crowd buzzing. There's a real positive vibe at Goodison these days, just a few months removed from what was a disastrous 2015/16 campaign. Ronald Koeman has come in and completely changed the feel surrounding the club in a short time.
(1’) AND WE'RE OFF! Stoke get us underway, attacking left to right in their red and white stripes, with Everton in their royal blue home strip.
Mark Hughes has made two alterations to his XI from the heavy defeat to Manchester City, though the Potters continue to be without Xherdan Shaqiri as he nurses an ankle injury. Geoff Cameron comes into defence, partnering Ryan Shawcross at centre-half, while Peter Crouch is brought in to lead the line, with Philipp Wollscheid and Bojan the ones to give way.
Ronald Koeman makes three changes from the victory over West Brom a week ago. Ashley Williams and Yannick Bolasie are handed their first Premier League starts for the Toffees, replacing Ramiro Funes Mori and James McCarthy. Romelu Lukaku is also brought in to lead the line, following the news that he will not be sold this summer, at the expense of Gerard Deulofeu, who drops to the bench.

SUBS: Kone, Oviedo, Robles, Deulofeu, Funes Mori, Davies, Lennon.

They showed their potential under Mark Hughes last season but inconsistency prevented what could have been a higher finish. You get the sense that the potential is there for them to make a real run at improving last season’s ninth-place standing, and a win today at Goodison would go a long way in helping them get off the mark.
Stoke played better than the scoreline suggested in their 4-1 defeat to Manchester City last weekend, but they have not been entirely convincing out of the gate. They were very much second best in their draw with Middlesbrough on the opening weekend, relying on a Xherdan Shaqiri stunner to steal a point.
Their new signings have integrated nicely and it does not look like Koeman is done just yet. They have the pieces in place to be a very competitive side in the Premier League, and the Dutchman has proved his worth as a manager in this division. There’s a real sense of excitement – and for good reason – on Merseyside.
The Toffees are off to a strong start under Ronald Koeman. They will consider themselves unlucky not to have nicked three points against Spurs in their opener, but they showed great resilience to come from behind and claim victory at the Hawthorns last weekend, before routing Yeovil Town in the League Cup on Tuesday.
